# REDZ.UI - the documentation in full

# Getting started

REDZ.UI is a stylesheet, its icons and one small script on the browser platform. Nothing is built where it is used: link the three files, write Bootstrap-like markup, and the browser does the rest.

## Get it

Every release is an immutable release on GitHub: once it is out, neither its tag nor its files can change. `redz-ui-0.23.0.zip` is the folder a project serves, as it is: `css/` and `js/` with minified files only, the license files and the passport, `redz-ui.json` - the version, the floor, the files to link, every class, token, command and text key, and the sha256 of every file. The icons are a release of their own, `redz-ui-icons-1.13.2.zip`, which changes only with Bootstrap Icons: the passport's `icons` names the version a release needs, and a project keeps it in a folder of its own, so a new release of the library leaves the icons and their cache alone. `checks.zip` beside the library is the sheet of the probes the release passed in every engine.

```js
gh release download v0.23.0 --repo redz-tech/REDZ.UI --pattern 'redz-ui-*.zip'
gh release verify-asset v0.23.0 redz-ui-0.23.0.zip --repo redz-tech/REDZ.UI
gh release download icons-1.13.2 --repo redz-tech/REDZ.UI --pattern 'redz-ui-icons-*.zip'
gh release verify-asset icons-1.13.2 redz-ui-icons-1.13.2.zip --repo redz-tech/REDZ.UI
```

Or from jsDelivr, which serves a release by its tag:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/redz-tech/REDZ.UI@v0.23.0/dist/css/redz-ui.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/redz-tech/REDZ.UI@icons-1.13.2/css/icons.min.css">
```

## Include it

The stylesheet, the icons and the scripts, with the page's own words for the few things the library says - every word comes from the page, the library has none of its own.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="redz-ui/css/redz-ui.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="redz-ui-icons/css/icons.min.css">
  <script type="module" src="redz-ui/js/redz-ui.min.js"></script>
  <script type="application/json" id="redz-ui-text">{"close": "Close", "confirm.ok": "OK", "confirm.cancel": "Cancel", "busy": "Loading…"}</script>
</head>
```

- `css/redz-ui.min.css` is the layers, the tokens, the components and the utilities in one file, within its budget of 38 KB gzipped: the stylesheets `css/index.css` pulls in, squeezed.
- `css/icons.min.css` is apart: one mask per Bootstrap Icons file, used only by name. It reaches each file by a URL relative to itself, `../icons/NAME.svg`, so the pack's folders keep their shape where a project serves them. A project that marks its static files by their content (`?h=…`) cannot mark the icons this way, and needs not: the pack's folder is named by its version, which changes only with Bootstrap Icons.
- `js/redz-ui.min.js` is one ES module of the behaviors, within its budget of 52 KB gzipped: the modules of `js/index.js` joined, squeezed and given short local names. It sets `REDZ.ui` for calls from code.
- The island `#redz-ui-text` gives the library its words, in the page's language: every key of the passport's `texts`, and for each key of its `plurals` the other forms its language's plural rules name (`found.one`, `found.few`). Its `args` names the `{names}` the library fills in each of them, `[]` for none: a text of the page that uses another name shows it as it is. The example shows four of them.
- The two files are made from `css/` and `js/`, which stay to read. A project that bundles its own may join the stylesheets in the passport's order instead.

## How it reads

- A component, its variant, its size and its parts are one class each: `btn btn-primary btn-sm`, `card-header` - Bootstrap 5's names, and Bootstrap 6's where it moved onto the platform: `dialog`, `drawer`, `menu`.
- A utility is `property-value`: `d-flex`, `text-muted`. The number is the value - `p-16` is 16 px, `w-50` is 50 %.
- A condition is a prefix: `md:cols-2`, `print:d-none`. A width prefix measures the region the element sits in - a column, a card, a dialog - not the window.
- A state is an HTML attribute: `aria-pressed`, `aria-current`, `disabled`, `[open]`. A button opens a menu or a dialog with the browser's own command: `commandfor` + `command`.
- Tokens are `--redz-` plus the same words: `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-space-16`.

## Theme and direction

Without an attribute the page follows the system's light or dark. `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` fixes one - set it on the server, so the page never flashes. Right to left is `dir="rtl"`: one stylesheet serves both directions, by logical properties, and icons that point mirror with `flip-rtl`.

```html
<html lang="ar" dir="rtl" data-theme="dark">
```

## From script

Menus, tabs, dialogs and their keys need no call: the library listens on the document. Three calls are for code:

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `REDZ.ui.toast({title, text, tone, action, persistent})` | Shows a notice; answers a function that closes it. [Toasts](toast.md) |
| `await REDZ.ui.confirm({title, text, note, sections, ok, cancel, tone, phrase})` | Asks a question in a dialog; answers `true` or `false`. [Dialogs](dialog.md) |
| `await REDZ.ui.busy(element, promise)` | Marks a button or a region busy until the promise settles. [Busy](busy.md) |

## Browsers

Bootstrap 6's floor: Chrome and Edge 130+, Firefox 132+, Safari 18+ on macOS and iOS. What must work rests on features of the floor; invoker commands and anchor positioning are written in their final form, and a small script stands in below them. Every page of these docs is checked in real engines at the floor and above - [the checks](https://redz-tech.github.io/REDZ.UI/checks/).

Below the floor a page shows its own words, not a broken screen. `js/floor.min.js`, a plain script first in the head, before the stylesheets, marks `<html data-floor="below">` when the browser lacks a feature the library is built on; the page's own style shows its "update your browser" then. Every product that loads it judges a browser the same way, and the floor gate holds that no browser at the floor fails it.

```html
<script src="redz-ui/js/floor.min.js"></script>
<style>.floor-notice { display: none; } [data-floor="below"] .floor-notice { display: block; }</style>
```

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-bs-theme` | `data-theme` | rename | light or dark on <html> |

# Layout

The parent sets the grid, the number is the count, and a width prefix measures the region the element is in. Stacks for a column or a row of items, gaps between them, no margins on components.

## Grids

`grid` on the parent, `cols-N` for N equal columns, `gap-*` between them. A width prefix adds columns as the region grows: `grid md:cols-2` is one column until the region is 768 px wide. Every example on these pages is a region of its own - resize the window and watch the examples, not the window.

```html
<div class="grid sm:cols-2 lg:cols-4 gap-16">
	<div class="card"><div class="card-body">One</div></div>
	<div class="card"><div class="card-body">Two</div></div>
	<div class="card"><div class="card-body">Three</div></div>
	<div class="card"><div class="card-body">Four</div></div>
</div>
```

### Spans on a 12-column grid

A child's exception: `span-N` or `span-full`, with a prefix where it changes.

```html
<div class="grid md:cols-12 gap-16">
	<div class="card md:span-8"><div class="card-body">The main column - <code>md:span-8</code></div></div>
	<div class="card md:span-4"><div class="card-body">The side - <code>md:span-4</code></div></div>
</div>
```

### As many as fit

`cols-min-240`: as many columns as fit, none narrower than 240 px.

```html
<div class="grid cols-min-160 gap-12">
	<div class="card"><div class="card-body">lagoon.example</div></div>
	<div class="card"><div class="card-body">villas.lagoon.example</div></div>
	<div class="card"><div class="card-body">northbay.example</div></div>
</div>
```

## Stacks

`vstack` is a column of items, `hstack` a row of them centered on one line; `gap-*` spaces them and `ms-auto` pushes the rest to the end.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-8">
	<span class="badge">Draft</span>
	<span class="text-muted">Edited 2 hours ago</span>
	<button class="btn btn-sm ms-auto" type="button">Preview</button>
	<button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" type="button">Publish</button>
</div>
```

## Regions and breakpoints

Regions are the shell's main and side columns, cards, dialogs, drawers, and any block with the class `region`. A page without the shell marks its own `region`; the root is never one.

| Prefix | The region is at least |
| --- | --- |
| `sm:` | 576 px |
| `md:` | 768 px |
| `lg:` | 1024 px |
| `xl:` | 1280 px |
| `2xl:` | 1536 px |
| `print:` | on paper |

- A region inside a flex row needs a width - `flex-grow-1` or a grid track: its size cannot come from its content.
- A card in the 8-of-12 column at 1440 px is about 740 px wide: `sm:` inside it, not `md:`.

| `offset-10` | - | review | no offsets: a span with an empty track before it |
| `offset-11` | - | review | no offsets: a span with an empty track before it |
| `offset-2` | - | review | no offsets: a span with an empty track before it |
| `offset-3` | - | review | no offsets: a span with an empty track before it |
| `offset-4` | - | review | no offsets: a span with an empty track before it |
| `offset-5` | - | review | no offsets: a span with an empty track before it |
| `offset-6` | - | review | no offsets: a span with an empty track before it |
| `offset-7` | - | review | no offsets: a span with an empty track before it |
| `offset-8` | - | review | no offsets: a span with an empty track before it |
| `offset-9` | - | review | no offsets: a span with an empty track before it |
| `row` | `grid` | grid | on the parent, with cols-N for equal columns or cols-12 for spans; no gutters to undo |
| `row-cols-1` | `cols-1` | grid | on the same parent |
| `row-cols-2` | `cols-2` | grid | on the same parent |

| `row-cols-auto` | - | review | items as wide as their content: hstack flex-wrap |
| `--bs-breakpoint-xs` | - | remove | REDZ.UI's widths are the region prefixes sm: to 2xl: |
| `--bs-gutter-x` | - | review | the grid's gap: gap-* on the grid |
| `--bs-gutter-y` | - | review | the grid's gap: gap-* on the grid |

# Utilities

Single-purpose classes with Bootstrap 5's names, where the number is the value: `p-16`, `gap-8`, `fs-14`, `rounded-8`, `w-50`. Written once from a vocabulary file and committed - nothing is generated where they are used.

## Scales

- Space, in px: 0 2 4 8 12 16 20 24 32 40 48 64 - for `m`, `p` and `gap` with their sides: `mt` `mb` `ms` `me` `mx` `my`, the same for `p`. `ms` and `me` are the start and the end of the line, so they turn right to left.
- Font size: 11 12 14 16 18 20 24 32 40 48 - 11 for the smallest caption, 40 and 48 for one hero number; line height: 16 20 24 28; radius: 0 4 6 8 12 16 and `rounded-full`.
- Width prefixes come on placement and spacing - display, flex, grid, gaps, order, text alignment, margins and paddings: `md:d-none`, `lg:p-24`.
- `d-none` beats every other display class and component on its element, and a width prefix beats it: `d-none md:d-flex` shows from `md`. Page styles outside the layers beat it too: use `hidden` there.

## Aspect ratio

`ratio-1x1`, `ratio-4x3`, `ratio-16x9` and `ratio-21x9` keep an element's shape as its width changes - on a video, a map, an image's frame; `ratio-auto` lets it go. `ratio-1.91x1` is the shape of a link's preview image on social networks, 1200 × 630. The class goes on the element itself: an image inside a frame fills it with `w-100 h-100 object-fit-cover`.

```html
<div class="ratio-16x9 w-50 hstack justify-content-center rounded-8 bg-page text-muted">16 × 9</div>
<div class="ratio-1x1 w-25 hstack justify-content-center rounded-8 bg-page text-muted">1 × 1</div>
<div class="ratio-1.91x1 w-50 hstack justify-content-center rounded-8 bg-page text-muted">1.91 × 1</div>
```

## Sizes in pixels

Where a control or a mark needs a fixed size - a narrow field in a toolbar, a column of codes, a thumbnail - the number is the pixels, as with the spaces:

- `w-56` `w-64` `w-80` `w-96` `w-120` `w-160` beside the shares `w-25` to `w-100`; `h-32` `h-40` `h-72` beside `h-25` to `h-100`.
- `min-w-56` `min-w-120` `min-w-160` `min-w-200` `min-w-240` `min-w-288`; `max-w-80` to `max-w-1200`, with 360 and 560 among them.
- `size-32` `size-48` `size-64` `size-80` set both sides at once: a square.

```html
<span class="size-32 rounded-8 bg-page"></span>
<span class="size-48 rounded-8 bg-page"></span>
<span class="size-64 rounded-8 bg-page"></span>
<span class="size-80 rounded-8 bg-page"></span>
<input class="form-control w-120" type="text" name="code" aria-label="Code" value="SPRING-26">
```

## Text: kept lines, captions, clamps

`text-pre-wrap` keeps the lines and the spaces a person typed - a note, an address - and still wraps a long line. `tracking-wide` spaces the letters of a caption in capitals. `line-clamp-2` and `line-clamp-3` cut a text after two or three lines with an ellipsis; the whole text stays in the page for a screen reader and for search.

```html
<p class="text-pre-wrap">Villa 12, Harbor Road&#10;Main Island 00000</p>
<p class="fs-11 text-uppercase tracking-wide text-muted">Last 30 days</p>
<p class="line-clamp-2 max-w-360">North Bay by speedboat: a day among the forty-two islands of the marine park, with snorkelling at Reef Islet, the emerald lake of Emerald Islet and lunch on the beach, back by five.</p>
```

## Shown when focused

`visually-hidden-focusable` hides an element until it or something in it takes the focus - the first link of a page that jumps to its content. Press `Tab` into the example to see it.

```html
<a class="visually-hidden-focusable btn" href="#utilities-all">Skip to every utility</a>
<span class="text-muted">The link above shows on focus.</span>
```

## A flash and a sticky panel

`flash` lights an element's ground once and lets it fade - a row a click elsewhere changed. To light it again, take the class off, let the browser lay the element out, and put the class back. `sticky-top` keeps an element at the top while the page scrolls: under the app header in the shell, at `--redz-sticky-top` anywhere else.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="flash" aria-controls="utilities-flash-target">Change the row</button>
<span class="p-8 rounded-8" id="utilities-flash-target">A row a click elsewhere changed</span>
```

```js
row.classList.remove('flash');
void row.offsetWidth;
row.classList.add('flash');
```

## Off the screen

`offscreen` puts an element outside the page, where no one sees it, yet it stays rendered: not `display: none`, `visibility: hidden` or the clip of `visually-hidden`, which bots look for. Two uses:

- A form's trap for bots: a field a person never fills. Its wrapper carries `aria-hidden="true"` so no screen reader meets it; the field has `tabindex="-1"`, `autocomplete="off"` and a plausible name, such as `company_url`. The server refuses a form that comes back with it filled. Name the class and the field plainly: bots skip what is called a honeypot.
- A field that takes what a keyboard-wedge reader types - a badge or a fob read at a kiosk - kept focused while nothing else is.

```html
<div class="offscreen" aria-hidden="true"><label>Company site<input type="text" name="company_url" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off"></label></div>
<span class="text-muted">A field is here, off the screen.</span>
```

## Dividers, rules and icon links

`divide-x` and `divide-y` on a parent draw a line between its children, across or down, with no class on any child. `vr` is a rule between the items of a row. `icon-link` lines an icon up with the words of a link.

```html
<div class="hstack divide-x"><span class="px-12">Bookings</span><span class="px-12">Guests</span><span class="px-12">Revenue</span></div>
<div class="hstack gap-12"><button class="btn btn-sm" type="button">Copy</button><span class="vr"></span><button class="btn btn-sm" type="button">Delete</button></div>
<a class="icon-link" href="#utilities-divide"><i class="bi bi-box-arrow-up-right" aria-hidden="true"></i>Open on the site</a>
```

# Tokens

The custom properties on `:root` that the components read: colors by role in pairs that pass WCAG AA in both themes, spacing, type, radii, shadows and motion. A theme changes tokens, never component rules.

## How they are made

- Colors by role: `--redz-text`, `-muted`, `-faint`; `--redz-bg-page`, `--redz-bg`, `-raised`, `-hover`; a tone, its `-subtle` fill and its `-contrast` text for primary, secondary, success, danger, warning and info. `--redz-focus` and `--redz-link` are the primary tone unless a theme gives them their own - a white-label palette sets the links' color in `--redz-link` alone.
- Text is at least 4.5:1 on its background, the borders of fields and the focus ring 3:1, in the light and the dark theme - computed in OKLCH and written as checked hex.
- A component declares a few properties of its own on its root and never on rows or items: hundreds of properties on small elements slow every style recalculation.

## A white label from one colour

`data-brand` on `html`, or on one region, makes the primary tone of one colour, `--redz-brand`: the library derives the tone, its `-subtle` fill, its `-contrast` text - black or white, whichever reads at 4.5:1 on it, as one of the two always does - the focus ring and the links, in both themes; in the dark one the tone is lightened until it reads on the dark ground. `data-brand="#0a7f5a"` gives the colour, which the library sets through the CSSOM after its script loads; a page that knows the colour on its server writes `--redz-brand` in its own stylesheet beside the attribute, and nothing waits for the script. Where the tone is text - a link, a subtle badge, an outline button, `text-primary`, an alert's icon - it is `--redz-primary-text`: in the light theme the colour darkened, its hue kept, until its luminance is at most 0.13, which reads at 4.5:1 on white and on its subtle fill; in the dark theme the tone itself. A fill keeps the colour as given. The other tones follow their own keys the same way: `data-brand-secondary`, `data-brand-success`, `data-brand-info`, `data-brand-warning` and `data-brand-danger` - a company's own red for its errors - each derive that tone, its `-subtle`, `-contrast` and `-text`. Every tone has its `--redz-TONE-text`, the tone itself unless a brand key derives it. The relative colours it is derived with are on the floor: Chrome 119, Firefox 128, Safari 18.

```html
<div class="hstack flex-wrap gap-8" data-brand="#0a7f5a">
	<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button">Book now</button>
	<button class="btn btn-outline-primary" type="button">Details</button>
	<span class="badge badge-subtle-primary">New</span>
	<a href="#tokens-brand">A link</a>
</div>
<div class="hstack flex-wrap gap-8" data-brand="#f4c542">
	<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button">Book now</button>
	<button class="btn btn-outline-primary" type="button">Details</button>
	<span class="badge badge-subtle-primary">New</span>
	<a href="#tokens-brand">A link</a>
</div>
<div class="hstack flex-wrap gap-8" data-brand-danger="#ff6b5b" data-brand-success="#3ddc84">
	<button class="btn btn-danger" type="button">Delete</button>
	<span class="badge badge-subtle-danger">Overdue</span>
	<span class="badge badge-subtle-success">Paid</span>
	<span class="text-danger">2 failed</span>
</div>
```

# Icons

Bootstrap Icons 1.13.2 under their own class names - `<i class="bi bi-pencil">` - each a CSS mask over its own SVG file: the color of the text around it, no font, no script, no build.

## Examples

An icon takes the size of the text and its color: a utility or the parent sets both.

```html
<i class="bi bi-pencil" aria-hidden="true"></i>
<i class="bi bi-trash3 text-danger" aria-hidden="true"></i>
<i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill text-success fs-20" aria-hidden="true"></i>
<i class="bi bi-stars text-primary fs-24" aria-hidden="true"></i>
<i class="bi bi-chevron-right flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i>
<i class="bi bi-arrow-left flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i>
```

The names are Bootstrap Icons' own - look one up at [icons.getbootstrap.com](https://icons.getbootstrap.com/). A name the set does not have paints a filled square, and the checks flag it.

## From another host

A browser fetches a mask in CORS mode, as it does a font. Served from another origin, every icon stays blank unless that host sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` on `.svg`. jsDelivr and GitHub Pages do; on your own CDN, add `svg` to the types that get the header. A file already fetched without it stays broken in the browser's cache for its whole lifetime when it is `immutable`, so a change of header alone does not reach those visitors: give the files a new address too.

## Accessibility

- An icon beside words is `aria-hidden="true"`. An icon alone takes its meaning from its parent: the button's `aria-label`, or hidden words.
- Icons that point - chevrons, arrows, back and next - mirror right to left with `flip-rtl`; a check, a clock, a search glass, media controls do not.
- Icons keep the forced color of their parent and print in their color.

# From Bootstrap 5.3

Most of Bootstrap 5's names stay. What changes is the spacing numbers, the grid, the breakpoints, states and triggers, and the three components Bootstrap 6 renamed. The two libraries are never on one page: a project switches its stylesheet at once.

## What changes

- **Spacing:** the number is the pixels. `p-3` becomes `p-16`, `mb-2` `mb-8`, `gap-4` `gap-24` - and `p-4` exists in both with another size: Bootstrap's 24 px, REDZ.UI's 4 px. Never rename by chained replacements; rewrite each file once.
- **Grid:** `row` and `col-md-6` become the parent's `grid md:cols-2`; a column's own width is `span-N`.
- **Breakpoints:** the infix becomes a prefix - `d-md-none` is `md:d-none` - and it measures the region, not the window.
- **States:** classes become attributes - `.active` is `aria-current`, `aria-selected` or `aria-pressed`; `.disabled` is `disabled` or `aria-disabled`; `.is-invalid` is `aria-invalid="true"`.
- **Triggers:** `data-bs-toggle` becomes the browser's commands - `commandfor` + `command="show-modal"`, `"close"` or `"toggle-popover"`; `bootstrap.Modal` becomes `dialog.showModal()`.
- **Renamed:** modal → `dialog` on a `<dialog>`, dropdown → `menu` on a popover, offcanvas → `drawer`.
- **Icons:** Bootstrap Icons keep their classes; swap the font's stylesheet for `css/icons.min.css`.

## With an agent

The skill `redz-ui-from-bootstrap-5` moves a project file by file: `scripts/scan.sh` finds every Bootstrap class, attribute and call with its replacement and checks every class against the vocabulary; the agent rewrites the whole file in one pass, scans it again until nothing is left, and compares the screens before and after. Install it with `npx skills add redz-tech/REDZ.UI`.

Content kept in a database - page bodies an editor wrote long ago - moves once, with no hand on each body: the skill's `scripts/convert.php` (PHP 8.4 or later) rewrites a body by the map, gives a row the columns its children's spans need, follows a few rows by their context (a badge's tone, a compact table, a lead paragraph, white text on a tone) and lists what it left for a person to decide.

## The map

Every class of Bootstrap 5.3.8 that changes, with what it becomes; a class not listed keeps its name, and a breakpoint form follows its class - `mb-md-3` is `md:mb-16`. The full map, every class and form, is the skill's `assets/map.tsv`.

# Buttons

A button runs an action; a link drawn as a button goes somewhere. One class, `btn`, then a tone, a size or an icon when the button needs one.

## Examples

The plain `btn` is neutral. `btn-primary` marks the one main action of a screen; the other tones say what an action does.

```html
<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button">Save</button>
<button class="btn" type="button">Cancel</button>
<button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button">Duplicate</button>
<button class="btn btn-success" type="button">Publish</button>
<button class="btn btn-danger" type="button">Delete</button>
<button class="btn btn-warning" type="button">Withdraw</button>
<button class="btn btn-info" type="button">Preview</button>
```

### Outline, subtle, text and link

Quieter forms of the same tones for secondary actions, rows and toolbars. `btn-text` has no fill until hovered; `btn-link` reads as a link and keeps a button's size, and it alone wraps a long text.

```html
<button class="btn btn-outline-primary" type="button">Outline</button>
<button class="btn btn-outline-danger" type="button">Outline danger</button>
<button class="btn btn-subtle-primary" type="button">Subtle</button>
<button class="btn btn-subtle-danger" type="button">Subtle danger</button>
<button class="btn btn-text" type="button">Text</button>
<button class="btn btn-link" type="button">Link</button>
<button class="btn btn-link text-start" type="button">A long link wraps inside its box, like the title of a card that opens a window</button>
```

### Sizes

A size is a word: `btn-xs` 24 px, `btn-sm` 28 px, the default 32 px, `btn-lg` 40 px - the heights of every control of the same size. `btn-xl`, 56 px, is for a touch screen and the one action of a page; in a [kiosk](kiosk.md) it grows to a kiosk's size.

```html
<button class="btn btn-primary btn-xs" type="button">Extra small</button>
<button class="btn btn-primary btn-sm" type="button">Small</button>
<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button">Default</button>
<button class="btn btn-primary btn-lg" type="button">Large</button>
<button class="btn btn-primary btn-xl" type="button">Extra large</button>
```

### Icons

An icon sits beside the words, or alone in a square `btn-icon` whose name is its `aria-label`. `btn-close` draws the close glyph by itself.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button"><i class="bi bi-plus-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i>New excursion</button>
<a class="btn" href="#btn-icons">Open the site<i class="bi bi-box-arrow-up-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></a>
<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" aria-label="Edit"><i class="bi bi-pencil" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
<button class="btn btn-icon btn-text" type="button" aria-label="More actions"><i class="bi bi-three-dots" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
<button class="btn btn-icon btn-sm btn-subtle-danger" type="button" aria-label="Remove"><i class="bi bi-trash3" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
<button class="btn-close" type="button" aria-label="Close"></button>
```

### Groups and toolbars

`btn-group` joins buttons into one control - here a choice of view, each button pressed or not. `btn-toolbar` lays groups and buttons out in a wrapping row.

```html
<div class="btn-toolbar" role="group" aria-label="List view">
	<div class="btn-group" role="group" aria-label="Layout">
		<button class="btn" type="button" aria-pressed="true">List</button>
		<button class="btn" type="button" aria-pressed="false">Board</button>
		<button class="btn" type="button" aria-pressed="false">Calendar</button>
	</div>
	<div class="btn-group" role="group" aria-label="Export">
		<button class="btn" type="button">Export</button>
		<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" aria-label="Export options"><i class="bi bi-chevron-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	</div>
</div>
```

### A choice of one

A segmented choice is Bootstrap's: in a `btn-group`, each `input type="radio" class="btn-check"` before its `label class="btn"`. The radio stays the control - the arrow keys move the choice, the form sends it - and the checked one is drawn pressed, an outline tone filled with its colour; the focus ring goes on the label. A link or a button that is the current one of a group carries `aria-current` and is drawn pressed too.

```html
<div class="btn-toolbar">
	<div class="btn-group" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Period">
		<input class="btn-check" type="radio" name="period" id="btn-segmented-day" value="day">
		<label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="btn-segmented-day">Day</label>
		<input class="btn-check" type="radio" name="period" id="btn-segmented-week" value="week" checked>
		<label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="btn-segmented-week">Week</label>
		<input class="btn-check" type="radio" name="period" id="btn-segmented-month" value="month">
		<label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="btn-segmented-month">Month</label>
	</div>
	<div class="btn-group" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Status">
		<input class="btn-check" type="radio" name="state" id="btn-segmented-all" value="all" checked>
		<label class="btn" for="btn-segmented-all">All</label>
		<input class="btn-check" type="radio" name="state" id="btn-segmented-open" value="open">
		<label class="btn" for="btn-segmented-open">Open</label>
		<input class="btn-check" type="radio" name="state" id="btn-segmented-closed" value="closed">
		<label class="btn" for="btn-segmented-closed">Closed</label>
	</div>
	<nav class="btn-group" aria-label="Year">
		<a class="btn btn-sm" href="#btn-segmented">2025</a>
		<a class="btn btn-sm" href="#btn-segmented" aria-current="page">2026</a>
	</nav>
</div>
```

`btn-group-vertical` stacks the buttons of a group, each as wide as the widest.

```html
<div class="btn-group-vertical" role="group" aria-label="Order">
	<button class="btn" type="button"><i class="bi bi-arrow-up" aria-hidden="true"></i>Move up</button>
	<button class="btn" type="button"><i class="bi bi-arrow-down" aria-hidden="true"></i>Move down</button>
	<button class="btn" type="button"><i class="bi bi-trash" aria-hidden="true"></i>Remove</button>
</div>
```

### Toggle and busy

A toggle carries `aria-pressed`. While its action runs, `REDZ.ui.busy(button, promise)` shows a spinner in the button and marks it `aria-disabled`: it keeps the focus and ignores clicks until the promise settles. See [Busy](busy.md) for the words a button says while it waits.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" aria-pressed="false" data-docs-run="toggle"><i class="bi bi-pin-angle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Pin</button>
<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button" data-docs-run="busy-button">Save for 2 seconds</button>
```

### A wait before it works again

`data-cooldown="N"` makes a button wait N seconds: it is `aria-disabled` - it keeps the focus and ignores clicks - and shows the seconds left after its words, in the page's text `cooldown`; then it wakes and the attribute goes. Setting the attribute again starts the wait again; a page reloaded during a wait renders the seconds left. The count is drawn, not read out every second: say the wait in words once, when it starts - "A new code is on its way; ask again in a minute". A cooldown set while the button is [busy](busy.md#busy-button) keeps it disabled after the wait, until its count ends.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" data-cooldown="20" data-docs-run="cooldown"><i class="bi bi-arrow-clockwise" aria-hidden="true"></i>Send the code again</button>
```

## States

A state is the attribute accessibility needs anyway, on the button itself: no `active` or `disabled` classes. `aria-expanded` is set by the browser on a button that opens a menu or a dialog.

## Keyboard and accessibility

- `<button type="button">` for an action, `<a href>` for a place; `btn` draws both the same. Enter and Space press a button, Enter follows a link.
- A button with only an icon takes its name from `aria-label`; the icon is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- `disabled` takes a button out of the tab order and hides why. `aria-disabled="true"` keeps it focusable - so a tooltip can say why - and the library swallows its clicks.
- A button that opens a menu or a dialog uses the browser's command: `commandfor` + `command`, never `data-bs-toggle`.
- A segmented choice is radios: one Tab stop, the arrow keys move the choice, a screen reader says "1 of 3". A group of toggles that each stand alone is buttons with `aria-pressed`.
- The focus ring is 2 px of `--redz-focus`, 3:1 against the page in both themes.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/btn.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/btn.css). It declares `--redz-btn-bg`, `--redz-btn-fg`, `--redz-btn-hover`, `--redz-btn-hover-fg`, `--redz-btn-on-bg`, `--redz-btn-on-fg` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-control-height`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-radius-8`, `--redz-focus`, `--redz-bg-page`, `--redz-text-faint`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-primary-contrast`, `--redz-secondary`, `--redz-secondary-contrast`, `--redz-success`, `--redz-success-contrast`, `--redz-danger`, `--redz-danger-contrast`, `--redz-warning`, `--redz-warning-contrast`, `--redz-info`, `--redz-info-contrast`, `--redz-primary-text`, `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-secondary-text`, `--redz-secondary-subtle`, `--redz-success-text`, `--redz-success-subtle`, `--redz-danger-text`, `--redz-danger-subtle`, `--redz-warning-text`, `--redz-warning-subtle`, `--redz-info-text`, `--redz-info-subtle`, `--redz-control-height-xs`, `--redz-radius-6`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-control-height-sm`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-control-height-lg`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-fs-16`, `--redz-space-24`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-fs-20`, `--redz-control-height-float`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-motion`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `btn-close-white` | - | remove | the close glyph takes the text color |
| `btn-dark` | - | review | no light or dark buttons: btn or btn-text |
| `btn-light` | - | review | no light or dark buttons: btn or btn-text |
| `btn-outline-dark` | - | review | btn-outline-secondary |
| `btn-outline-light` | - | review | btn-outline-secondary |
| `data-bs-toggle="button"` | `aria-pressed` | review | switch aria-pressed in your click handler |

# Button commands

Buttons that act without a line of the page's script: copy a value, print the page, switch the theme, share an address. Each carries its command in `command` and names what it acts on in `aria-controls`, as [`--toggle`](collapse.md) does - no `commandfor`.

## Copy

`command="--copy"` copies its `data-copy`, or the value of the field `aria-controls` names, or that element's text. It says politely that it did - the page's texts `copy.done` and `copy.failed` - and shows a check in place of its icon for a moment; the page hears `redz:copy` with `detail.text`. A page served over plain http has no Clipboard API: the browser's copy command stands in.

```html
<label class="form-label" for="commands-copy-key">The key for the API</label>
<div class="input-group">
	<input class="form-control font-monospace" id="commands-copy-key" type="text" value="rz_live_4f9a1c2e7b" readonly>
	<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" command="--copy" aria-controls="commands-copy-key" aria-label="Copy the key"><i class="bi bi-copy" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</div>
<div class="hstack gap-8">
	<button class="btn" type="button" command="--copy" data-copy="https://lagoon.example/tours/north-bay"><i class="bi bi-link-45deg" aria-hidden="true"></i>Copy the address</button>
</div>
```

## Download

`command="--download"` with `aria-controls` naming a field, a `textarea` or any element - a `pre` of a report - downloads its value or its text as a file: `data-file` names it, `download.txt` by default, and `data-type` is its type, `text/plain`. A `text/csv` file starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark, so a spreadsheet reads its letters right; `data-bom="false"` leaves it out. An element holding a picture - an `svg`, an `img`, a `canvas`, a [QR tile](qr.md#qr-download) - downloads it as a PNG instead. Each download is said politely, in the page's text `downloaded`. From code, `REDZ.ui.download({text, file, type, bom})` does the same for words made at the moment - a report built from the rows on the screen - and `{blob, file}` for a `Blob` of any kind.

```html
		<pre class="docs-code w-100" id="commands-download-text" tabindex="0">Boat A	12 trips	286 seats
Boat C	 9 trips	201 seats</pre>
		<button class="btn" type="button" command="--download" aria-controls="commands-download-text" data-file="boats.txt"><i class="bi bi-download" aria-hidden="true"></i>Download the report</button>
```

```js
const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('#agents tbody tr')].map((row) => [...row.cells].map((cell) => cell.textContent.trim()).join(';'));
REDZ.ui.download({text: rows.join('\r\n'), file: 'agents-2026-11-08.csv', type: 'text/csv'});
```

## Print

`command="--print"` prints the page. However printing starts - the button, the browser's menu, a key - every closed `details`, an accordion's item among them, and every region a `--toggle` button holds closed open for the paper and close again after. A card is not cut across two pages, and a scrolling card's body prints whole; the shell, toasts, the save bar and anything with `print:d-none` stay off the paper.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" command="--print"><i class="bi bi-printer" aria-hidden="true"></i>Print</button>
```

## Theme

Buttons with `command="--theme"` and the value `light`, `dark` or `system` set the page's theme - `data-theme` on `html`, removed for system - and `aria-pressed` says which shows. One button with the value `toggle` flips the theme shown between light and dark, the system's read from `prefers-color-scheme`: it is pressed while dark, so its words name the dark theme. The page hears `redz:theme` with `detail.theme` and keeps the choice - in a cookie, in the account - and writes `data-theme` on `html` on its server, so the page paints in its theme at once.

```html
<div class="btn-group" role="group" aria-label="Theme">
	<button class="btn" type="button" command="--theme" value="light"><i class="bi bi-sun" aria-hidden="true"></i>Light</button>
	<button class="btn" type="button" command="--theme" value="dark"><i class="bi bi-moon" aria-hidden="true"></i>Dark</button>
	<button class="btn" type="button" command="--theme" value="system"><i class="bi bi-circle-half" aria-hidden="true"></i>System</button>
</div>
<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" command="--theme" value="toggle" aria-label="Dark theme"><i class="bi bi-moon-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
```

## Share

`command="--share"` shares `data-share-url` - the page's own address when it has none - and `data-share-title` through the device's share sheet where it has one, as a phone does. Elsewhere it opens its menu, `aria-controls`, whose links the library writes by their class: `share-telegram`, `share-facebook`, `share-messenger`, `share-linkedin`, `share-vk`, `share-line` and `share-whatsapp`; a `--copy` item without `data-copy` copies the address. Each class gives its icon the network's colour; Bootstrap Icons has no VK mark, so `share-vk` draws its letters. Messenger opens its app, on a phone.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" command="--share" aria-controls="commands-share-menu" aria-haspopup="menu" data-share-url="https://lagoon.example/tours/north-bay" data-share-title="North Bay by speedboat"><i class="bi bi-share" aria-hidden="true"></i>Share</button>
<div id="commands-share-menu" class="menu menu-start" popover role="menu" aria-label="Share">
	<a class="menu-item share-telegram" role="menuitem"><i class="bi bi-telegram" aria-hidden="true"></i>Telegram</a>
	<a class="menu-item share-whatsapp" role="menuitem"><i class="bi bi-whatsapp" aria-hidden="true"></i>WhatsApp</a>
	<a class="menu-item share-line" role="menuitem"><i class="bi bi-line" aria-hidden="true"></i>LINE</a>
	<a class="menu-item share-facebook" role="menuitem"><i class="bi bi-facebook" aria-hidden="true"></i>Facebook</a>
	<a class="menu-item share-messenger" role="menuitem"><i class="bi bi-messenger" aria-hidden="true"></i>Messenger</a>
	<a class="menu-item share-linkedin" role="menuitem"><i class="bi bi-linkedin" aria-hidden="true"></i>LinkedIn</a>
	<a class="menu-item share-vk" role="menuitem">VK</a>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" command="--copy"><i class="bi bi-link-45deg" aria-hidden="true"></i>Copy the address</button>
</div>
```

Three more networks: `share-x` posts on X with the title as its words, `share-viber` opens Viber's app with them - its mark drawn as letters, as VK's, or the page's own `img` or `svg` in the link -, and `share-wechat`, which has no address to share by, is a plain button that opens the page's popover with a [QR code](qr.md) of the address to scan in WeChat. `data-share-url` and `data-share-title` on any element write the links and the copy inside it, a row on the page without a menu: neutral buttons, each with the network's coloured icon and its name, as a filled brand colour leaves most names unreadable.

```html
<div class="hstack flex-wrap gap-8" role="group" aria-label="Share your link" data-share-url="https://lagoon.example/join?ref=sample" data-share-title="Book North Bay trips with my link">
	<a class="btn btn-sm share-whatsapp"><i class="bi bi-whatsapp" aria-hidden="true"></i>WhatsApp</a>
	<a class="btn btn-sm share-telegram"><i class="bi bi-telegram" aria-hidden="true"></i>Telegram</a>
	<a class="btn btn-sm share-x"><i class="bi bi-twitter-x" aria-hidden="true"></i>X</a>
	<a class="btn btn-sm share-viber">Viber</a>
	<button class="btn btn-sm share-wechat" type="button" commandfor="commands-share-wechat" command="toggle-popover"><i class="bi bi-wechat" aria-hidden="true"></i>WeChat</button>
	<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button" command="--copy"><i class="bi bi-link-45deg" aria-hidden="true"></i>Copy the link</button>
	<div class="popover" id="commands-share-wechat" popover role="dialog" aria-label="Scan in WeChat">
		<div class="vstack gap-8 align-items-center">
			<div class="qr"><img src="img/qr.svg" alt="QR code of your link"></div>
			<p class="fs-12 text-muted">Scan in WeChat to share</p>
		</div>
	</div>
</div>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

- Each command is a `button`: `Enter` and `Space` run it, and one that is `aria-disabled` does nothing.
- A copy is said once, politely, inside an open modal dialog when there is one; the check that shows for a moment is not read out.
- The theme buttons say which theme shows in `aria-pressed`; the one toggle is pressed while dark, its words the dark theme's.
- The share menu is a [menu](menu.md): it opens on its first link, the arrow keys move through it, and `Escape` closes it back to its button, which says in `aria-expanded` whether it is open.

## Texts

The library has no words of its own; it reads these from the page's island `#redz-ui-text`.

| Key | For | In English |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy.done` | Said when a copy is done | Copied |
| `copy.failed` | Said when the browser refuses it | Could not copy |

# Chips

A chip is a small rounded choice: a filter that is on or off, a saved view, an applied filter with its count and a way to remove it.

## Examples

A filter chip is a toggle button: `aria-pressed` says whether it is on. A chip that opens a menu is the menu's button.

```html
<button class="chip" type="button" aria-pressed="true"><i class="bi bi-eye" aria-hidden="true"></i>Published</button>
<button class="chip" type="button" aria-pressed="false"><i class="bi bi-pencil-square" aria-hidden="true"></i>Drafts</button>
<button class="chip" type="button" aria-pressed="false"><i class="bi bi-translate" aria-hidden="true"></i>Language: any</button>
<button class="chip" type="button" commandfor="chip-site-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu"><i class="bi bi-globe2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Site: all<i class="bi bi-chevron-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
<div id="chip-site-menu" class="menu menu-start" popover role="menu" aria-label="Site">
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="true">All sites</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false">lagoon.example</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false">northbay.example</button>
</div>
```

### Saved views and applied filters

Links between saved views mark the current one with `aria-current="true"`. An applied filter is a group: its name, its count in `chip-count`, and a `chip-dismiss` button named after what it removes.

```html
<a class="chip" href="#chip-views" aria-current="true">All<span class="chip-count">28</span></a>
<a class="chip" href="#chip-views">Needs attention<span class="chip-count">3</span></a>
<a class="chip" href="#chip-views">Mine<span class="chip-count">11</span></a>
<span class="chip" role="group" aria-label="Filter: section Marine"><i class="bi bi-diagram-3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Section: Marine<span class="chip-count">9</span><button class="chip-dismiss" type="button" aria-label="Remove filter: section Marine"><i class="bi bi-x" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></span>
```

## States

## Keyboard and accessibility

- A filter chip is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed`; Space or Enter toggles it. Change the attribute when the filter changes - the look follows it.
- A saved view is a link; the current one carries `aria-current="true"`.
- An applied filter is `role="group"` named after the filter, and its dismiss button names what it removes - "Remove filter: section Marine", not "Remove".
- A count is part of the chip's name; say what it counts in the words around it when it is not obvious.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/chip.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/chip.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-control-height-sm`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-text-muted`.

# Menus

A menu is a short list of actions or choices that opens from a button: the browser's popover, placed beside the button by CSS anchor positioning, driven by the keyboard as the WAI-ARIA menu button.

## Examples

The button opens the menu with the browser's command - `commandfor` names the menu, `command="toggle-popover"` opens and closes it - and the library keeps its `aria-expanded`, which Firefox does not give such a button. No script is needed to open a menu; the library adds the arrow keys.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="menu-actions-list" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu"><i class="bi bi-three-dots" aria-hidden="true"></i>Actions</button>
<div id="menu-actions-list" class="menu" popover role="menu" aria-label="Actions">
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem"><i class="bi bi-pencil" aria-hidden="true"></i>Edit</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem"><i class="bi bi-files" aria-hidden="true"></i>Duplicate</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" aria-disabled="true"><i class="bi bi-archive" aria-hidden="true"></i>Archive</button>
	<a class="menu-item" href="#menu-actions" role="menuitem"><i class="bi bi-box-arrow-up-right" aria-hidden="true"></i>Open on the site</a>
	<hr class="menu-divider">
	<button class="menu-item menu-item-danger" type="button" role="menuitem"><i class="bi bi-trash3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Delete</button>
</div>
```

### Choices and headers

A choice of one is a set of `menuitemradio` items, the chosen one `aria-checked="true"` with a check drawn after it. `menu-header` titles a part of the menu. `menu-start` lines the menu up with its button's start edge instead of its end.

```html
<button class="btn btn-text" type="button" commandfor="menu-choice-list" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu"><span class="dot dot-success"></span>All sites<i class="bi bi-chevron-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
<div id="menu-choice-list" class="menu menu-start" popover role="menu" aria-label="Work context">
	<div class="menu-header">Work context</div>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="true"><i class="bi bi-grid-3x3-gap" aria-hidden="true"></i>All sites</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false"><i class="bi bi-globe2" aria-hidden="true"></i>lagoon.example</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false"><i class="bi bi-globe2" aria-hidden="true"></i>northbay.example</button>
</div>
```

### Items that stay checked

A `menuitemcheckbox` chosen flips its `aria-checked`, and a `menuitemradio` in a `role="group"` checks itself and unchecks the others of its group; the menu stays open for the next choice, and the page hears `redz:check` with `detail.item` and `detail.checked`. A `menuitemradio` outside a group is a choice of one, as above: it checks itself and closes the menu.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="menu-checks-list" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu"><i class="bi bi-layout-three-columns" aria-hidden="true"></i>Columns<i class="bi bi-chevron-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
<div id="menu-checks-list" class="menu" popover role="menu" aria-label="Columns">
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemcheckbox" aria-checked="true">Guest</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemcheckbox" aria-checked="true">Tour</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemcheckbox" aria-checked="false">Pickup</button>
	<div class="menu-header" id="menu-checks-sort">Sort by</div>
	<div role="group" aria-labelledby="menu-checks-sort">
		<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="true">Date</button>
		<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false">Name</button>
	</div>
</div>
```

## States

The items of an open menu. `:focus-visible` is where the arrow keys are; `aria-current="true"` marks the page a menu of links is on.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | On the button | In the menu |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Opens the menu, the focus on the checked or the first item | Runs the item and closes the menu |
| `↓` / `↑` | Opens the menu on the first / the last item | The next / the previous item, round the ends |
| `Home` / `End` | - | The first / the last item |
| A letter | - | The next item that begins with it |
| `Esc` | - | Closes the menu, the focus back on the button |
| `Tab` | - | Closes the menu and moves on |

- The menu is `popover` with `role="menu"` and a name; its items are `menuitem`, `menuitemradio` or `menuitemcheckbox`. A list of site sections is navigation, not a menu - use links.
- The button carries `aria-haspopup="menu"`; the library keeps its `aria-expanded`, and the browser moves the focus back to it on close and closes the menu on a click outside or `Esc`.
- Where an engine does not put the menu beside its button - no anchor positioning below Firefox 147 and Safari 26, no anchor from a popover's button in Chrome 130-132, a table cell in Chrome 135-136, the bottom of a long page in Safari 26 - `js/menu-place.js` places it, again when the page scrolls or the menu or its button changes size, and the probes record each such place.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/menu.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/menu.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-bg-raised`, `--redz-shadow-2`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-control-height`, `--redz-radius-8`, `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-text-faint`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-danger`, `--redz-motion`, `--redz-ease`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dropdown` | - | remove | no wrapper: the menu flips by itself |
| `dropdown-center` | - | remove | no wrapper: the menu flips by itself |
| `dropdown-divider` | `menu-divider` | rename |  |
| `dropdown-header` | `menu-header` | rename |  |
| `dropdown-item` | `menu-item` | rename | role="menuitem" |
| `dropdown-item-text` | - | review | menu-header, or plain text |
| `dropdown-menu` | `menu` | rename | with popover and role="menu" |
| `dropdown-menu-dark` | - | remove | the theme sets it |
| `dropdown-menu-end` | - | remove | the menu meets its button's end edge by default |
| `dropdown-menu-start` | `menu-start` | rename |  |
| `dropdown-toggle` | - | review | the button: commandfor + command="toggle-popover" + aria-haspopup="menu"; a chevron is an icon |
| `dropdown-toggle-split` | - | review | a btn-group of the action and a btn-icon that opens the menu |
| `dropend` | - | remove | no wrapper: the menu flips by itself |
| `dropstart` | - | remove | no wrapper: the menu flips by itself |
| `dropup` | - | remove | no wrapper: the menu flips by itself |
| `dropup-center` | - | remove | no wrapper: the menu flips by itself |
| `data-bs-toggle="dropdown"` | `commandfor="ID" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu"` | trigger | the menu gets popover and role="menu" |
| `data-bs-placement` | - | remove | anchor positioning places and flips the menu |
| `data-bs-offset` | - | remove | anchor positioning places and flips the menu |
| `data-bs-auto-close` | - | remove | anchor positioning places and flips the menu |
| `data-bs-display` | - | remove | anchor positioning places and flips the menu |
| `data-bs-reference` | - | remove | anchor positioning places and flips the menu |
| `data-bs-boundary` | - | remove | anchor positioning places and flips the menu |
| `data-bs-popper-config` | - | remove | anchor positioning places and flips the menu |
| `bootstrap.Dropdown` | `menu.showPopover(), menu.hidePopover(), menu.togglePopover()` | trigger |  |
| `show.bs.dropdown` | `toggle` | rename | the popover's toggle event; event.newState is "open" or "closed" |
| `shown.bs.dropdown` | `toggle` | rename | the popover's toggle event; event.newState is "open" or "closed" |
| `hide.bs.dropdown` | `toggle` | rename | the popover's toggle event; event.newState is "open" or "closed" |
| `hidden.bs.dropdown` | `toggle` | rename | the popover's toggle event; event.newState is "open" or "closed" |

# Form fields

Text fields, selects and text areas with Bootstrap 5's names: a label floating in the field or above it, a hint, an error said in words, an icon inside the field, chips for typed values.

## Examples

`form-floating` keeps the label inside the field and lifts it when the field has a value or the focus. The label follows the control, and the control needs a `placeholder` - it is how CSS knows the field is empty.

```html
<div class="form-floating">
	<input class="form-control" id="form-floating-name" value="North Bay: marine park by speedboat" placeholder="A name people search for">
	<label for="form-floating-name">Name</label>
</div>
<div class="form-floating">
	<input class="form-control" id="form-floating-mail" type="email" placeholder="name@example.com">
	<label for="form-floating-mail">E-mail</label>
</div>
<div class="form-floating">
	<select class="form-select" id="form-floating-section"><option>Marine</option><option>Land</option><option>Evening</option></select>
	<label for="form-floating-section">Section</label>
</div>
<div class="form-floating">
	<textarea class="form-control" id="form-floating-note" placeholder="A note for the guides">Pick up at the pier at 8:30.</textarea>
	<label for="form-floating-note">Note</label>
</div>
```

### A label above, a hint, an error

`form-field` stacks a field's parts: `form-label`, the control, `form-text` for a hint and `invalid-feedback` for an error. The control points at both with `aria-describedby`; an error sets `aria-invalid="true"`, and the browser's own `:user-invalid` draws the same after the person has edited the field.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-stacked-slug">Address</label>
	<input class="form-control font-monospace" id="form-stacked-slug" value="north-bay" aria-describedby="form-stacked-slug-hint">
	<div class="form-text" id="form-stacked-slug-hint">Full address /excursions/north-bay/. The old one answers with a 301 redirect.</div>
</div>
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-stacked-price">Adult price, THB</label>
	<input class="form-control tabular-nums" id="form-stacked-price" type="number" value="2500" min="0" step="100" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="form-stacked-price-error">
	<div class="invalid-feedback" id="form-stacked-price-error"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-triangle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Lower than the child price</div>
</div>
```

### A longer hint

A `details` with `form-more` folds what a short hint cannot say. Its chevron turns as it opens.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-more-keep">Keep the log for, days</label>
	<input class="form-control tabular-nums" id="form-more-keep" type="number" value="90" min="1" aria-describedby="form-more-hint">
	<div class="form-text" id="form-more-hint">Older records are removed at night.</div>
	<details class="form-more form-text"><summary><i class="bi bi-chevron-right" aria-hidden="true"></i>More</summary><div class="mt-4">The count starts from the day a record is written. A record a person marked to keep stays, whatever this number says, until the mark is taken off.</div></details>
</div>
```

### An icon in the field

`form-adorn` puts an icon inside a field or a select, at its start; the field keeps its own name. With `form-floating` on the same element the label starts after the icon, inside the one border - the way a sign-in form draws its fields.

```html
<div class="form-adorn">
	<i class="bi bi-search" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<input class="form-control" type="search" name="q" placeholder="Name, slug or code" aria-label="Search excursions">
</div>
<div class="form-floating form-adorn">
	<i class="bi bi-envelope" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<input class="form-control" id="form-adorn-mail" type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" autocomplete="email">
	<label for="form-adorn-mail">E-mail</label>
</div>
<div class="form-floating form-adorn">
	<i class="bi bi-globe2" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<select class="form-select" id="form-adorn-country" autocomplete="country-name"><option>Northland</option><option>Southland</option><option>Eastland</option></select>
	<label for="form-adorn-country">Country</label>
</div>
<div class="input-group">
	<div class="form-floating form-adorn">
		<i class="bi bi-key" aria-hidden="true"></i>
		<input class="form-control" id="form-adorn-password" type="password" placeholder="Password" autocomplete="current-password">
		<label for="form-adorn-password">Password</label>
	</div>
	<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" commandfor="form-adorn-password" command="--reveal" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Show the password"><i class="bi bi-eye" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</div>
```

### Sizes

`form-control-sm` and `form-select-sm` are 28 px high, the default 32 px, `-lg` 40 px - the same heights as the buttons beside them.

```html
<input class="form-control form-control-sm" name="small-field" placeholder="Small" aria-label="Small field">
<input class="form-control" name="default-field" placeholder="Default" aria-label="Default field">
<input class="form-control form-control-lg" name="large-field" placeholder="Large" aria-label="Large field">
<select class="form-select form-select-sm" name="small-select" aria-label="Small select"><option>Small select</option></select>
```

### A one-time code

`form-control-otp` spaces the digits of a code from an app or a message in one field. One field takes a paste and the code the system offers above the keyboard - a box per digit takes neither - and the form goes by its button, never by the last digit.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-otp-code">6-digit code from your app</label>
	<input class="form-control form-control-otp" id="form-otp-code" type="text" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code" pattern="[0-9 \-]*" spellcheck="false" enterkeyhint="done" aria-describedby="form-otp-code-hint">
	<div class="form-text" id="form-otp-code-hint">Spaces and dashes are fine.</div>
</div>
```

### A new password

A button with `command="--reveal"` for a password field shows its text and hides it again - `aria-pressed` says which - and the field hides it on its form's submit and when the page comes back from the history. Each change bubbles from the field as `redz:reveal`, `detail.revealed` true or false, so a page that copies the shown text elsewhere hides it there too. Each element with `data-strength` naming the field shows its level as it is typed: shorter than its `minlength`, long enough, then longer or of three kinds of characters, then both - a `meter` at once, and the words, the page's texts `strength.short`, `.fair`, `.good` and `.strong`, once the typing pauses, said politely by a live region of the field's own - VoiceOver says nothing of a password field's own description changing, so the words' element needs no `aria-live`. The level is a hint: the server keeps its own rules.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-password-new">New password</label>
	<div class="input-group">
		<input class="form-control" id="form-password-new" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" minlength="12" spellcheck="false" aria-describedby="form-password-hint form-password-level">
		<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" commandfor="form-password-new" command="--reveal" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Show the password"><i class="bi bi-eye" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	</div>
	<meter class="meter" min="0" max="4" low="2" high="3" optimum="4" value="0" data-strength="form-password-new" aria-label="Password strength"></meter>
	<div class="form-text" id="form-password-level" data-strength="form-password-new"></div>
	<div class="form-text" id="form-password-hint">At least 12 characters. A phrase of a few words is easy to remember.</div>
</div>
```

### A range

`form-range` on an `<input type="range">` is the browser's own slider in the theme's accent: it keeps its keys (the arrows, `Home`, `End`, `Page Up` and `Page Down`) and its look in forced colors. The label says what it sets; when the number matters, write it beside the slider.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-range-quality">Photo quality</label>
	<input class="form-range" id="form-range-quality" type="range" min="40" max="100" step="5" value="80">
</div>
```

### A button beside a floating field

`btn-float` makes a button as tall as a floating field, for the one action beside it; with `btn-icon` it is square.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-8">
	<div class="form-floating flex-fill">
		<input class="form-control" id="form-float-button-code" placeholder="Voucher code">
		<label for="form-float-button-code">Voucher code</label>
	</div>
	<button class="btn btn-secondary btn-float" type="button">Apply</button>
</div>
```

### A text that grows

`data-grow` on a `textarea` starts it at its `rows` - `rows="1"` is one line - and grows it with its text, without the five lines a text area takes otherwise. Where the browser has `field-sizing: content` - Chrome 123, Firefox 152, Safari 26.2 - CSS does it; below, the library sizes it from its text as it is typed, reset and loaded. A `max-h-*` caps it, and past the cap it scrolls.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-grow-text">Translation</label>
	<textarea class="form-control max-h-160" id="form-grow-text" rows="1" data-grow>Speedboat to the marine park</textarea>
</div>
```

### A count of characters

`form-counter` with `data-counter` naming a field shows how much is typed against its `maxlength`, or against the counter's `data-counter-max`, which lets the text go over - a title the search results cut. From nine tenths it turns to the warning tone, past the most to danger (`data-state` `near` and `over`), and once the typing pauses near or over, the count is said politely in the page's text `counter`. Joined to the field by `aria-describedby`, the count is read with it.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-counter-title">Page title</label>
	<input class="form-control" id="form-counter-title" value="North Bay marine park by speedboat" aria-describedby="form-counter-title-count">
	<div class="form-counter" id="form-counter-title-count" data-counter="form-counter-title" data-counter-max="60"></div>
</div>
```

### Number steps

Buttons with `command="--step-up"` or `"--step-down"` and `aria-controls` naming a number field step it by its `step` within its `min` and `max`, and fire `input` and `change` as typing does; at an end a button is `aria-disabled`. The arrow keys in the field step it already: the buttons are for a pointer.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-step-guests">Guests</label>
	<div class="input-group max-w-160">
		<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" command="--step-down" aria-controls="form-step-guests" aria-label="One guest fewer"><i class="bi bi-dash-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
		<input class="form-control tabular-nums text-center" id="form-step-guests" type="number" min="1" max="12" value="2">
		<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" command="--step-up" aria-controls="form-step-guests" aria-label="One guest more"><i class="bi bi-plus-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	</div>
</div>
```

### Chips for typed values

`chip-input` is one field of several typed values, drawn as one box: the values as chips, then the entry, a `form-ghost` of any type. What the form sends is the box's hidden field - the values joined by `data-chips-join`, a comma by default - and the chips are drawn from it, at load and whenever it changes. `Enter`, the separator or the `command="--add"` button takes what is typed, by the entry's own rules - `min`, `max`, `step`, `pattern`, `type`; a value held already and one past `data-chips-max` are refused too. A refusal keeps the typed text, marks the entry `aria-invalid` and stands in words under the box. `data-chips-order` sorts the values - numbers as numbers in a number entry, words in the page's language - and without it they stay as typed. A chip reads as the entry's `datalist` option of its value, else as the value.

```html
<div class="form-field max-w-360">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-chips-days">Remind before the event, days</label>
	<div class="chip-input" data-chips-max="8" data-chips-order="descending">
		<input type="hidden" name="remind_days" value="30,7,1">
		<input class="form-ghost tabular-nums" id="form-chips-days" type="number" min="1" max="365" step="1" list="form-chips-days-words" aria-describedby="form-chips-days-hint">
		<button class="btn btn-icon btn-sm" type="button" command="--add" aria-controls="form-chips-days" aria-label="Add a day"><i class="bi bi-plus-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	</div>
	<datalist id="form-chips-days-words"><option value="1">The day before</option><option value="7">A week before</option></datalist>
	<div class="form-text" id="form-chips-days-hint">From 1 to 365 days, up to 8.</div>
</div>
<div class="form-field max-w-360">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-chips-rooms">Rooms to clean first</label>
	<div class="chip-input">
		<input type="hidden" name="rooms" value="B204,A101">
		<input class="form-ghost font-monospace" id="form-chips-rooms" pattern="[A-Z][0-9]{3}" autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false" aria-describedby="form-chips-rooms-hint">
	</div>
	<div class="form-text" id="form-chips-rooms-hint">A capital letter and three digits; a comma or Enter after each.</div>
</div>
```

| Part | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `chip-input` | The box, drawn as a field. `data-chips-max` caps the count; `data-chips-order` is `ascending` or `descending`; `data-chips-join` joins the values, a comma by default. |
| `input type="hidden"` | The value the form sends, its `name` the field's. Every change fires `input` and `change` on it; a script that sets it, with or without those events, has the chips drawn again. |
| `form-ghost` | The entry, with an `id` for its label and no `name` of its own: its type and constraints are the rules of a value, its `list` the labels of values. |
| `command="--add"` | An optional button in the box, `aria-controls` naming the entry, for a keypad without `Enter`. Like `--step-up`, it has no `commandfor`. |
| `chip-list` | The chips, a `role="list"` the library draws before the entry and names by the entry's label; each chip's `chip-dismiss` button is named by the page's text `remove`. |
| `invalid-feedback` | The refusal's words, which the library puts after the box and joins to the entry by `aria-describedby`; the next edit of the entry takes them away. |

In a tracked form the hidden field is one field: `data-changed` and a refusal's `aria-invalid` go on the box, the field is named by the entry's label, the refusal's words stand under the box, and Discard draws the chips again.

### A colour

`form-control-color` is the browser's own colour picker in a field's box. A text field with `data-color-for` naming the picker is its hex twin: each follows the other, and a twin that holds no colour - `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`, the `#` optional - is `aria-invalid`. A stored colour is drawn by `data-color`, which the library sets as `--redz-color` through the CSSOM, so a page under a strict CSP writes no style: on a `dot`, an `icon-tile` - its icon black or white by the colour's lightness -, a `choice-media`, and the edges `edge-top-color` and `edge-start-color`.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-color-hex">Label colour</label>
	<div class="input-group max-w-240">
		<input class="form-control form-control-color" id="form-color-pick" type="color" value="#2a9d8f" aria-label="Pick the label colour">
		<input class="form-control font-monospace" id="form-color-hex" data-color-for="form-color-pick" value="#2a9d8f" spellcheck="false" autocomplete="off">
	</div>
</div>
<div class="hstack gap-12">
	<span class="dot" data-color="#2a9d8f"></span>
	<span class="icon-tile" data-color="#e9c46a"><i class="bi bi-tag" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
	<span class="icon-tile" data-color="#264653"><i class="bi bi-tag" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
	<div class="card edge-start-color" data-color="#e76f51"><div class="card-body">Overdue</div></div>
</div>
```

### Sent on a change

`data-submit="change"` on a form or on one of its controls sends the form when such a control changes - a filter's select, a sort, a switch - by `requestSubmit`, so the browser's checks and the page's submit listeners run. A text field changes when it is left, not at every key; a combobox's list when a value is chosen.

```html
<form class="hstack flex-wrap gap-12" action="#form-submit" data-submit="change" data-docs-submit>
	<select class="form-select max-w-240" name="sort" aria-label="Sort by"><option value="new">Newest first</option><option value="price">Lowest price first</option></select>
	<label class="form-check"><input class="check" type="checkbox" name="open"> Open now</label>
	<output class="text-muted" data-docs-sent></output>
</form>
```

### Shown by another field

`data-show-when` on a region names a field of its form, and `data-show-in` the values that show it, a space between them; without it, any value does. A checkbox or a radio counts its value when checked. A hidden field beside a checkbox of the same name is what the form sends while it is off: `data-show-in` can name its value, and a region without `data-show-in` does not count it. While the region is hidden its fields are disabled, so the form sends none of them; a field the page disabled itself stays disabled. A region inside a hidden region counts as hidden, whatever its own field holds.

```html
<form class="vstack gap-12">
	<div class="form-floating max-w-320">
		<select class="form-select" id="form-show-pay" name="pay"><option value="cash">Cash on the day</option><option value="card">Card</option><option value="invoice">Invoice</option></select>
		<label for="form-show-pay">Payment</label>
	</div>
	<div class="form-floating max-w-320" id="form-show-tax-region" data-show-when="pay" data-show-in="invoice">
		<input class="form-control" id="form-show-tax" name="tax_id" placeholder="Tax ID">
		<label for="form-show-tax">Tax ID</label>
	</div>
	<div class="vstack gap-4">
		<input type="hidden" name="remind" value="0">
		<label class="form-check"><input class="switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" name="remind" value="1"> Remind the guest</label>
		<div class="form-text" id="form-show-on" data-show-when="remind">A message goes out the evening before.</div>
		<div class="form-text" id="form-show-off" data-show-when="remind" data-show-in="0">The guest is told nothing.</div>
	</div>
</form>
```

### Enabled or required by another field

`data-enable-when` enables its element while a field of its form holds a value `data-enable-in` lists, and `data-require-when` with `data-require-in` makes it required, read as `data-show-when` reads: the values a space apart, any value without the list. A rule on a field owns its `disabled` or `required`, as the server drew it too; a `fieldset` takes its own `disabled`; any other element sets each field inside it, and a field the page disabled or required itself stays so. A disabled field counts as empty for every rule, as the form sends nothing of it: the fields of a hidden region drive nothing. A field hidden by a class or by `hidden` counts by its value, a hidden input too, and a field inside the rule's element never counts.

A disabled field is out of the keyboard's reach, so the field that drives it says why: while a rule disables a field, a text with its own `data-show-when` that the field names in `aria-describedby` joins, as long as it shows, the `aria-describedby` of every control of the driving name. A checked radio a rule disables hands its check to the radio of its group with `data-enable-else`, which fires `input` and `change`; without one the group is left with none checked. A number's step buttons follow the field.

```html
<form class="vstack gap-16">
	<div class="vstack gap-8">
		<input type="hidden" name="wait_on" value="0">
		<label class="form-check"><input class="switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" name="wait_on" value="1" id="form-enable-wait-on"> Wait for late guests</label>
		<div class="form-field">
			<label class="form-label" for="form-enable-wait">Minutes</label>
			<div class="input-group max-w-160">
				<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" command="--step-down" aria-controls="form-enable-wait" aria-label="One minute fewer"><i class="bi bi-dash-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
				<input class="form-control tabular-nums text-center" id="form-enable-wait" name="wait" type="number" min="1" max="60" value="10" aria-describedby="form-enable-wait-why" data-enable-when="wait_on" data-enable-in="1">
				<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" command="--step-up" aria-controls="form-enable-wait" aria-label="One minute more"><i class="bi bi-plus-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
			</div>
			<div class="form-text" id="form-enable-wait-why" data-show-when="wait_on" data-show-in="0">Turn on Wait for late guests to set the minutes.</div>
		</div>
	</div>
	<fieldset class="vstack gap-8" id="form-enable-kind">
		<legend class="form-label">Key kind</legend>
		<label class="form-check"><input class="radio" type="radio" name="kind" value="secret" checked> Secret</label>
		<label class="form-check"><input class="radio" type="radio" name="kind" value="public"> Public</label>
		<label class="form-check"><input class="radio" type="radio" name="kind" value="test"> Test</label>
	</fieldset>
	<div class="form-field">
		<label class="form-label" for="form-enable-domains">Domains</label>
		<textarea class="form-control" id="form-enable-domains" name="domains" rows="2" aria-describedby="form-enable-domains-hint" data-require-when="kind" data-require-in="public"></textarea>
		<div class="form-text" id="form-enable-domains-hint">A public key needs its domains, one a line.</div>
	</div>
	<fieldset class="vstack gap-8">
		<legend class="form-label">Check by</legend>
		<label class="form-check"><input class="radio" type="radio" name="call" value="format" id="form-enable-format" data-enable-else checked> Format check</label>
		<label class="form-check"><input class="radio" type="radio" name="call" value="network" id="form-enable-network" aria-describedby="form-enable-call-why" data-enable-when="kind" data-enable-in="test"> Network call</label>
		<div class="form-text" id="form-enable-call-why" data-show-when="kind" data-show-in="secret public">Only a test key can make a network call.</div>
	</fieldset>
</form>
```

| Attribute | On | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-show-when`, `data-show-in` | Any element | Shows it while the field holds a listed value, else hides it and disables its fields |
| `data-enable-when`, `data-enable-in` | A field, a fieldset or any element of fields | Enables it while the field holds a listed value, else disables it |
| `data-require-when`, `data-require-in` | A field or any element of fields | Makes it required while the field holds a listed value |
| `data-enable-else` | A radio | Takes its group's check from a checked radio a rule disables |

Rules follow `input`, `change` and `reset`, so a tracked form's Discard needs nothing. A value set by code fires no event: `REDZ.ui.follow(form)` reads the rules of the form again, or of the whole page without one.

```js
form.elements.kind.value = 'test';
REDZ.ui.follow(form);
```

## States

## Keyboard and accessibility

- Every control has a visible label: a `<label for>`, or `aria-label` only where the context says it all - a search field with its icon.
- A placeholder is never the label: it goes away as the person types. In `form-floating` the placeholder is only the empty marker.
- An error is said in words in `invalid-feedback`, joined to the control by `aria-describedby`; a color alone never tells it.
- The borders of fields and the focus ring are at least 3:1 against the page in both themes; the text 4.5:1.
- `form-select` paints its own chevron from the theme, mirrored right to left; a multiple select or one with `size` drops it.
- A count of characters is said only near or over its most, once the typing pauses; at every key it would drown the typing.
- Number step buttons are named by `aria-label` and keep their place in the Tab order; from the keyboard the field's own arrow keys step it.
- A region shown by another field is `hidden` while it does not apply, so a screen reader skips it and the form sends nothing of it.
- A field disabled by another field is skipped by `Tab`: its reason, joined to the driving field, is heard there.
- In a chips field, `Enter`, the separator or the `--add` button takes the entry, and `Enter` never sends the form. Each chip's remove button keeps its place in the Tab order; a click, `Delete` or `Backspace` on it removes the chip, and the focus goes to the next chip, else to the entry. `Backspace` in the entry only edits its text: a person who clears the text by it never loses a chip.
- A refused value is said at once, in the words that stand under the box; an added or a removed value is said politely. The remove buttons and the `--add` button follow the entry's `disabled`, its fieldset's too.

## Texts
