- On a page that sends `require-trusted-types-for 'script'`, the editor makes one Trusted Types policy, `redz-editor`, once, as its package loads: that page names it in `trusted-types redz-editor`. The name is part of the editor's contract. Markup reaches the policy only as the editor's own panels, a value through the cleaner, or raw markup parsed inert to be cleaned or read. No other package needs a policy: the main bundle, the charts and the QR codes build by the DOM, and the build refuses a string of markup in them.

## License

Unlike the library, the editor is not under MIT. From 0.17.0 it is under [PolyForm Strict 1.0.0](https://polyformproject.org/licenses/strict/1.0.0): noncommercial use only, no changes, no redistribution. It comes with REDZ products under their terms; any other commercial use needs a separate license. Versions up to 0.16.0 stay under MIT.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Alt` `F10` | From the text to the toolbar |
| `→` / `←`, `Home` / `End` | In the toolbar, the next, the previous, the first, the last button, mirrored right to left |
| `⌘` `B`, `I`, `U`, `K` | Bold, italic, underline, a link |
| `⌘` `Z`, `⇧` `⌘` `Z` | Undo and redo, the editor's own |
| `⌘` `/` | All the commands, by name |
| `Alt` `Enter` | The card of the block under the caret |
| `⌘` `⇧` `↑` / `↓` | Moves the block under the caret |
| `Tab`, `Enter` in a table | The next cell, a new row after the last; the cell below |
| `Enter`, `Backspace` in a list block | A new item; an empty item away |

- The toolbar is one tab stop, named; the marks say whether they are on in `aria-pressed`, the menus are REDZ.UI menus, the dialogs REDZ.UI dialogs.
- The text is a text field of many lines, named by the placeholder; a block's tools are buttons named by what they do.
- Every word comes from the page's texts, the keys of the passport's `editor.texts`; `editor.args` names the `{names}` each one is given.

# Cards

A card is a bordered region of a screen: a header with its title and actions, a body, a footer. It is a region - the width prefixes inside it measure the card, not the window.

## Examples

A card that is a section of the screen is a `<section>` named by its heading. The header holds an icon, the title and whatever belongs to it; the footer holds the card's actions.

```html
<section class="card" aria-labelledby="card-basic-title">
	<div class="card-header"><i class="bi bi-cash-coin" aria-hidden="true"></i><h2 id="card-basic-title">Price</h2><span class="text-muted fs-12">in the base currency THB</span></div>
	<div class="card-body vstack gap-8">
		<p>Adults 2,500 · children 1,900 · under four free.</p>
		<p class="text-muted">The visitor's currency is an estimate.</p>
	</div>
	<div class="card-footer justify-content-end">
		<button class="btn" type="button">Cancel</button>
		<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button">Save</button>
	</div>
</section>
```

A product tints the head of every card with `--redz-card-header-bg`.

### Images

`card-img-top` and `card-img-bottom` round the image with the card's corners; `card-img-overlay` lays the card's words over a `card-img`, in white on a shade that rises from the bottom, so they read on any picture; the picture fills its card when a grid stretches the card. A `stretched-link` makes the whole card its link.

```html
<div class="grid md:cols-2 gap-16">
	<section class="card" aria-labelledby="card-images-title">
		<img class="card-img-top ratio-16x9" src="img/lagoon.svg" alt="A lagoon under green hills">
		<div class="card-body vstack gap-4">
			<h2 class="fs-16" id="card-images-title"><a class="stretched-link" href="#card-images">North Bay by speedboat</a></h2>
			<p class="text-muted mb-0">From 2 500 THB · a day</p>
		</div>
	</section>
	<section class="card" aria-labelledby="card-overlay-title">
		<img class="card-img ratio-16x9" src="img/lagoon.svg" alt="">
		<div class="card-img-overlay vstack justify-content-end">
			<h2 class="fs-16" id="card-overlay-title">The emerald lake</h2>
		</div>
	</section>
</div>
```

### Tabs on a card

A `nav` placed straight in the card lines up with the header's padding.

```html
<section class="card" aria-labelledby="card-tabs-title">
	<div class="card-header"><h2 id="card-tabs-title">North Bay</h2></div>
	<div class="nav nav-underline" role="tablist" aria-label="North Bay">
		<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="card-tabs-1" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="card-tabs-panel-1">Details</button>
		<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="card-tabs-2" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="card-tabs-panel-2">Prices</button>
	</div>
	<div class="card-body" id="card-tabs-panel-1" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="card-tabs-1" tabindex="0"><p>A day at sea: snorkelling at two reefs, lunch on the boat.</p></div>
	<div class="card-body" id="card-tabs-panel-2" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="card-tabs-2" tabindex="0" hidden><p>Adults 2,500 · children 1,900.</p></div>
</section>
```

### A grid of cards

The parent sets the grid; each card measures itself. Under 576 px of the region the cards stack.

```html
<div class="grid sm:cols-2 gap-16">
	<section class="card" aria-labelledby="card-grid-a"><div class="card-header"><h2 id="card-grid-a">Bookings</h2></div><div class="card-body"><p class="fs-24 fw-600 tabular-nums">128</p><p class="text-muted">this week</p></div></section>
	<section class="card" aria-labelledby="card-grid-b"><div class="card-header"><h2 id="card-grid-b">Revenue</h2></div><div class="card-body"><p class="fs-24 fw-600 tabular-nums">312,400 THB</p><p class="text-muted">this week</p></div></section>
</div>
```

### A body that scrolls

`card-scroll` with a height - `max-h-*`, from 160 to 640 px - keeps the card's header and footer in view and scrolls its body between them, as a dialog does: a list of tickets, a [thread](thread.md) above its reply box.

```html
<section class="card card-scroll max-h-240" aria-labelledby="card-scrolling-title">
	<div class="card-header"><h2 id="card-scrolling-title">Tickets</h2></div>
	<div class="card-body" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-labelledby="card-scrolling-title">
		<div class="list-group list-group-flush">
			<button class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" type="button" aria-current="true">The booking page shows the wrong price</button>
			<button class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" type="button">A new language for the site</button>
			<button class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" type="button">The invoice for October</button>
			<button class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" type="button">Photos do not upload from a phone</button>
			<button class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" type="button">Change the site's address</button>
			<button class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" type="button">Two owners for one site</button>
		</div>
	</div>
	<div class="card-footer"><button class="btn btn-sm" type="button"><i class="bi bi-plus-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i>New ticket</button></div>
</section>
```

### A state on its edge

The utility `edge-top-{tone}` draws a 3 px line of a state on a card's top edge, instead of coloring its frame; `edge-start-{tone}` does it on the start edge of a row. The words still say the state.

```html
<div class="grid sm:cols-2 gap-16">
	<section class="card edge-top-success" aria-labelledby="card-edge-a"><div class="card-header"><h2 id="card-edge-a">Dispatcher</h2></div><div class="card-body"><p>Running, last beat 4 s ago</p></div></section>
	<section class="card edge-top-warning" aria-labelledby="card-edge-b"><div class="card-header"><h2 id="card-edge-b">Mail queue</h2></div><div class="card-body"><p>Late by 6 minutes</p></div></section>
</div>
<ul class="list-group" aria-label="Plan items">
	<li class="list-group-item hstack gap-12 edge-start-primary"><span>Online booking<span class="d-block fs-12 text-muted">Calendar, deposits, reminders</span></span><span class="ms-auto tabular-nums">490 THB</span></li>
	<li class="list-group-item hstack gap-12 edge-start-success bg-page"><span>Site and hosting<span class="d-block fs-12 text-muted">Included in every plan</span></span><span class="ms-auto text-muted">Included</span></li>
</ul>
```

For a category instead of a state - a site, a team, a kind of job - `edge-top-chart-1` to `-8` and `edge-start-chart-1` to `-8` take the charts' eight colors, so a row matches its series in a [chart](chart.md).

```html
<ul class="list-group" aria-label="Sites">
	<li class="list-group-item edge-start-chart-1">Main Island</li>
	<li class="list-group-item edge-start-chart-2">South Bay</li>
	<li class="list-group-item edge-start-chart-3">West Bay</li>
</ul>
```

## Accessibility

- A card that is a part of the page is a `<section>` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its heading; a card in a list of cards is an `<article>` or a list item.
- A card has no outer margin: the gap between cards belongs to their parent.
- A card being refreshed in place turns busy with `REDZ.ui.busy(card, promise)` - see [Busy](busy.md).

## Tokens

From [`css/components/card.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/card.css). It declares `--redz-link` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-card-header-bg`, `--redz-text-muted`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `card-group` | - | review | grid with gap-16 |
| `card-header-pills` | - | review | a nav straight in the card |
| `card-header-tabs` | - | review | a nav straight in the card |
| `card-link` | - | review | a heading and paragraphs in card-body |
| `card-subtitle` | - | review | a heading and paragraphs in card-body |
| `card-text` | - | review | a heading and paragraphs in card-body |
| `card-title` | - | review | a heading and paragraphs in card-body |

# Accordions

Sections that open one at a time, or each on its own, on the browser's own disclosure - `<details>` and `<summary>`: no script, the keys and the open state built in, and the browser's find in page opens a closed section on a match.

## Examples

Items that share a `name` are one group: opening one closes the one that was open. `open` opens an item from the start.

```html
<div class="accordion">
	<details class="accordion-item" name="accordion-basic" open>
		<summary class="accordion-header">What does a day trip include?<i class="bi bi-chevron-down accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
		<div class="accordion-body">The transfer from the hotel, the boat, lunch, snorkelling gear and the park fee.</div>
	</details>
	<details class="accordion-item" name="accordion-basic">
		<summary class="accordion-header">Can I cancel a booking?<i class="bi bi-chevron-down accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
		<div class="accordion-body">Free of charge up to 24 hours before the start; later, half the price is kept.</div>
	</details>
	<details class="accordion-item" name="accordion-basic">
		<summary class="accordion-header">Are children welcome?<i class="bi bi-chevron-down accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
		<div class="accordion-body">From four years old; under four they travel free.</div>
	</details>
</div>
```

### Each on its own

Without `name` every item opens and closes by itself.

```html
<div class="accordion">
	<details class="accordion-item" open>
		<summary class="accordion-header">Pickup<i class="bi bi-chevron-down accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
		<div class="accordion-body">07:30 at the pier, 07:00 from the hotels of the old town.</div>
	</details>
	<details class="accordion-item">
		<summary class="accordion-header">What to bring<i class="bi bi-chevron-down accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
		<div class="accordion-body">Swimwear, a towel and a sunscreen that spares the reef.</div>
	</details>
</div>
```

### Flush

`accordion-flush` drops the frame and the side padding, for sections inside a card or a drawer.

```html
<div class="card">
	<div class="card-body">
		<div class="accordion accordion-flush">
			<details class="accordion-item" name="accordion-flush" open>
				<summary class="accordion-header">Prices<i class="bi bi-chevron-down accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
				<div class="accordion-body">Adults 2,500 · children 1,900 · under four free.</div>
			</details>
			<details class="accordion-item" name="accordion-flush">
				<summary class="accordion-header">History<i class="bi bi-chevron-down accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
				<div class="accordion-body">Edited yesterday by M. K.; published on three sites.</div>
			</details>
		</div>
	</div>
</div>
```

### Contents from the server

An element with `data-lazy` - a `details` or its `accordion-body`, a region a [--toggle button](collapse.md) opens, a [tab panel](nav.md), a [tree's group](tree.md), a popover or a dialog or a region in one - fires `redz:load` on itself with `{region}` the first time it shows: open at load, put in open later, or opened by a person, never for the paper. The library takes `data-lazy` away first. A page that loads the contents cancels the event and answers with a promise by `event.detail.respondWith`: meanwhile an empty region shows three placeholder lines and, to a screen reader, the page's text `busy`. A refusal puts `data-lazy` back and shows its words in the region, which stays open; the next opening tries again. Writing `data-lazy` again on a region that shows - its contents are stale - loads it again at once.

```html
<div class="accordion">
	<details class="accordion-item">
		<summary class="accordion-header">History of changes<i class="bi bi-chevron-down accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
		<div class="accordion-body" data-lazy data-docs-history></div>
	</details>
</div>
```

```js
document.addEventListener('redz:load', (event) => {
	if (event.target.id !== 'history') {
		return;
	}
	event.preventDefault();
	event.detail.respondWith(fetch('/excursions/12/history')
		.then((answer) => answer.ok ? answer.text() : Promise.reject(new Error('The history could not be loaded.')))
		.then((html) => {
			event.detail.region.innerHTML = html;
		}));
});
```

## States

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | On a section's header |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Opens or closes the section; in a group, opening it closes the open one |
| `Tab` | The next header, or the first control inside an open section |

- The header is the `<summary>` itself, which the browser announces as expanded or collapsed. Put no heading inside it: screen readers announce a heading in a summary unevenly. When the sections need a place in the page's outline, a heading goes before the accordion.
- The chevron is decoration, `aria-hidden="true"`; it turns as the section opens.
- A section opens with a short animation only where the browser has `interpolate-size`, and only when the reader allows motion; elsewhere it opens at once.
- From script: `details.open = true`, and the `toggle` event after each change.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/accordion.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/accordion.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-border`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-radius-8`, `--redz-motion`, `--redz-ease`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accordion-button` | - | remove | the summary is the button; its chevron is <i class="bi bi-chevron-down accordion-icon"> |
| `accordion-collapse` | - | remove | the body follows the summary inside the <details> |
| `accordion-header` | `accordion-header` | review | the item's <summary> with the button's words in it; no heading and no button inside |
| `accordion-item` | `accordion-item` | review | a <details>; the items of one group share a name, as data-bs-parent did |
| `data-bs-parent` | `name` | trigger | the same name on every <details> of the group |

# Carousels

A row of slides seen one or a few at a time: tours, photos, reviews. The browser scrolls and snaps the row - a swipe, a wheel, the arrow keys - and the buttons move a slide back or on.

## Examples

`carousel` on the frame, a named region; `carousel-inner` on the row, a named group that takes the focus; `carousel-item` on each slide. Buttons with `command="--prev"` or `"--next"` and `aria-controls` naming the carousel move a slide, round the ends. An empty `carousel-indicators` fills with a button per slide. The slide in place is `aria-current="true"`.

```html
<div class="carousel" id="carousel-basic-tours" role="region" aria-label="Tours">
	<div class="carousel-inner" role="group" tabindex="0" aria-label="Tours">
		<div class="carousel-item"><div class="p-24 bg-primary-subtle vstack gap-8"><strong>North Bay marine park</strong><span>Kayaks, a lagoon and a viewpoint, a day by speedboat.</span></div></div>
		<div class="carousel-item"><div class="p-24 bg-success-subtle vstack gap-8"><strong>Turtle Cove snorkeling</strong><span>Two bays and a coral garden, lunch on board.</span></div></div>
		<div class="carousel-item"><div class="p-24 bg-warning-subtle vstack gap-8"><strong>Sunset cruise</strong><span>A catamaran round the south coast at dusk.</span></div></div>
	</div>
	<div class="hstack gap-8 justify-content-between">
		<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" command="--prev" aria-controls="carousel-basic-tours" aria-label="Previous"><i class="bi bi-chevron-left" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
		<div class="carousel-indicators"></div>
		<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" command="--next" aria-controls="carousel-basic-tours" aria-label="Next"><i class="bi bi-chevron-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	</div>
</div>
```

### Several at a time

Three custom properties on the carousel set the row, in the module's own stylesheet: `--redz-carousel-items` slides in view, `--redz-carousel-gap` between them and `--redz-carousel-peek` of the next one at the edges. `carousel-center` snaps a slide to the middle, `carousel-auto` lets each slide keep its own width.

```js
.tour-reviews { --redz-carousel-items: 2; --redz-carousel-gap: 12px; --redz-carousel-peek: 24px; }
```

```html
<div class="carousel" id="carousel-several-reviews" role="region" aria-label="Reviews">
	<div class="carousel-inner" role="group" tabindex="0" aria-label="Reviews">
		<div class="carousel-item"><div class="card card-body h-100">“The best day of our trip.” - Anna</div></div>
		<div class="carousel-item"><div class="card card-body h-100">“Kind guides and a clean boat.” - Mark</div></div>
		<div class="carousel-item"><div class="card card-body h-100">“The lagoon is worth the climb.” - Somchai</div></div>
		<div class="carousel-item"><div class="card card-body h-100">“Lunch was a surprise, a good one.” - Leila</div></div>
	</div>
	<div class="hstack gap-8 justify-content-end">
		<button class="btn btn-icon btn-sm" type="button" command="--prev" aria-controls="carousel-several-reviews" aria-label="Previous"><i class="bi bi-chevron-left" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
		<button class="btn btn-icon btn-sm" type="button" command="--next" aria-controls="carousel-several-reviews" aria-label="Next"><i class="bi bi-chevron-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	</div>
</div>
```

### One at a time, fading, playing

`carousel-fade` stacks the slides and shows the current one. `carousel-overlay` lays its buttons over the slides. A button with `command="--play"` plays the slides on every 5 seconds while it is `aria-pressed="true"` - written so, it plays from the start - and pauses while the pointer rests on the carousel or the focus is in it; it never plays for a person who asks for less motion.

```html
<div class="carousel carousel-fade" id="carousel-fade-island" role="region" aria-label="The island">
	<div class="carousel-inner" role="group" tabindex="0" aria-label="The island">
		<div class="carousel-item"><div class="p-32 bg-info-subtle text-center"><strong>Beaches</strong></div></div>
		<div class="carousel-item"><div class="p-32 bg-success-subtle text-center"><strong>Waterfalls</strong></div></div>
		<div class="carousel-item"><div class="p-32 bg-warning-subtle text-center"><strong>Temples</strong></div></div>
	</div>
	<div class="carousel-overlay">
		<button class="btn btn-icon btn-sm" type="button" command="--prev" aria-controls="carousel-fade-island" aria-label="Previous"><i class="bi bi-chevron-left" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
		<button class="btn btn-icon btn-sm" type="button" command="--next" aria-controls="carousel-fade-island" aria-label="Next"><i class="bi bi-chevron-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	</div>
	<div class="hstack gap-8 justify-content-center">
		<button class="btn btn-icon btn-sm btn-text" type="button" command="--play" aria-controls="carousel-fade-island" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Play the slides"><i class="bi bi-play-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i><i class="bi bi-pause-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
		<div class="carousel-indicators"></div>
	</div>
</div>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The carousel is a named region and each slide a group named by the page's text `slide` - “2 of 5”; an indicator button says the same, the current one `aria-current="true"`.
- The row takes the focus (`tabindex="0"` and a name): the arrow keys scroll it, a slide at a time in a fading carousel.
- A slide a person moves to by a button is told politely in a status of the carousel; nothing is told while it plays.
- The play button is a toggle button, pressed while it plays; the pointer resting on the carousel, the focus inside it and a hidden page pause it (WCAG 2.2.2).
- The buttons have no `commandfor`, which WebKit would announce as collapsed; their icons mirror right to left. An indicator is a 24 px target round its dot.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/carousel.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/carousel.css). It declares `--redz-carousel-items`, `--redz-carousel-gap`, `--redz-carousel-peek` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-border-strong`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-ease`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `carousel-caption` | - | review | the slide's own text, laid out with utilities |
| `carousel-control-next` | - | review | a btn btn-icon with command="--next" and aria-controls naming the carousel |
| `carousel-control-next-icon` | `bi bi-chevron-right` | rename | mirrored right to left |
| `carousel-control-prev` | - | review | a btn btn-icon with command="--prev" and aria-controls naming the carousel |
| `carousel-control-prev-icon` | `bi bi-chevron-left` | rename | mirrored right to left |
| `carousel-dark` | - | review | data-theme="dark" on the carousel |
| `carousel-item-end` | - | remove | the browser scrolls the row |
| `carousel-item-next` | - | remove | the browser scrolls the row |
| `carousel-item-prev` | - | remove | the browser scrolls the row |
| `carousel-item-start` | - | remove | the browser scrolls the row |
| `data-bs-slide="prev"` | `command="--prev" aria-controls="ID"` | trigger | the id of the carousel, without commandfor |
| `data-bs-slide="next"` | `command="--next" aria-controls="ID"` | trigger | the id of the carousel, without commandfor |
| `data-bs-slide-to` | - | remove | an empty carousel-indicators makes its buttons |
| `data-bs-ride` | `command="--play" aria-pressed="true"` | review | a play button pressed from the start, which a person who asks for less motion never sees play |
| `data-bs-interval` | - | remove | slides turn every 5 seconds |
| `bootstrap.Carousel` | `the --prev and --next buttons` | review | or scrollBy on carousel-inner; the row scrolls by the browser |

# Collapse

A button that opens and closes a region elsewhere on the page - help under a toolbar, more filters, the details of a row - by the library's own command, `--toggle`. A closed region is `hidden="until-found"`, so the browser's find in page still reaches its words and opens it. A section that opens under its own header is an [accordion](accordion.md).

## Examples

The button carries `command="--toggle"`, names its region in `aria-controls` and says in `aria-expanded` whether the region is open: write it as the region starts, and the library keeps it. It takes no `commandfor`: WebKit would then tell a screen reader the button is collapsed whatever its `aria-expanded` says.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-8">
	<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button" command="--toggle" aria-controls="collapse-help-text" aria-expanded="false"><i class="bi bi-question-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>How prices work</button>
</div>
<div id="collapse-help-text" hidden="until-found">
	<p class="text-muted">A price is per person. Children from four to eleven pay the child price; under four they travel free.</p>
</div>
```

### Open from the start

A region without `hidden` starts open, its button `aria-expanded="true"`.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-8">
	<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button" command="--toggle" aria-controls="collapse-open-filters" aria-expanded="true"><i class="bi bi-funnel" aria-hidden="true"></i>More filters</button>
</div>
<div id="collapse-open-filters" class="hstack flex-wrap gap-8">
	<button class="chip" type="button" aria-pressed="true">With lunch</button>
	<button class="chip" type="button" aria-pressed="false">Private</button>
	<button class="chip" type="button" aria-pressed="false">Sunset</button>
</div>
```

### A chevron and words that follow

Inside a button with `aria-expanded`, an icon `toggle-chevron` turns over while the region is open, `toggle-open` shows only then and `toggle-closed` only while it is closed - by CSS alone, from the state the button already says.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-8">
	<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button" command="--toggle" aria-controls="collapse-chevron-text" aria-expanded="false"><span class="toggle-closed">Show the route</span><span class="toggle-open">Hide the route</span><i class="bi bi-chevron-down toggle-chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</div>
<div id="collapse-chevron-text" hidden="until-found">
	<p class="text-muted">The pier at 08:30, the emerald lake at 11:00, lunch on Emerald Islet, back by 17:00.</p>
</div>
```

### A details row in a table

A row under a row opens and closes the same way: the region is a `<tr>` with one cell across the table. A table's row cannot be hidden "until found", so it starts as plain `hidden` and closes so again; find in page does not open it.

```html
<table class="table" aria-label="Deleted records">
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">When</th><th scope="col">What</th><th scope="col"><span class="visually-hidden">Details</span></th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr>
			<td class="tabular-nums">12:40</td>
			<td>3 excursions</td>
			<td class="text-end"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-text" type="button" command="--toggle" aria-controls="collapse-row-details" aria-expanded="false">Details</button></td>
		</tr>
		<tr id="collapse-row-details" hidden>
			<td colspan="3">North Bay, Turtle Cove and the sunset cruise, with their photos and reviews.</td>
		</tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | On the button |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Opens or closes the region; every button for it says the new state |

- Find in page opens a closed region on a match where the browser has `hidden="until-found"` - Chrome, Firefox 148 and Safari 26.2 on - and the library marks its buttons open; in older browsers the region stays closed until its button opens it.
- Put the region right after its button in the reading order, or name it, so a reader who opens it finds it.
- From script: `region.hidden = false` opens it - set `aria-expanded` on its buttons yourself then.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collapse` | - | state | closed: hidden="until-found" on the region; open: no hidden; its button has command="--toggle" |
| `collapse-horizontal` | - | review | not planned: a region opens downward, in its place |
| `collapsing` | - | remove | the region opens at once |
| `data-bs-toggle="collapse"` | `command="--toggle" aria-controls="ID" aria-expanded="false"` | trigger | the region is hidden="until-found" while closed; in an accordion the item is a <details> |
| `bootstrap.Collapse` | `region.hidden = false` | review | and setAttribute('hidden', 'until-found') to close; set aria-expanded on its buttons then: a button with command="--toggle" does both |

# List groups

A column of items in one frame - plain rows, or links and buttons to choose from - with the current one and the unavailable ones marked by the same attributes the browser reads.

## Examples

`list-group` on a list, `list-group-item` on each item.

```html
<ul class="list-group">
	<li class="list-group-item">North Bay Marine Park</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">Turtle Cove and Pearl Cove</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">The Five Islands by kayak</li>
</ul>
```

### Links and buttons

`list-group-item-action` makes an item a choice. The current one is `aria-current` - `"page"` for a link to the page shown, `"true"` otherwise; one that cannot be chosen is a `disabled` button, or a link without `href` and with `aria-disabled="true"`. A plain item whose title is a `stretched-link` is that link as a whole, as a [table's row](table.md) is: a click anywhere on it but on its own controls follows the title - with `Ctrl`, `Cmd` or the middle button into a new tab - unless the person was selecting its words, which stay selectable; the title is the one link a keyboard and a screen reader meet. Its other links, buttons, switches and handles stay their own. A `list-group-actions` at its end holds the item's buttons; its icon buttons are dimmed until the item is pointed at or holds the focus, on a device with a pointer, while a button with words keeps its contrast.

```html
<nav class="list-group" aria-label="Sites">
	<a class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" href="#list-group-action" aria-current="page">All sites</a>
	<a class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" href="#list-group-action">lagoon.example</a>
	<a class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" href="#list-group-action">northbay.example</a>
	<a class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" aria-disabled="true">archive.example</a>
</nav>
<div class="list-group" role="group" aria-label="Import from">
	<button class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" type="button">A CSV file</button>
	<button class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" type="button">Another site</button>
	<button class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" type="button" disabled>The old catalog</button>
</div>
```

```html
<ul class="list-group" aria-label="Ways to pay" data-density="compact">
	<li class="list-group-item hstack gap-12"><span class="vstack flex-grow-1"><a class="stretched-link fw-600" href="#list-group-rows">Bank card</a><span class="text-muted fs-12">Visa, Mastercard · 2.9 %</span></span><span class="list-group-actions"><a class="btn btn-sm" href="#list-group-rows">Configure</a><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text" type="button" aria-label="Copy the settings: Bank card"><i class="bi bi-copy" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></span><label class="form-check"><input class="switch" type="checkbox" name="bank-card-on" role="switch" checked aria-label="Bank card on"></label></li>
	<li class="list-group-item hstack gap-12"><span class="vstack flex-grow-1"><a class="stretched-link fw-600" href="#list-group-rows">Bank transfer</a><span class="text-muted fs-12">Three working days</span></span><span class="list-group-actions"><a class="btn btn-sm" href="#list-group-rows">Configure</a></span><label class="form-check"><input class="switch" type="checkbox" name="bank-transfer-on" role="switch" aria-label="Bank transfer on"></label></li>
</ul>
```

An item's padding follows `data-density`, as a table's row does: 12 px by default, 8 px `compact`, 16 px `comfortable`, 20 px `spacious`.

### Flush, numbered, with counts

`list-group-flush` drops the frame, for a list inside a card: its rows' words line up with the card's. A flush list of `list-group-item-action` rows keeps the rows' room, so a hover's tint and the current row's bar stand off the words - as in [a card that scrolls](card.md#card-scrolling). `list-group-numbered` on an `<ol>` numbers the items.

```html
<div class="card">
	<div class="card-body">
		<ol class="list-group list-group-flush list-group-numbered">
			<li class="list-group-item hstack gap-8"><span class="flex-fill">North Bay Marine Park</span><span class="badge">28</span></li>
			<li class="list-group-item hstack gap-8"><span class="flex-fill">Turtle Cove</span><span class="badge">11</span></li>
			<li class="list-group-item hstack gap-8"><span class="flex-fill">The Five Islands</span><span class="badge badge-subtle-warning">3</span></li>
		</ol>
	</div>
</div>
```

### Headings

`list-group-header` on an item that is not one: a small heading over the items that follow it, in capitals, on the page's own background.

```html
<ul class="list-group">
	<li class="list-group-header list-group-item">Today</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">North Bay Marine Park</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">Night market and street food</li>
	<li class="list-group-header list-group-item">Tomorrow</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">Turtle Cove and Pearl Cove</li>
</ul>
```

### Side by side

`list-group-horizontal` sets the items in a row; with a width prefix, from that width of the region on: `md:list-group-horizontal`.

```html
<ul class="list-group md:list-group-horizontal">
	<li class="list-group-item">Transfer</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">Boat</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">Lunch</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">Park fee</li>
</ul>
```

### With checks

```html
<div class="list-group" role="group" aria-label="Show on">
	<label class="list-group-item hstack gap-8"><input class="check" type="checkbox" name="lagoon-example" checked>lagoon.example</label>
	<label class="list-group-item hstack gap-8"><input class="check" type="checkbox" name="northbay-example" checked>northbay.example</label>
	<label class="list-group-item hstack gap-8"><input class="check" type="checkbox" name="turtlecove-example">turtlecove.example</label>
</div>
```

### Filtered by a search

A search field with `data-filter` naming a region hides, as the person types, the region's items whose words lack one of the typed words - case and accents aside: list items, items with a `data-value`, [media tiles](media.md), [tree items](tree.md) and table rows; an item's `data-search` stands in for its text. A tree keeps the ancestors of a match and opens their groups. An element with `data-filter-empty` in the region shows when nothing matches. The count is said once the typing pauses, in the page's count text `found`; `Esc` in the field clears it. A hidden item carries `data-filtered`.

```html
<input class="form-control" type="search" name="q" data-filter="list-group-search-list" aria-label="Find an excursion" placeholder="Find an excursion" autocomplete="off">
<ul class="list-group" id="list-group-search-list">
	<li class="list-group-item">North Bay Marine Park</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">Turtle Cove and Pearl Cove</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">The Five Islands by kayak</li>
	<li class="list-group-item" data-search="elephant sanctuary chang">Elephant sanctuary</li>
	<li class="list-group-item text-muted" data-filter-empty hidden>No excursion has these words.</li>
</ul>
```

### Filtered by buttons

A button with `command="--filter"` and `aria-controls` naming the region shows only the items whose `data-NAME` holds a word of its `value`: `NAME` is the button's `name`, `state` without one, and an item may hold several words - `data-state="late failed"`. The buttons of one name are one choice wherever they stand, their `aria-pressed` saying which; a button with `value=""` shows all and stays pressed while nothing narrows, and without one, pressing the pressed button again shows all. Names narrow together, and with the search. A `data-filter-count` inside a button shows how many items it would show; with the region's id as its value anywhere else it reads the page's text `filter.count`, "3 of 9". An element with `data-filter-group` - a card of items, a section - hides while none of its items shows, and a count inside it is its own. A press says the count; the region fires `redz:filter` with `{count, total}`; items the page puts in or changes are filtered again. `REDZ.ui.filter(region, {state: 'paid'})` chooses from code and answers the count; `null` clears every choice and the search.

```html
<div class="hstack flex-wrap gap-8" role="group" aria-label="Show bookings">
	<button class="chip" type="button" command="--filter" aria-controls="list-group-states-list" value="" aria-pressed="true">All<span class="chip-count" data-filter-count></span></button>
	<button class="chip" type="button" command="--filter" aria-controls="list-group-states-list" value="paid" aria-pressed="false">Paid<span class="chip-count" data-filter-count></span></button>
	<button class="chip" type="button" command="--filter" aria-controls="list-group-states-list" value="waiting late" aria-pressed="false">Not paid<span class="chip-count" data-filter-count></span></button>
</div>
<div class="hstack flex-wrap gap-8" role="group" aria-label="Boat">
	<button class="chip" type="button" command="--filter" aria-controls="list-group-states-list" name="boat" value="a" aria-pressed="false">Boat A</button>
	<button class="chip" type="button" command="--filter" aria-controls="list-group-states-list" name="boat" value="b" aria-pressed="false">Boat B</button>
</div>
<input class="form-control" type="search" name="q" data-filter="list-group-states-list" aria-label="Find a guest" placeholder="Find a guest" autocomplete="off">
<p class="fs-12 text-muted" data-filter-count="list-group-states-list"></p>
<ul class="list-group" id="list-group-states-list">
	<li class="list-group-item" data-state="paid" data-boat="a">Alex Sample, boat A, paid</li>
	<li class="list-group-item" data-state="waiting" data-boat="a">Ben Sample, boat A, waiting</li>
	<li class="list-group-item" data-state="late" data-boat="b">Chris Sample, boat B, late</li>
	<li class="list-group-item" data-state="paid" data-boat="b">Dana Sample, boat B, paid</li>
	<li class="list-group-item" data-state="paid" data-boat="b">Ella Sample, boat B, paid</li>
	<li class="list-group-item text-muted" data-filter-empty hidden>No booking matches.</li>
</ul>
```

### Searched on the server

A field with `data-filter-server` hides nothing itself: it asks the page by `redz:search` on the field, with `{query, form, signal}` - `form` the `FormData` of its `<search>` or form, a status select beside it included. It asks 600 ms after the typing pauses, at once on `Enter` and on `Esc`, which clears it, and at once when another control of its search changes. The page cancels the event and answers with a promise by `event.detail.respondWith`; meanwhile the region carries `aria-busy` and, in a `form-adorn`, the field shows a ring at its end. A newer question aborts the `signal` of the one before, and a late answer is dropped. The count is said in the page's text `found`: the answer's `count`, else the items there are. A [Show more](#list-group-more) over the region starts again from the answer.

```html
<search class="hstack flex-wrap gap-8" aria-label="Requests">
	<div class="form-adorn flex-grow-1"><i class="bi bi-search" aria-hidden="true"></i><input class="form-control" type="search" name="q" data-filter="list-group-server-list" data-filter-server aria-label="Search requests" placeholder="Subject or person" autocomplete="off"></div>
	<select class="form-select w-auto" name="status" aria-label="Status"><option value="">Any status</option><option value="open">Open</option><option value="closed">Closed</option></select>
</search>
<ul class="list-group" id="list-group-server-list" data-docs-server>
	<li class="list-group-item">The pier gate does not open</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">Refund for a cancelled trip</li>
	<li class="list-group-item">A second invoice for one booking</li>
</ul>
```

```js
document.addEventListener('redz:search', (event) => {
	if (!event.target.matches('[data-filter="requests"]')) {
		return; // a combobox's search fires redz:search too
	}
	event.preventDefault();
	const {form, signal} = event.detail;
	event.detail.respondWith(fetch('/requests?' + new URLSearchParams(form), {signal})
		.then((answer) => answer.json())
		.then(({rows, count}) => {
			document.getElementById('requests').replaceChildren(...rows.map(row));
			return {count};
		}));
});
```

### Show more

A `list-more` under a list holds its count and a button with `command="--more"` and `aria-controls` naming the list - a list group, any element whose children are its items, a table or its body. The button fires `redz:more` on the list with `{shown, signal}`; the page answers with a promise by `event.detail.respondWith` and the button is busy until the page has put the next items in. Then the focus goes to the first new item, or to its first link or button when it is neither and holds one, and the page's text `more.loaded` says how many came. The answer may say `{total}` or `{done: true}`; an answer that adds nothing is the end too, and `data-more-total` on the button is a total known from the start. At the end the button hides. With `data-more-max` it hides at that many items and a `data-more-cap` beside it shows the page's sentence instead - "Narrow the search to see older requests". A `data-more-count` reads the page's text `more.count`, "10 of 23", or `more.some`, "10+", while the total is unknown. A refusal keeps the button and the focus where they were. Buttons and lists the page puts in later, or a button given `aria-controls` later, are written at once, and a list the page redraws is counted again. After it replaced the items - a refresh, a filter its server answered - the page says what it knows: `REDZ.ui.more(list, {total: 23})`, `REDZ.ui.more(list, {done: true})`, or `REDZ.ui.more(list, {})` while the total is unknown; a question still out is aborted.

```html
<section class="card" aria-labelledby="list-group-more-title">
	<div class="card-header"><h2 class="fs-14" id="list-group-more-title">Pickup points</h2></div>
	<ul class="list-group list-group-flush" id="list-group-more-list" data-docs-more>
		<li class="list-group-item"><a href="#list-group-more">Pickup point 1</a></li>
		<li class="list-group-item"><a href="#list-group-more">Pickup point 2</a></li>
		<li class="list-group-item"><a href="#list-group-more">Pickup point 3</a></li>
		<li class="list-group-item"><a href="#list-group-more">Pickup point 4</a></li>
	</ul>
	<div class="list-more">
		<span data-more-count></span>
		<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button" command="--more" aria-controls="list-group-more-list" data-more-total="11" data-more-max="8">Show more</button>
		<span data-more-cap hidden>Search by name to find the other points.</span>
	</div>
</section>
```

### Reordering

A list with `data-reorder` naming a hidden field moves its items, each with a `data-value`, by a `drag-handle`: a button opening the list's menu of moves, whose items carry `data-move` - `up`, `down`, `first`, `last` - or the pointer dragging the handle: a lifted copy follows the pointer, the item's place - an empty slot - goes where it will land, and the other items glide aside; near the edge of the box the list scrolls in, it scrolls, and `Escape` takes the item back. A move by the menu glides too; with reduced motion nothing glides. Each move ends with the focus back on the handle, and the page's text `moved` says the new place. Then `redz:move` fires on the item: a page that saves cancels it and answers with a promise - refused, the move is undone and the page's words are said; left alone, hidden fields beside the list hold the new order for the form.

```html
<ul class="list-group" id="list-group-moves-list" aria-label="Stops of the tour" data-reorder="stops[]">
	<li class="list-group-item hstack gap-8" data-value="pier"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="list-group-moves-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: The pier"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>The pier</li>
	<li class="list-group-item hstack gap-8" data-value="lagoon"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="list-group-moves-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: The emerald lake"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>The emerald lake</li>
	<li class="list-group-item hstack gap-8" data-value="beach"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="list-group-moves-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Lunch on the beach"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>Lunch on the beach</li>
</ul>
<div class="menu" id="list-group-moves-menu" popover role="menu" aria-label="Move">
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="up"><i class="bi bi-arrow-up" aria-hidden="true"></i>Move up</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="down"><i class="bi bi-arrow-down" aria-hidden="true"></i>Move down</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="first">Move to the top</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="last">Move to the bottom</button>
</div>
```

A table's rows move the same: `data-reorder` on the `tbody`, a `data-value` on each row and its `drag-handle` in a cell. The hidden fields and the polite status go after the table.

```html
<table class="table" aria-label="Lines of the estimate">
	<thead><tr><th scope="col"><span class="visually-hidden">Move</span></th><th scope="col">Item</th><th scope="col" class="text-end">Amount</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody data-reorder="lines[]">
		<tr data-value="cement"><td><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="list-group-moves-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Cement"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></td><td>Cement</td><td class="text-end tabular-nums">12,400</td></tr>
		<tr data-value="steel"><td><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="list-group-moves-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Steel bars"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></td><td>Steel bars</td><td class="text-end tabular-nums">38,900</td></tr>
		<tr data-value="labor"><td><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="list-group-moves-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Labor"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></td><td>Labor</td><td class="text-end tabular-nums">21,000</td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

In a grid of more than one column, or a row, the pointer drags in two dimensions: the item under it takes the dragged one before or after it, by the half of it the pointer is in. The menu's moves go earlier and later in the order - give them those words.

```html
<div class="grid cols-2 md:cols-3 gap-12" aria-label="Dashboard cards" role="list" data-reorder="cards[]">
	<div class="card" role="listitem" data-value="sales"><div class="card-body hstack gap-8"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="list-group-moves-grid-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Sales"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>Sales</div></div>
	<div class="card" role="listitem" data-value="bookings"><div class="card-body hstack gap-8"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="list-group-moves-grid-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Bookings"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>Bookings</div></div>
	<div class="card span-full md:span-1" role="listitem" data-value="tasks"><div class="card-body hstack gap-8"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="list-group-moves-grid-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Tasks"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>Tasks</div></div>
	<div class="card" role="listitem" data-value="weather"><div class="card-body hstack gap-8"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="list-group-moves-grid-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Weather"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>Weather</div></div>
</div>
<div class="menu" id="list-group-moves-grid-menu" popover role="menu" aria-label="Move">
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="up"><i class="bi bi-arrow-left flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i>Move earlier</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="down"><i class="bi bi-arrow-right flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i>Move later</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="first">Move to the start</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="last">Move to the end</button>
</div>
```

```js
document.addEventListener('redz:move', (event) => {
	event.preventDefault();
	const {item, parent, position} = event.detail;
	event.detail.respondWith(fetch('/stops/' + item.dataset.value + '/place', {method: 'POST', body: new URLSearchParams({parent: parent?.dataset.value ?? '', position})})
		.then((answer) => answer.ok || Promise.reject('The stop could not be moved')));
});
```

## States

## Keyboard and accessibility

- Links and buttons keep their own keys: `Tab` from one to the next, `Enter` - and `Space` on a button - to choose. A list of links that moves between pages is a `<nav>` with its own name.
- The current item is `aria-current`, never a class: the screen reader says “current page”, the look follows the attribute.
- A link that may not be followed has no `href`: `aria-disabled` alone would leave it working.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/list-group.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/list-group.css). It declares `--redz-list-group-row`, `--redz-list-group-column` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-row-pad`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-row-hover`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-bg-page`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-text-faint`, `--redz-space-12`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list-group-item-danger` | - | review | no item tones: a badge or a dot in the item says it |
| `list-group-item-dark` | - | review | no item tones: a badge or a dot in the item says it |
| `list-group-item-info` | - | review | no item tones: a badge or a dot in the item says it |
| `list-group-item-light` | - | review | no item tones: a badge or a dot in the item says it |
| `list-group-item-primary` | - | review | no item tones: a badge or a dot in the item says it |
| `list-group-item-secondary` | - | review | no item tones: a badge or a dot in the item says it |
| `list-group-item-success` | - | review | no item tones: a badge or a dot in the item says it |
| `list-group-item-warning` | - | review | no item tones: a badge or a dot in the item says it |

# Trees

Pages under pages, a menu's items, folders: a list whose items open their own lists, each a link or a name, and moved by a handle.

## Examples

`tree` on the list, `tree-item` on each item, its `tree-row` holding a `tree-toggle` - a `--toggle` button naming the item's `tree-group` in `aria-controls`, as on [collapse](collapse.md) - and the item's link. The groups close as `hidden="until-found"`, so the browser's find in page still opens them. A button with `command="--expand-all"` or `"--collapse-all"` for the tree opens or closes every group that holds items.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-8">
	<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button" commandfor="tree-pages-list" command="--expand-all"><i class="bi bi-arrows-expand" aria-hidden="true"></i>Expand all</button>
	<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button" commandfor="tree-pages-list" command="--collapse-all"><i class="bi bi-arrows-collapse" aria-hidden="true"></i>Collapse all</button>
</div>
<ul class="tree" id="tree-pages-list" aria-label="Pages">
	<li class="tree-item">
		<div class="tree-row">
			<button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text tree-toggle" type="button" command="--toggle" aria-controls="tree-pages-excursions" aria-expanded="true" aria-label="Excursions"><i class="bi bi-chevron-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
			<a href="#tree-pages">Excursions</a>
		</div>
		<ul class="tree-group" id="tree-pages-excursions">
			<li class="tree-item"><div class="tree-row"><a href="#tree-pages">North Bay by speedboat</a></div></li>
			<li class="tree-item"><div class="tree-row"><a href="#tree-pages">Night market and street food</a></div></li>
		</ul>
	</li>
	<li class="tree-item">
		<div class="tree-row">
			<button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text tree-toggle" type="button" command="--toggle" aria-controls="tree-pages-islands" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Islands"><i class="bi bi-chevron-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
			<a href="#tree-pages">Islands</a>
		</div>
		<ul class="tree-group" id="tree-pages-islands" hidden="until-found">
			<li class="tree-item"><div class="tree-row"><a href="#tree-pages">Turtle Cove</a></div></li>
			<li class="tree-item"><div class="tree-row"><a href="#tree-pages">Moon Cove</a></div></li>
		</ul>
	</li>
	<li class="tree-item">
		<div class="tree-row">
			<button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text tree-toggle" type="button" command="--toggle" aria-controls="tree-pages-archive" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Archive"><i class="bi bi-chevron-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
			<a href="#tree-pages">Archive</a>
		</div>
		<ul class="tree-group" id="tree-pages-archive" hidden="until-found" data-lazy data-docs-lazy></ul>
	</li>
	<li class="tree-item"><div class="tree-row"><a href="#tree-pages">Contacts</a></div></li>
</ul>
```

### Children from the server

A group with `data-lazy` fires `redz:load` on it when it first opens, as any [region that loads](accordion.md#accordion-lazy) does. A page that loads the items cancels it and answers with a promise: the toggle is busy and the group shows placeholder lines until it settles; a refusal leaves the group open with its words and the next opening tries again. The Archive above answers after 400 ms.

```js
document.addEventListener('redz:load', (event) => {
	event.preventDefault();
	event.detail.respondWith(fetch('/pages?parent=' + event.target.dataset.parent)
		.then((answer) => answer.text())
		.then((items) => event.target.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', items)));
});
```

### Moved by a handle

A tree with `data-reorder` moves its items as a list does - see [reordering](list-group.md#list-group-reorder) - and its menu of moves adds `data-move="in"`, to the end of the group of the item above, and `"out"`, after its parent; an item can go in where the item above has a `tree-group`, empty or not. `data-parent` names the hidden field of each item's parent, its value the item's key.

```html
<ul class="tree" id="tree-menu-list" aria-label="The site's menu" data-reorder="menu[]" data-parent="menu_parent">
	<li class="tree-item" data-value="home">
		<div class="tree-row">
			<button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="tree-menu-moves" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Home"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
			<span>Home</span>
		</div>
		<ul class="tree-group" id="tree-menu-home"></ul>
	</li>
	<li class="tree-item" data-value="tours">
		<div class="tree-row">
			<button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="tree-menu-moves" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Tours"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
			<span>Tours</span>
		</div>
		<ul class="tree-group" id="tree-menu-tours">
			<li class="tree-item" data-value="boats">
				<div class="tree-row">
					<button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="tree-menu-moves" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Boats"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
					<span>Boats</span>
				</div>
				<ul class="tree-group" id="tree-menu-boats"></ul>
			</li>
		</ul>
	</li>
	<li class="tree-item" data-value="contacts">
		<div class="tree-row">
			<button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text drag-handle" type="button" commandfor="tree-menu-moves" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Move: Contacts"><i class="bi bi-grip-vertical" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
			<span>Contacts</span>
		</div>
		<ul class="tree-group" id="tree-menu-contacts"></ul>
	</li>
</ul>
<div class="menu" id="tree-menu-moves" popover role="menu" aria-label="Move">
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="up"><i class="bi bi-arrow-up" aria-hidden="true"></i>Move up</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="down"><i class="bi bi-arrow-down" aria-hidden="true"></i>Move down</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="in"><i class="bi bi-arrow-return-right flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i>Move into the item above</button>
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-move="out"><i class="bi bi-arrow-bar-left flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i>Move out</button>
</div>
```

### The current page, actions and checks

A row whose link has `aria-current` - the page open now - is tinted and its link bold. `tree-actions` at the end of a row holds its buttons: quiet until the row is hovered, holds the focus or has a menu open on a pointer screen, always shown on a touch screen. A `check` in a row posts by its own name, for a batch over the chosen pages. A search with [`data-filter`](list-group.md#list-group-filter) keeps the parents of a match.

```html
<input class="form-control" type="search" name="q" data-filter="tree-current-list" aria-label="Find a page" placeholder="Find a page" autocomplete="off">
<ul class="tree" id="tree-current-list" aria-label="Pages to publish">
	<li class="tree-item">
		<div class="tree-row">
			<input class="check" type="checkbox" name="pages[]" value="excursions" aria-label="Choose: Excursions">
			<a href="#tree-current">Excursions</a>
			<span class="tree-actions"><button class="btn btn-xs btn-icon btn-text" type="button" aria-label="Add a page under Excursions"><i class="bi bi-plus-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></span>
		</div>
		<ul class="tree-group">
			<li class="tree-item">
				<div class="tree-row">
					<input class="check" type="checkbox" name="pages[]" value="north-bay" aria-label="Choose: North Bay by speedboat" checked>
					<a href="#tree-current" aria-current="page">North Bay by speedboat</a>
					<span class="tree-actions"><button class="btn btn-xs btn-icon btn-text" type="button" aria-label="Add a page under North Bay by speedboat"><i class="bi bi-plus-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></span>
				</div>
			</li>
			<li class="tree-item">
				<div class="tree-row">
					<input class="check" type="checkbox" name="pages[]" value="night-market" aria-label="Choose: Night market and street food">
					<a href="#tree-current">Night market and street food</a>
					<span class="tree-actions"><button class="btn btn-xs btn-icon btn-text" type="button" aria-label="Add a page under Night market and street food"><i class="bi bi-plus-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></span>
				</div>
			</li>
		</ul>
	</li>
</ul>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The tree is a list of lists with buttons and links - the disclosure pattern: Tab goes from one control to the next, `Enter` or `Space` opens or closes a group, and the toggle says it in `aria-expanded`. It is not the ARIA tree widget, which the APG itself keeps for choosing, not for links.
- A toggle is named after its item; its chevron points along the line of reading, mirrored right to left.
- The moves are a menu on the handle, so a keyboard, a screen reader and a single tap move an item as a drag does; after a move the focus stays on the moved item's handle and its new place is said politely.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/tree.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/tree.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-control-height`, `--redz-control-height-sm`, `--redz-radius-6`, `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-motion`, `--redz-ease`.

# Message threads

A conversation in a card: each message with its author, time and files, the person's own at the end in a tint, the other side's at the start - edited in place, the reply box held under the thread.

## Example

`ol class="thread"` of `thread-message`s; `data-mine` puts the person's own at the end in a tint. A message holds an [avatar](avatar.md) and `thread-body`: `thread-meta` - the name, a `time`, `thread-edited` and the message's buttons -, `thread-bubble`, which keeps its line breaks, and `thread-files` - thumbnails up to 9rem × 7rem, each with a `thread-file-remove` that shows while the message is edited. Editing is an [inline edit](inline-edit.md): the form takes the bubble's place. In a `card card-scroll` with a height the thread scrolls between the card's header and its footer, which holds the reply.

```html
<section class="card card-scroll max-h-560" aria-labelledby="thread-desk-title">
	<div class="card-header hstack flex-wrap gap-8"><h2 id="thread-desk-title">The booking page shows the wrong price</h2><span class="badge badge-subtle-warning">Open</span></div>
	<div class="card-body">
		<ol class="thread" aria-label="Messages">
			<li class="thread-message">
				<span class="avatar avatar-sm" aria-hidden="true">AR</span>
				<div class="thread-body">
					<div class="thread-meta"><span>Example Resort</span><time datetime="2026-11-04T09:12">09:12</time></div>
					<div class="thread-bubble">The child price on North Bay shows 2,500 THB.&#10;It should be 1,900 THB since Monday.</div>
					<div class="thread-files"><a href="img/lagoon.svg"><img src="img/lagoon.svg" alt="Screenshot of the price"></a></div>
				</div>
			</li>
			<li class="thread-message" data-mine>
				<span class="avatar avatar-sm" aria-hidden="true">RZ</span>
				<div class="thread-body">
					<div class="thread-meta"><span>REDZ support</span><time datetime="2026-11-04T09:30">09:30</time><span class="thread-edited">edited</span><button class="btn btn-xs btn-icon btn-text" type="button" commandfor="thread-desk-edit" command="--edit" aria-label="Edit the message"><i class="bi bi-pencil" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></div>
					<div class="thread-bubble" id="thread-desk-reply">Thank you - the price list was published before the change. It is fixed now; please check the page again.</div>
					<form class="inline-edit-form" id="thread-desk-edit" data-for="thread-desk-reply" hidden>
						<textarea class="form-control" name="text" aria-label="Message" rows="3">Thank you - the price list was published before the change. It is fixed now; please check the page again.</textarea>
						<button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" type="submit">Save</button>
						<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button" commandfor="thread-desk-edit" command="--cancel">Cancel</button>
						<div class="invalid-feedback" hidden></div>
					</form>
					<div class="thread-files"><span><img src="img/qr.svg" alt="The fixed page"><button class="btn btn-xs btn-icon thread-file-remove" type="button" aria-label="Remove the fixed page"><i class="bi bi-x-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></span></div>
				</div>
			</li>
		</ol>
	</div>
	<div class="card-footer">
		<textarea class="form-control" name="reply" rows="2" aria-label="Reply" placeholder="Write a reply"></textarea>
		<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button"><i class="bi bi-send" aria-hidden="true"></i>Send</button>
		<button class="btn ms-auto" type="button">Close the ticket</button>
	</div>
</section>
```

## Accessibility

- The thread is a list with a name; each message starts with its author and time in words, so the side is never told by place or tint alone.
- A file's thumbnail has the file's own `alt`; its remove button is named by the file.
- The scrolling body of a card is reached by `Tab` through its buttons and links; give it `tabindex="0"` and a name when it holds none.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/thread.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/thread.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-radius-4`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-radius-8`.

# Charts

A chart is the table of its numbers, drawn: columns stacked by day, a sparkline of the last runs, a board of lanes over the next hours. The numbers stay in the page as text, so a screen reader reads the table; a small script only hands them to the stylesheet.

## A package of the release

Charts are linked apart, on the screens that show them, beside the two files: `css/redz-ui-charts.min.css` draws, and `js/redz-ui-charts.min.js` hands it the numbers - every `data-v`, `data-at`, `data-from`, `data-to`, `data-median` and `data-now` becomes a custom property through the CSSOM, which a strict CSP allows where it would refuse a `style` attribute. A number is a share, 0 to 1: a value over the largest, a time over the window.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="redz-ui/css/redz-ui-charts.min.css">
<script type="module" src="redz-ui/js/redz-ui-charts.min.js"></script>
```

## Columns by day

`table class="chart"`: its `caption` is the title, the header cells after the first are the series and draw as the legend, and each row is a day - `th scope="row"` its label, each `td` a segment whose `data-v` is its share of the tallest day, stacked from the first up. The series take eight colors in order, `--redz-chart-1` to `-8`, chosen to stay apart for color-blind eyes in both themes; `data-tone` gives a segment a state's color instead. A row's `title` is its tooltip, a row with `data-empty` a stub on the axis, and a label wrapped in `visually-hidden` is read, not shown - label every few days when there are many. `--redz-chart-height` sets the height, 10rem by default; ninety days fit a card 700 px wide.

```html
<table class="chart">
	<caption>Messages sent per day</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Day</th><th scope="col" data-tone="success">Free</th><th scope="col" data-tone="warning">Paid</th><th scope="col" data-tone="danger">Failed</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr title="Nov 1: 120 free, 30 paid, 4 failed"><th scope="row">Nov 1</th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.615">120</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.154">30</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.021">4</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 2: 132 free, 28 paid, 2 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 2</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.677">132</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.144">28</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.01">2</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 3: 98 free, 41 paid, 6 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 3</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.503">98</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.21">41</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.031">6</td></tr>
		<tr data-empty title="Nov 4: none"><th scope="row">Nov 4</th><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 5: 144 free, 35 paid, 3 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 5</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.738">144</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.179">35</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.015">3</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 6: 160 free, 22 paid, 1 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 6</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.821">160</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.113">22</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.005">1</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 7: 110 free, 30 paid, 9 failed"><th scope="row">Nov 7</th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.564">110</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.154">30</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.046">9</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 8: 90 free, 25 paid, 2 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 8</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.462">90</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.128">25</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.01">2</td></tr>
		<tr data-empty title="Nov 9: none"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 9</span></th><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 10: 150 free, 40 paid, 5 failed"><th scope="row">Nov 10</th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.769">150</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.205">40</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.026">5</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 11: 170 free, 12 paid, 0 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 11</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.872">170</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.062">12</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0">0</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 12: 125 free, 33 paid, 4 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 12</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.641">125</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.169">33</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.021">4</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 13: 140 free, 29 paid, 3 failed"><th scope="row">Nov 13</th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.718">140</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.149">29</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.015">3</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 14: 155 free, 31 paid, 2 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 14</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.795">155</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.159">31</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.01">2</td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

Series without a tone take the chart colors by their column.

```html
<table class="chart">
	<caption>Bookings by channel, this week</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Day</th><th scope="col">Site</th><th scope="col">Partners</th><th scope="col">Walk-in</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr title="Mon: 12 site, 5 partners, 3 walk-in"><th scope="row">Mon</th><td data-v="0.25">12</td><td data-v="0.104">5</td><td data-v="0.062">3</td></tr>

	</tbody>
</table>
```

`chart-values` writes each column's number above it - for one series and a few columns, where the numbers are what a person reads.

```html
<table class="chart chart-values">
	<caption>Guests per month</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Month</th><th scope="col">Guests</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr><th scope="row">Jul</th><td data-v="0.55">220</td></tr>
		<tr><th scope="row">Aug</th><td data-v="0.7">280</td></tr>
		<tr><th scope="row">Sep</th><td data-v="0.45">180</td></tr>
		<tr><th scope="row">Oct</th><td data-v="0.6">240</td></tr>
		<tr><th scope="row">Nov</th><td data-v="0.85">340</td></tr>
		<tr><th scope="row">Dec</th><td data-v="1">400</td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

### A line

`chart chart-line` draws one series as a line with its area under it, through each row's first `data-v`: the script draws one SVG behind the rows, so the line is one stroke at any width, and each row keeps its tooltip and marks its point under the pointer. The scale is the page's: `data-v` is a share of the range it chose - from the lowest to the highest day, padded - and the captions say it. The header names the series for a screen reader and is hidden from sight.

```html
<table class="chart chart-line" data-tooltips>
	<caption>Storage used, last 14 days</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Day</th><th scope="col">Used</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody><tr title="Nov 1 · 40.5 GB"><th scope="row">Nov 1</th><td data-v="0.42">40.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 2 · 41.2 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 2</span></th><td data-v="0.45">41.2 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 3 · 41.0 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 3</span></th><td data-v="0.44">41.0 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 4 · 42.5 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 4</span></th><td data-v="0.5">42.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 5 · 42.0 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 5</span></th><td data-v="0.48">42.0 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 6 · 43.8 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 6</span></th><td data-v="0.55">43.8 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 7 · 44.5 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 7</span></th><td data-v="0.58">44.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 8 · 44.2 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 8</span></th><td data-v="0.57">44.2 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 9 · 45.5 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 9</span></th><td data-v="0.62">45.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 10 · 47.5 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 10</span></th><td data-v="0.7">47.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 11 · 47.0 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 11</span></th><td data-v="0.68">47.0 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 12 · 48.5 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 12</span></th><td data-v="0.74">48.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 13 · 50.0 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 13</span></th><td data-v="0.8">50.0 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 14 · 49.5 GB"><th scope="row">Nov 14</th><td data-v="0.78">49.5 GB</td></tr></tbody>
</table>
```

## Shares of a whole

`chart-bar` with `chart` draws one row as a single bar across: each segment's `data-v` is its share of the whole, and the legend under it names the series - write the share in the legend's words too. The bar is 12 px thick; `--redz-chart-bar-height` sets another.

```html
<table class="chart chart-bar">
	<caption>Payments in November</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Method</th><th scope="col">Card, 58%</th><th scope="col">PromptPay, 31%</th><th scope="col">Cash, 11%</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr><th scope="row">November</th><td data-v="0.58">58%</td><td data-v="0.31">31%</td><td data-v="0.11">11%</td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

`table class="chart-rows"` breaks a whole into rows, longest first: each `tr` a label, its count and its share in words, and a bar under them whose length is the row's `data-v`. The header cells name the columns for a screen reader and are hidden from sight. The bars take the first chart color; a row's `data-tone` gives it a state's.

```html
<table class="chart-rows">
	<caption>Where bookings came from</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Source</th><th scope="col">Bookings</th><th scope="col">Share</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr data-v="0.52"><th scope="row">Search</th><td>182</td><td>52%</td></tr>
		<tr data-v="0.27"><th scope="row">Partners</th><td>94</td><td>27%</td></tr>
		<tr data-v="0.14"><th scope="row">Social networks</th><td>49</td><td>14%</td></tr>
		<tr data-v="0.07" data-tone="secondary"><th scope="row">Other</th><td>25</td><td>7%</td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

## Sparklines

`span class="spark"` with `role="img"` and its summary in `aria-label` draws one bar per run, oldest first: `data-v` its share of the longest, `data-state` - `ok`, `running`, `timeout`, `failed` - its color, `title` its tooltip. 18 px high in a row, `spark-md` 34 px, `spark-lg` 64 px; `spark-median` with `data-median` draws the median as a dashed line.

```html
<table class="table" aria-label="Agents">
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Agent</th><th scope="col">Last 20 runs</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr><td class="font-monospace">backup.nightly</td><td><span class="spark" role="img" aria-label="20 runs: 18 OK, 1 timeout, 1 failed"><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.28" title="OK · 1.1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.36" title="OK · 1.4 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.33" title="OK · 1.3 s"></i><i data-state="timeout" data-v="1" title="Timeout · 3.9 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.26" title="OK · 1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.38" title="OK · 1.5 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="failed" data-v="0.72" title="Failed · 2.8 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.33" title="OK · 1.3 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.28" title="OK · 1.1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.41" title="OK · 1.6 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.33" title="OK · 1.3 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.28" title="OK · 1.1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.36" title="OK · 1.4 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="running" data-v="0.15" title="Running · 0.6 s"></i></span></td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
<figure class="vstack gap-4">
	<span class="spark spark-lg spark-median" role="img" aria-label="20 runs, median 1.2 s, longest 3.9 s" data-median="0.31"><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="Nov 3, 02:00 · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.28" title="Nov 3, 03:00 · 1.1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.36" title="Nov 3, 04:00 · 1.4 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.33" title="Nov 3, 05:00 · 1.3 s"></i><i data-state="timeout" data-v="1" title="Nov 3, 06:00 · 3.9 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="Nov 3, 07:00 · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.26" title="Nov 3, 08:00 · 1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.38" title="Nov 3, 09:00 · 1.5 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="Nov 3, 10:00 · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="failed" data-v="0.72" title="Nov 3, 11:00 · 2.8 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.33" title="Nov 3, 12:00 · 1.3 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.28" title="Nov 3, 13:00 · 1.1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="Nov 3, 14:00 · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.41" title="Nov 3, 15:00 · 1.6 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="Nov 3, 16:00 · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.33" title="Nov 3, 17:00 · 1.3 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.28" title="Nov 3, 18:00 · 1.1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.36" title="Nov 3, 19:00 · 1.4 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="Nov 3, 20:00 · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="running" data-v="0.15" title="Nov 3, 21:00 · 0.6 s"></i></span>
```
