```html
	<a class="nav-link" href="#badge-beside">Paid<span class="badge">128</span></a>
</nav>
<h3 class="hstack gap-8 fs-16">North Bay <span class="badge badge-subtle-warning"><i class="bi bi-clock-history" aria-hidden="true"></i>Stale</span></h3>
```

## Accessibility

- A badge's words are read with the thing it stands beside; write them so - "5" in "New 5" reads as five new orders only if the link says New.
- The tones of text against their fill are at least 4.5:1 in both themes; a tone alone is never the meaning.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/badge.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/badge.css). It declares `--redz-badge-bg`, `--redz-badge-fg` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-fs-11`, `--redz-fs-14`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-primary-contrast`, `--redz-secondary`, `--redz-secondary-contrast`, `--redz-success`, `--redz-success-contrast`, `--redz-danger`, `--redz-danger-contrast`, `--redz-warning`, `--redz-warning-contrast`, `--redz-info`, `--redz-info-contrast`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-primary-text`, `--redz-secondary-subtle`, `--redz-secondary-text`, `--redz-success-subtle`, `--redz-success-text`, `--redz-danger-subtle`, `--redz-danger-text`, `--redz-warning-subtle`, `--redz-warning-text`, `--redz-info-subtle`, `--redz-info-text`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text-bg-danger` | `badge-danger` | review | on a badge; elsewhere bg-danger with the tone's -contrast text in the module's CSS |
| `text-bg-dark` | `badge-inverse` | review | on a badge: the text color as its background, light in the dark theme |
| `text-bg-info` | `badge-info` | review | on a badge; elsewhere bg-info with the tone's -contrast text in the module's CSS |
| `text-bg-light` | - | review | a plain badge, or a tone |
| `text-bg-primary` | `badge-primary` | review | on a badge; elsewhere bg-primary with the tone's -contrast text in the module's CSS |
| `text-bg-secondary` | `badge-secondary` | review | on a badge; elsewhere bg-secondary with the tone's -contrast text in the module's CSS |
| `text-bg-success` | `badge-success` | review | on a badge; elsewhere bg-success with the tone's -contrast text in the module's CSS |
| `text-bg-warning` | `badge-warning` | review | on a badge; elsewhere bg-warning with the tone's -contrast text in the module's CSS |

# Dots

An 8 px dot of a tone beside a word: online, live, the color of a site. The dot repeats what the word says; it never says it alone.

## Examples

```html
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot"></span>Offline</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-primary"></span>Primary</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-secondary"></span>Secondary</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-success"></span>Live</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-danger"></span>Down</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-warning"></span>Slow</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-info"></span>Updating</span>
```

### Categories

`dot-chart-1` to `dot-chart-8` take the charts' eight colors, for a category - a site, a team, a kind of job - not a state: the dot beside a name in a legend or a list matches its series in a [chart](chart.md).

```html
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-chart-1"></span>Main Island</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-chart-2"></span>South Bay</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-chart-3"></span>West Bay</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-chart-4"></span>Hill Town</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-chart-5"></span>East Bay</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-chart-6"></span>Beach Town</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-chart-7"></span>Harbor Town</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-chart-8"></span>Turtle Cove</span>
```

### Live

`dot-live` breathes while its `data-state="running"` - a job at work, a stream on air - and is still at any other state, and always with reduced motion. The word beside it says the state.

```html
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-live dot-primary" data-state="running"></span>Importing</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-live dot-success" data-state="done"></span>Imported</span>
```

## Accessibility

- A dot has no name; the word beside it carries the meaning. In forced colors every dot is drawn in the text color, so the word is what tells them apart.
- Dots print with their colors.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/dot.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/dot.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-text-faint`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-secondary`, `--redz-success`, `--redz-danger`, `--redz-warning`, `--redz-info`, `--redz-color`, `--redz-chart-1`, `--redz-chart-2`, `--redz-chart-3`, `--redz-chart-4`, `--redz-chart-5`, `--redz-chart-6`, `--redz-chart-7`, `--redz-chart-8`.

# Avatars

A round mark of a person: their initials in the accent, 32 px or 24 px with `avatar-sm`.

## Examples

An avatar beside the person's name hides from assistive technology; an avatar alone - the profile button - is named by its button.

```html
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="avatar" aria-hidden="true">MK</span>Marina K.</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="avatar avatar-sm" aria-hidden="true">AT</span>Arthit T.</span>
<button class="btn btn-text btn-icon" type="button" aria-label="MK, profile"><span class="avatar">MK</span></button>
```

## Accessibility

- The initials are 4.5:1 against the fill in both themes.
- Where a person's photo is wanted, put an `<img alt="">` inside the avatar; the name beside it carries the meaning.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/avatar.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/avatar.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-primary-text`, `--redz-fs-12`.

# Logos

A white mat for someone else's logo - a bank, a payment service, a partner - that keeps it readable in both themes and gives logos of any shape the same weight on a line.

## Examples

`logo` around an `img`: a white ground with a thin border and rounded corners in both themes and in forced colors, the picture contained in it. One height for a line - 32 px, `logo-sm` 28 px, `logo-lg` 40 px, an `h-*` utility for a banner, `h-88` - and a width by the logo's area: `data-ratio`, its width by its height as the server measured it, widens the mat by that ratio to the power 0.75, from square to four times as wide, and the picture fills 90 by 80 % of it: a long wordmark stays readable, and a round mark beside it does not look smaller.

```html
<span class="logo logo-sm" data-ratio="4"><img src="img/logo-wide.svg" alt="Lagoonpay"></span>
<span class="logo" data-ratio="4"><img src="img/logo-wide.svg" alt="Lagoonpay"></span>
<span class="logo logo-lg" data-ratio="4"><img src="img/logo-wide.svg" alt="Lagoonpay"></span>
<span class="logo logo-lg"><img src="img/logo-mark.svg" alt="North Bay Tours"></span>
```

A logo drawn on a solid color fills the mat in that color: `data-color` is the color of its edge, and `logo-fade` on the picture softens its sides into it. A photo gets a blurred copy of itself behind it, an `img class="logo-ground"` with an empty `alt`.

```html
<span class="logo logo-lg" data-ratio="3" data-color="#1f3a93"><img class="logo-fade" src="img/logo-solid.svg" alt="Baybank"></span>
<span class="logo logo-lg" data-ratio="1.5"><img class="logo-ground" src="img/lagoon.svg" alt=""><img src="img/lagoon.svg" alt="The lagoon at noon"></span>
```

On a [choice tile](choice.md), a `choice-media` takes the same `data-ratio`, `data-color` and `logo-ground`: the banner of a payment method. There a logo is as high as the banner over the fourth root of its ratio - a 4:1 wordmark gets 70 % of the height, a round mark all of it - and one on its own color fills the banner.

```html
<div class="grid cols-2 gap-12 max-w-480" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Pay with">
	<label class="choice"><input type="radio" name="logo-choice-pay" checked><span class="choice-media" data-ratio="4"><img src="img/logo-wide.svg" alt=""></span><span class="fw-600">Lagoonpay</span><span class="fs-12 text-muted">Card or wallet</span></label>
	<label class="choice"><input type="radio" name="logo-choice-pay"><span class="choice-media" data-ratio="3" data-color="#1f3a93"><img src="img/logo-solid.svg" alt=""></span><span class="fw-600">Baybank</span><span class="fs-12 text-muted">Bank transfer</span></label>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- A logo that names something has an `alt` with that name; beside the same name in words, an empty one.
- The mat stays white in the dark theme and in forced colors, so a logo made for white keeps its colors.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/logo.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/logo.css). It declares `--redz-logo-side`, `--redz-logo-ground` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-ratio`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-6`, `--redz-color`, `--redz-shadow-2`.

# Icon tiles

A rounded square with an icon in it: the mark of a screen's subject in its title, of a kind of record, of a drop zone.

## Examples

The plain tile is in the accent; the tones and `icon-tile-sm` follow Bootstrap's grammar.

```html
<span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-compass" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-secondary"><i class="bi bi-archive" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-success"><i class="bi bi-check-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-danger"><i class="bi bi-x-octagon" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-warning"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-triangle" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-info"><i class="bi bi-info-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-sm"><i class="bi bi-upload" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-lg"><i class="bi bi-building" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
```

### Categories

`icon-tile-chart-1` to `icon-tile-chart-8` take the charts' eight colors, for a category, not a state - the tile of a kind of record matches its series in a [chart](chart.md) and its [dot](dot.md#dot-categories).

```html
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-chart-1"><i class="bi bi-airplane" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-chart-2"><i class="bi bi-car-front" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-chart-3"><i class="bi bi-tree" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-chart-4"><i class="bi bi-sun" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-chart-5"><i class="bi bi-flower1" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-chart-6"><i class="bi bi-bicycle" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-chart-7"><i class="bi bi-moon-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-chart-8"><i class="bi bi-heart" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
```

### In a title

```html
<div class="hstack gap-12">
	<span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-compass" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
	<div><h3 class="fs-20">Excursions</h3><p class="text-muted">Content type · 28 items</p></div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- The tile is decoration: its icon is `aria-hidden="true"` and the words beside it name the subject.
- The icon keeps a 3:1 contrast with its tile in both themes.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/icon-tile.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/icon-tile.css). It declares `--redz-tile-bg`, `--redz-tile-fg`, `--redz-tile-chart` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-tile-base-bg`, `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-tile-base-fg`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-radius-8`, `--redz-radius-16`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-chart-1`, `--redz-chart-2`, `--redz-chart-3`, `--redz-chart-4`, `--redz-chart-5`, `--redz-chart-6`, `--redz-chart-7`, `--redz-chart-8`, `--redz-secondary-subtle`, `--redz-secondary-text`, `--redz-success-subtle`, `--redz-success-text`, `--redz-danger-subtle`, `--redz-danger-text`, `--redz-warning-subtle`, `--redz-warning-text`, `--redz-info-subtle`, `--redz-info-text`, `--redz-color`.

# Stat tiles

A number with its label and an icon in a tone - and, as a button, the filter for what it counts: the numbers a person reads are the buttons they press.

## Examples

`stat` holds an [icon tile](icon-tile.md), a `stat-value` and a `stat-label`; `stat-primary`, `stat-success`, `stat-warning`, `stat-danger`, `stat-info` and `stat-secondary` - a quiet zero - tint the icon and the number. As a `button` with `aria-pressed` a tile is a toggle: pressed, it wears its tone's border and the list below shows only what it counts. A row is a grid: two tiles a row on a phone, four from `md:`.

```html
<div class="grid cols-2 md:cols-4 gap-12" role="group" aria-label="Show agents">
	<button class="stat" type="button" aria-pressed="true"><span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-cpu" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">24</span><span class="stat-label">All agents</span></span></button>
	<button class="stat stat-primary" type="button" aria-pressed="false"><span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-play-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">3</span><span class="stat-label">Running</span></span></button>
	<button class="stat stat-warning" type="button" aria-pressed="false"><span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-clock-history" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">2</span><span class="stat-label">Late</span></span></button>
	<button class="stat stat-secondary" type="button" aria-pressed="false"><span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-x-octagon" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">0</span><span class="stat-label">Failed</span></span></button>
</div>
```

A tile takes the stat's tone unless it has its own: `icon-tile-chart-3` or `icon-tile-success` on the tile stays, for a category in a neutral stat.

```html
<div class="grid cols-2 gap-12 max-w-480">
	<div class="stat"><span class="icon-tile icon-tile-chart-3"><i class="bi bi-cloud-arrow-up" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">14</span><span class="stat-label">Uploaded</span></span></div>
	<div class="stat stat-success"><span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-check-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">2,126</span><span class="stat-label">Matched</span></span></div>
</div>
```

Without a button it only reads: a `div class="stat"`. One long word breaks instead of running past a narrow tile.

```html
<div class="grid cols-2 gap-12 max-w-320">
	<div class="stat"><span><span class="stat-value">14</span><span class="stat-label">Reconfigurations</span></span></div>
	<div class="stat"><span><span class="stat-value">3</span><span class="stat-label">Refunds</span><span class="stat-sub">Counterbalancing</span></span></div>
</div>
```

### Links

As an `a` a tile leads to the list it counts, filtered on its server; the tile of the list shown carries `aria-current="page"` and wears its tone's border, as a pressed one does.

```html
<nav class="grid cols-2 md:cols-4 gap-12" aria-label="Bookings by state">
	<a class="stat stat-primary" href="#stat-links" aria-current="page"><span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-calendar-check" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">128</span><span class="stat-label">Confirmed</span></span></a>
	<a class="stat stat-warning" href="#stat-links"><span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-hourglass-split" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">14</span><span class="stat-label">Waiting</span></span></a>
	<a class="stat stat-danger" href="#stat-links"><span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-x-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">3</span><span class="stat-label">Cancelled</span></span></a>
	<a class="stat" href="#stat-links"><span><span class="stat-value">145</span><span class="stat-label">All bookings</span></span></a>
</nav>
```

### A second line, a trend, a bar and a time

`stat-sub` is a second line under the label. `stat-delta` shows a change with an arrow: `data-trend="up"` or `"down"` turns it, and it is green when the trend is the good one - up, unless `data-good="down"` says that less is better, as for refunds - and red when not; its words say the change, "+12%", and the arrow only repeats them. A `progress` or a `meter` in the tile's words takes their width; `stat-meta` sits at the end - when the number was counted. A tile with no icon tile lays out its words alone, and `stat-emphasis` tints the whole tile in its tone, for the one number a screen leads with. `aria-busy="true"` draws the number as a placeholder while it is counted.

```html
<div class="grid sm:cols-3 gap-12">
	<div class="stat stat-success stat-emphasis"><span><span class="stat-value">412,000 THB</span><span class="stat-label">Revenue in November</span><span class="stat-sub"><span class="stat-delta" data-trend="up">+12%</span> on October</span></span></div>
	<div class="stat"><span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-arrow-counterclockwise" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">6</span><span class="stat-label">Refunds</span><span class="stat-sub"><span class="stat-delta" data-trend="up" data-good="down">+2</span> on October</span></span></div>
	<div class="stat stat-info"><span class="icon-tile"><i class="bi bi-door-open" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span><span class="stat-value">68%</span><span class="stat-label">Rooms filled</span><progress class="progress progress-xs progress-info" value="68" max="100" aria-label="Rooms filled, 68 percent"></progress></span><span class="stat-meta">5 min ago</span></div>
</div>
<div class="grid sm:cols-3 gap-12">
	<div class="stat" aria-busy="true"><span><span class="stat-value">0</span><span class="stat-label">Guests today</span></span></div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- A tile button's name is its number and its label, "2 Late"; `aria-pressed` says it filters. Put the row in a `group` with a name.
- The tone repeats the label; it never says alone what the tile counts. A delta's color and arrow repeat its words.
- A tile link's name is its number and its label; the tile of the list shown says `aria-current="page"`. A tile counting its number is `aria-busy="true"`, and its words come when it is done.
- Pressed, the tile also draws an outline in forced colors.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/stat.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/stat.css). It declares `--redz-stat-tone`, `--redz-tile-base-bg`, `--redz-tile-base-fg` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-text`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-space-2`, `--redz-success`, `--redz-danger`, `--redz-radius-6`, `--redz-fs-24`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-warning`, `--redz-info`.

# QR codes

A white tile for a QR code: a scanner reads dark modules on white, so the tile stays white in the dark theme, in forced colors and on paper.

## Examples

`qr` around an inline `svg`, an `img` or a `canvas`. The code keeps its own quiet zone - four modules of white round it, drawn by the code's generator; the tile adds 8 px more. `--redz-qr-size` sets the code's width, 11rem (176 px) by default.

```html
<figure class="vstack gap-8 align-items-center">
	<div class="qr"><img src="img/qr.svg" alt="QR code: the address of this site"></div>
	<figcaption class="fs-12 text-muted">Scan to open the docs</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure class="vstack gap-8 align-items-center">
	<div class="qr" id="qr-small"><img src="img/qr.svg" alt="QR code: the address of this site, smaller"></div>
	<figcaption class="fs-12 text-muted">7.5rem</figcaption>
</figure>
```

### Drawn by the package

The package `redz-ui-qr` - the module `js/redz-ui-qr.min.js`, linked beside the main script on a screen that shows codes - draws a code into a tile as one SVG path in the tile's black: `data-qr` holds the text, drawn at load, when the tile is put in later and when the text changes. The text goes in as UTF-8, in the smallest of the 40 versions that holds it at the error correction level of `data-qr-level` - `L`, `M` by default, `Q` or `H` - then at the highest level that same version still holds, for free. `data-qr-quiet` is the quiet zone in modules, 4 by default, as scanners need. The path traces the outline of each dark region, so neither paper nor a zoom shows a seam; the same text always draws the same code. The library makes the tile `role="img"`; its name is the page's, an `aria-label` that says what the code holds. A module never falls under 3 px: past the version that would, the tile grows - `--redz-qr-module-min` sets that floor, `0` takes it away, and a size of the page's own on the `svg`, a poster's, wins over both.

```html
<figure class="vstack gap-8 align-items-center">
	<div class="qr" data-qr="https://redz-tech.github.io/REDZ.UI/" role="img" aria-label="QR code: the address of this site"></div>
	<figcaption class="fs-12 text-muted">Drawn from data-qr</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure class="vstack gap-8 align-items-center">
	<div class="qr" id="qr-package-call" role="img" aria-label="QR code: a key for the app"></div>
	<figcaption class="fs-12 text-muted">Drawn by REDZ.ui.qr</figcaption>
</figure>
```

A text such as a two-factor secret should sit in no attribute: `REDZ.ui.qr(tile, text, {level, quiet})` draws it from a variable and answers `true`; the text goes into the code and nowhere else - no attribute, title, console line or storage, and no error quotes it. `REDZ.ui.qr(tile, null)` empties the tile. A text longer than version 40 holds at its level - 2,331 bytes at `M` - is refused: the tile empties, takes `data-qr-error` and hides, and the call answers `false`; the words beside the tile stand alone. The SVG carries no `style` attribute and is built without `innerHTML`, so a strict Content Security Policy with Trusted Types passes.

```js
const {uri} = await fetch('/profile/2fa', {method: 'POST'}).then((answer) => answer.json());
REDZ.ui.qr(document.getElementById('totp-code'), uri);
```

### Downloaded as a picture

A button with `command="--download"` and `aria-controls` naming the tile downloads its code as a PNG on white, to print on a room's door or a table's card: `data-file` names the file, `code.png` by default, and `data-size` is its side in pixels, 512. An inline `svg` is drawn through a `blob:` image, so the page's Content Security Policy needs `img-src blob:`; an `img` from another site needs that site's CORS.

```html
<div class="qr" id="qr-download-room-code"><img src="img/qr.svg" alt="QR code: the menu of room 12"></div>
<button class="btn" type="button" command="--download" aria-controls="qr-download-room-code" data-file="room-12.png" data-size="512"><i class="bi bi-download" aria-hidden="true"></i>Download the code</button>
```

## Accessibility

- A code is a picture of something a person may not be able to scan: give the same thing in words beside it - the address, or the secret key a 2FA app can take typed.
- An `img` gets an `alt` that says what the code holds; an inline `svg` gets `role="img"` and an `aria-label`.
- Forced colors leave the tile alone, so the code is never inverted.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/qr.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/qr.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-8`, `--redz-qr-size`, `--redz-qr-modules`, `--redz-qr-module-min`.

# Ticking times

A time that keeps itself current: how long a job has been running, how long ago a message came. The page writes the moment; the library writes the words and keeps them right.

## Examples

A `time` whose `datetime` is the moment - ISO, with its zone. With `data-elapsed` it shows the time since then as a clock, `m:ss` under an hour and `h:mm:ss` after; with `data-ago` it says how long ago it was, or how soon it comes, in the page's language, and its `title` holds the full moment; `data-ago="short"` says it short, for a narrow place such as a stat tile. One ticker serves every one on the page: each second while an elapsed time is there, else every 30 seconds, and none while the page is hidden. The page's own words stand inside until the library starts.

```html
<p>The backup has been running for <time datetime="2026-11-04T08:00:00Z" data-elapsed data-docs-since="95">1:35</time>.</p>
<p>The last message came <time datetime="2026-11-04T08:00:00Z" data-ago data-docs-since="300">5 minutes ago</time>; the next tour leaves <time datetime="2026-11-04T08:00:00Z" data-ago data-docs-since="-7200">in 2 hours</time>.</p>
<p>Last backup <time datetime="2026-11-04T08:00:00Z" data-ago="short" data-docs-since="2520">42 min. ago</time>.</p>
```

## Accessibility

- A ticking time is never read out as it ticks: a reader hears it where it is, as it is at that moment.
- Say a wait that matters in words once, where it starts - the time beside it is for the eye.

# Steps and timelines

The steps of a long job as it runs - a release, a publish, an install - each with what it found, and the events of a record's history, one under the other.

## A job's steps

`step-list` is an `ol` of steps, each with an icon, its name and a `step-list-detail` at the end; `data-state` says where it is: `done`, `current` - its icon turns while motion is allowed, `ready` - next, it waits for a press and its icon stays still, `failed`, `kept` - failed with the earlier state kept - and `pending`. A job's panel is a `card` with `sticky-top`, under the app header while the page scrolls, its head a [dot](dot.md), a title and the time, and a [progress](progress.md).

```html
<section class="card" aria-labelledby="step-list-job-title">
	<div class="card-header hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-primary"></span><h2 id="step-list-job-title">Publishing the site</h2><span class="ms-auto tabular-nums text-muted">01:42</span></div>
	<progress class="progress progress-xs" max="5" value="2" aria-labelledby="step-list-job-title"></progress>
	<div class="card-body">
		<ol class="step-list">
			<li data-state="done"><i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Check the templates<span class="step-list-detail">84 pages</span></li>
			<li data-state="kept"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-triangle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Resize the images<span class="step-list-detail">2 failed, the old ones kept</span></li>
			<li data-state="current" aria-current="step"><i class="bi bi-arrow-repeat" aria-hidden="true"></i>Write the pages<span class="step-list-detail">31 of 84</span></li>
			<li data-state="pending"><i class="bi bi-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Rebuild the sitemap</li>
			<li data-state="pending"><i class="bi bi-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Clear the CDN</li>
		</ol>
	</div>
</section>
```

### In a narrow box

A `step-list-detail` stays at the end of the line while the name and it fit, and falls under the name, aligned with it, when they do not, at any width of the page. An empty one takes no room, so it can wait for its words, and it can hold a [badge](badge.md).

```html
<ol class="step-list max-w-320" aria-label="Updating the site">
	<li data-state="done"><i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Download<span class="step-list-detail">4.6 MB</span></li>
	<li data-state="done"><i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Compare every file with the release<span class="step-list-detail">2,126 files</span></li>
	<li data-state="done"><i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Apply the changes<span class="step-list-detail">matched 2,126 · fetched 14 · 4.6 MB · 2 migrations · 1 seed</span></li>
	<li data-state="done"><i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Check the schema<span class="step-list-detail"><span class="badge badge-subtle-success">Clean</span></span></li>
	<li data-state="ready"><i class="bi bi-play-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Switch to the new version<span class="step-list-detail"></span></li>
</ol>
```

### More states, and a step's body

Six more states: `warning` - done with a warning, `info`, `ask` - the job waits for the person, `waiting` - for something else, `skipped` and `locked`. A `step-list-body` after a step's name is a block under it, for what the step found or asks; in a list with bodies every step is a block, and the current one, the one that asks and the one that failed are tinted.

```html
<ol class="step-list" aria-label="Moving the site">
	<li data-state="done"><i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Copy the files<span class="step-list-detail">2,140 files</span></li>
	<li data-state="warning"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-triangle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Check the links<span class="step-list-detail">3 broken</span></li>
	<li data-state="ask" aria-current="step"><i class="bi bi-question-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Point the domain here<div class="step-list-body vstack gap-8"><p>Set the A record of lagoon.example to 203.0.113.24 at your registrar, then check it.</p><div class="hstack gap-8"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" type="button">Check the domain</button><button class="btn btn-sm" type="button">Skip for now</button></div></div></li>
	<li data-state="waiting"><i class="bi bi-hourglass-split" aria-hidden="true"></i>Issue the certificate<span class="step-list-detail">after the domain</span></li>
	<li data-state="skipped"><i class="bi bi-skip-forward flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i>Import the old comments<span class="step-list-detail">skipped</span></li>
	<li data-state="locked"><i class="bi bi-lock" aria-hidden="true"></i>Switch off the old site<span class="step-list-detail">an owner's step</span></li>
</ol>
```

## A pipeline

`stage-list` is an `ol` of stages, each a frame: first a line with its icon and its name, then what it says, and a `stage-list-actions` slot for its buttons at the bottom. The stages run across from a region of 768 px and down below it, joined by a line; `data-state` takes the steps' states.

```html
<ol class="stage-list" aria-label="The release of 2.4">
	<li data-state="done"><span class="hstack gap-8"><i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i><strong>Build</strong></span><span class="fs-12">2 min 14 s</span><div class="stage-list-actions"><button class="btn btn-sm" type="button">Log</button></div></li>
	<li data-state="current" aria-current="step"><span class="hstack gap-8"><i class="bi bi-arrow-repeat" aria-hidden="true"></i><strong>Test</strong></span><span class="fs-12">412 of 580 checks</span><div class="stage-list-actions"><button class="btn btn-sm" type="button">Log</button><button class="btn btn-sm" type="button">Stop</button></div></li>
	<li data-state="ask"><span class="hstack gap-8"><i class="bi bi-question-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i><strong>Approve</strong></span><span class="fs-12">An owner signs off</span><div class="stage-list-actions"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" type="button">Approve</button></div></li>
	<li data-state="waiting"><span class="hstack gap-8"><i class="bi bi-hourglass-split" aria-hidden="true"></i><strong>Deploy</strong></span><span class="fs-12">After the approval</span></li>
</ol>
```

A stage that is next and waits for a press is `ready`: it wears the frame of `current`, and its icon stays still.

```html
<ol class="stage-list" aria-label="The update">
	<li data-state="done"><span class="hstack gap-8"><i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i><strong>Download</strong></span><span class="fs-12">4.6 MB</span></li>
	<li data-state="ready" aria-current="step"><span class="hstack gap-8"><i class="bi bi-play-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i><strong>Install</strong></span><span class="fs-12">Waits for your press</span><div class="stage-list-actions"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" type="button">Start</button></div></li>
	<li data-state="pending"><span class="hstack gap-8"><i class="bi bi-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i><strong>Verify</strong></span><span class="fs-12">After the install</span></li>
</ol>
```

## A timeline

`timeline` is an `ol` of events joined by a line: each starts with an [icon tile](icon-tile.md) in its tone, then a `timeline-time`, the words, and a `dl` of details when it has them.

```html
<ol class="timeline" aria-label="The payment's history">
	<li><span class="icon-tile icon-tile-info"><i class="bi bi-receipt" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><time class="timeline-time" datetime="2026-11-02T09:14">November 2, 09:14</time>Invoice issued<dl><dt>Amount</dt><dd>12,500 THB</dd><dt>Due</dt><dd>November 9</dd></dl></li>
	<li><span class="icon-tile icon-tile-warning"><i class="bi bi-bell" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><time class="timeline-time" datetime="2026-11-08T10:00">November 8, 10:00</time>Reminder sent</li>
	<li><span class="icon-tile icon-tile-success"><i class="bi bi-check-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><time class="timeline-time" datetime="2026-11-09T16:41">November 9, 16:41</time>Paid by PromptPay<dl><dt>Reference</dt><dd class="font-monospace">PP-88214</dd></dl></li>
</ol>
```

## Accessibility

- The words carry the state; the icon and the color repeat them - write the state in the step's detail when its name does not say it. Mark the current step `aria-current="step"`; a step or a stage that asks the person holds its own buttons.
- A pipeline's stages are a list in their order, read one after the other wherever they stand on the screen; the current, the asking and the failed one are also outlined in forced colors.
- A job that runs while the person waits says its new step in a polite live region the page keeps - one line per step, not every tick of the clock.
- A timeline's times are `<time datetime>`; its details are a description list, read as pairs.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/step-list.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/step-list.css). It declares `--redz-step-edge`, `--redz-step-top` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-space-2`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-success`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-danger`, `--redz-warning`, `--redz-info`, `--redz-text-faint`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-radius-8`, `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-warning-subtle`, `--redz-danger-subtle`, `--redz-fs-14`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-border-strong`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-fs-12`.

# Empty states

What a list, a panel or a search shows when it has nothing yet: what would be here, and the one action that starts it. And the drop zone of a file field.

## Examples

```html
<div class="empty-state">
	<i class="bi bi-compass" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<strong class="text-body">No excursions yet</strong>
	<p>An excursion is a page with a price, a schedule and a booking form.</p>
	<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button"><i class="bi bi-plus-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i>New excursion</button>
</div>
```

### A drop zone

`empty-state-drop` is a label around a hidden file input: a click or a dropped file goes to the input.

```html
<label class="empty-state empty-state-drop">
	<span class="icon-tile icon-tile-sm"><i class="bi bi-upload" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
	<span class="vstack gap-2"><strong class="text-body">Logo · light theme</strong><span class="form-text">SVG or PNG, drop a file or choose</span></span>
	<input class="visually-hidden" type="file" name="logo-light" accept="image/svg+xml,image/png">
</label>
```

## States

## Accessibility

- Say what would be here and why it is empty - "No excursions yet", "Nothing matches the filters" - and offer the action that changes it.
- The drop zone's file input is hidden visually only; its label is the zone's words, and the focus ring shows on the zone through the label.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/empty-state.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/empty-state.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-space-32`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-text-faint`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-border-strong`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-primary-subtle`.

# Placeholders

Grey bars in the shape of content that is on its way - the first load of a page or a panel. A region that already has content and reloads it gets an overlay instead: see [Busy](busy.md).

## Examples

Each bar is a `placeholder` sized by a width utility. They pulse slowly, and stand still for people who ask for less motion.

```html
<section class="card" aria-label="Loading">
	<div class="card-header"><span class="placeholder w-25"></span></div>
	<div class="card-body vstack gap-8">
		<span class="placeholder w-75"></span>
		<span class="placeholder w-50"></span>
		<span class="placeholder w-100"></span>
	</div>
</section>
```

## Accessibility

- Placeholders are empty elements; the region holding them is named "Loading" until the content takes its place.
- Keep the shapes close to the real content, so the page does not jump when it arrives.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/placeholder.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/placeholder.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-radius-6`, `--redz-border`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder-glow` | - | remove | placeholders pulse by themselves |
| `placeholder-wave` | - | remove | placeholders pulse by themselves |
| `placeholder-xs` | - | review | size by the height of the bar |

# Prose

Long text that comes from an editor or from Markdown, where no element carries a class: a page's content in a preview, a help page, a note. One class on the wrapper sets the size, the rhythm and the measure of everything inside.

## Examples

`prose` on the element that holds the text. Headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, code, rules, images and tables inside it take sizes for reading, a space between blocks and a line no longer than about 72 characters; the interface around it keeps its own smaller type.

```html
<article class="prose">
	<h2>A day at North Bay</h2>
	<p>The boat leaves the pier at eight and is back before sunset. Lunch is on the beach, and the water is calm from December to April.</p>
	<h3>What to bring</h3>
	<ul>
		<li>Shoes for the climb to the lookout</li>
		<li>A hat and water</li>
		<li>Cash for the park fee</li>
	</ul>
	<blockquote>
		<p>The emerald lake is a short walk from the beach.</p>
	</blockquote>
	<p>The booking code is <code>ANG-0812</code>; show it at the pier.</p>
</article>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

- Prose styles the elements the text already has: its headings stay headings, so a screen reader walks them as it walks any page. Start the text's headings below the page's own: a `prose` inside a page with an `<h1>` starts at `<h2>`.
- The measure keeps lines short enough to read; the text still wraps at any width, and a long word breaks rather than widening the page.
- Links are underlined in the text, so they are not told apart by colour alone.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/prose.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/prose.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-text`, `--redz-fs-16`, `--redz-fs-32`, `--redz-fs-24`, `--redz-fs-20`, `--redz-fs-18`, `--redz-link`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-radius-4`, `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-radius-8`, `--redz-bg-page`, `--redz-fs-14`, `--redz-space-8`.

# Dialogs

The browser's own modal `<dialog>`: opened by a command, the page behind it inert and dimmed, closed by its buttons, `Esc` or a click outside. And `REDZ.ui.confirm()` for a question asked from script.

## Examples

A button opens the dialog with `commandfor` + `command="show-modal"`; buttons inside close it with `command="close"`. `closedby="any"` lets a click outside close it too. The focus goes into the dialog - to the control marked `autofocus` - and back to the button when it closes.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="dialog-edit-note" command="show-modal"><i class="bi bi-chat-left-text" aria-hidden="true"></i>Add a note</button>
<dialog id="dialog-edit-note" class="dialog" closedby="any" aria-labelledby="dialog-edit-note-title">
	<div class="dialog-header">
		<h2 class="dialog-title" id="dialog-edit-note-title">A note for the guides</h2>
		<button class="btn-close" type="button" commandfor="dialog-edit-note" command="close" aria-label="Close"></button>
	</div>
	<div class="dialog-body vstack gap-8">
		<label class="form-field"><span class="form-label">Note</span><textarea class="form-control" name="note" autofocus>Pick up at the pier at 8:30.</textarea></label>
	</div>
	<div class="dialog-footer">
		<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="dialog-edit-note" command="close">Cancel</button>
		<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button" commandfor="dialog-edit-note" command="close">Save</button>
	</div>
</dialog>
```

A product tints the head of every dialog with `--redz-dialog-header-bg`; `--redz-dialog-header-end` gives it room below and `--redz-dialog-header-line` a line under it.

### Sizes

`dialog-sm` for a question, the default for a form, `dialog-lg` for a wide table or a preview. A dialog is a region, so the width prefixes inside it measure the dialog: `sm:` fires in the default one, and `md:` in `dialog-lg`, 800 px wide.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="dialog-sizes-sm" command="show-modal">Small</button>
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="dialog-sizes-lg" command="show-modal">Large</button>
<dialog id="dialog-sizes-sm" class="dialog dialog-sm" aria-labelledby="dialog-sizes-sm-title">
	<div class="dialog-header"><h2 class="dialog-title" id="dialog-sizes-sm-title">Publish now?</h2></div>
	<div class="dialog-body"><p>The page goes live on three sites.</p></div>
	<div class="dialog-footer">
		<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="dialog-sizes-sm" command="close" autofocus>Cancel</button>
		<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button" commandfor="dialog-sizes-sm" command="close">Publish</button>
	</div>
</dialog>
<dialog id="dialog-sizes-lg" class="dialog dialog-lg" closedby="any" aria-labelledby="dialog-sizes-lg-title">
	<div class="dialog-header">
		<h2 class="dialog-title" id="dialog-sizes-lg-title">History of changes</h2>
		<button class="btn-close" type="button" commandfor="dialog-sizes-lg" command="close" aria-label="Close"></button>
	</div>
	<div class="dialog-body"><p>Edited yesterday by M. K.; published on three sites; the Thai translation updated today.</p></div>
</dialog>
```

### A confirmation from script

`await REDZ.ui.confirm({title, text, ok, tone})` builds an `alertdialog`, waits for the answer and removes it: `true` for the confirming button, `false` for Cancel, `Esc` or a click outside. The focus starts on Cancel; the button words come from the caller or the page's texts.

```html
<button class="btn btn-danger" type="button" data-docs-run="confirm"><i class="bi bi-trash3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Delete 2 excursions</button>
<span class="text-muted fs-12" role="status" data-docs-answer></span>
```

For what cannot be undone, `phrase` asks the person to type a word first - the site's name, say: a field under the text, labelled by the page's text `confirm.phrase`, takes the focus, the confirming button waits until the words match, and `Enter` in the field confirms then.

```html
<button class="btn btn-danger" type="button" data-docs-run="confirm-phrase"><i class="bi bi-trash3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Delete the site</button>
<span class="text-muted fs-12" role="status" data-docs-answer></span>
```

What a deletion takes with it is said by `note` and `sections`: `note: {tone, text}` is an alert under the text - `warning` by default, `danger`, `info` or `success` - and each of `sections: [{title, items}]` a title over a list, such as what goes and what stays. Every word is text, never HTML.

```html
<button class="btn btn-danger" type="button" data-docs-run="confirm-lists"><i class="bi bi-trash3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Delete the project</button>
<span class="text-muted fs-12" role="status" data-docs-answer></span>
```

```js
await REDZ.ui.confirm({
  title: 'Delete the project Riverside tower?',
  note: {tone: 'danger', text: 'This cannot be undone.'},
  sections: [
    {title: 'Will be deleted:', items: ['128 tasks', '342 files', '1,204 log entries']},
    {title: 'Kept:', items: ['The audit history']},
  ],
  ok: 'Delete', tone: 'danger', phrase: 'Riverside tower',
});
```

### A question that waits for the server

With `run`, the confirming button carries the answer out before the dialog closes: `run({choice, phrase, signal})` answers a promise. Meanwhile the button is busy, the other buttons are unavailable, the body is inert, and `Esc` and a click outside are held. Resolved, the dialog closes and answers; refused with words - an `Error`'s message or a string -, a danger alert with them stands right above the footer, said at once, and the buttons wake with the focus still on the confirming one, for another try. A dialog closed meanwhile by code aborts the `signal`, and a refusal that comes after it is a danger toast. To leave the page on success, go there inside `run` and leave its promise pending: the button stays busy. `choice: {label, items: [{value, text, hint}], value}` puts radios above the phrase, and the answer is then the chosen value - a string - or `false`.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="confirm-run"><i class="bi bi-pause-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Pause the agent</button>
<span class="text-muted fs-12" role="status" data-docs-answer></span>
```

```js
const how = await REDZ.ui.confirm({
  title: 'Pause the agent on Boat A?',
  choice: {label: 'For how long', items: [{value: 'hour', text: 'One hour'}, {value: 'day', text: 'Until tomorrow'}], value: 'hour'},
  ok: 'Pause',
  run: ({choice, signal}) => fetch('/agents/a/pause', {method: 'POST', body: choice, signal})
    .then((answer) => answer.ok || answer.text().then((words) => Promise.reject(new Error(words)))),
}); // 'hour', 'day', or false
```

A third answer, `alt: {text, tone, value}`, stands at the footer's start - Discard, outlined in its tone, beside Stay and Save at the end - and answers its `value`, a string: compare it, never take it as true. The focus starts on Cancel; `focus: 'ok'` or `'alt'` starts it there, where the confirming answer is the safe one - Save -, never for an answer that destroys. In a dialog narrower than 368 px a footer of three buttons stacks them full width, the confirming one on top.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="confirm-alt"><i class="bi bi-box-arrow-right" aria-hidden="true"></i>Leave the price list</button>
<span class="text-muted fs-12" role="status" data-docs-answer></span>
```

A dialog of the page's own waits the same way: a `<form method="dialog">` inside it fires the cancelable `redz:save` on its submit, with `{form, data, submitter, signal}` - `data` the form's `FormData` with the pressed button's value. The page cancels it and answers with a promise by `event.detail.respondWith`; left alone, the form closes the dialog as the browser does. Marks on the fields stay the page's.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="dialog-wait-form-panel" command="show-modal"><i class="bi bi-tools" aria-hidden="true"></i>Take a boat out of service</button>
<dialog class="dialog dialog-sm" id="dialog-wait-form-panel" aria-labelledby="dialog-wait-form-title">
	<form method="dialog" data-docs-dialog-save>
		<div class="dialog-header"><h2 class="dialog-title" id="dialog-wait-form-title">Boat B out of service</h2></div>
		<div class="dialog-body vstack gap-12">
			<div class="vstack gap-4"><label class="form-label" for="dialog-wait-form-reason">Why</label><input class="form-control" id="dialog-wait-form-reason" name="reason" autocomplete="off"></div>
		</div>
		<div class="dialog-footer">
			<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="dialog-wait-form-panel" command="close">Cancel</button>
			<button class="btn btn-primary" value="save">Take out</button>
		</div>
	</form>
</dialog>
```

### A question for one value

`await REDZ.ui.prompt({title, text, label, value, placeholder, type, inputmode, pattern, required, ok, cancel, tone})` asks for one value in a modal dialog and answers it, or `null` for Cancel and `Esc`. The field takes the focus with its text selected; `Enter` answers once the field is valid - `required`, `pattern` and `type` are held by the browser's own checks. The field is labelled by `label`, or the title; the buttons' words come from the caller or the page's texts.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="prompt"><i class="bi bi-pencil" aria-hidden="true"></i>Rename the folder</button>
<span class="text-muted fs-12" role="status" data-docs-answer></span>
```

```js
const name = await REDZ.ui.prompt({title: 'Rename the folder', label: 'Name', value: 'Tours 2026', required: true, ok: 'Rename'});
if (name !== null) {
  // send it
}
```

### On a phone and full screen

On any window a long dialog keeps its header and its footer in view: only `dialog-body` scrolls between them. A `<form>` may hold all three - `<form method="dialog">` right inside the dialog, its submit buttons in the footer - and the body still scrolls alone. On a window narrower than 576 px a dialog fills the screen by itself, while `dialog-sm` and a confirmation stay a card in the middle. `dialog-fullscreen` fills the screen on any window.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="dialog-full-panel" command="show-modal"><i class="bi bi-arrows-fullscreen" aria-hidden="true"></i>Open full screen</button>
<dialog class="dialog dialog-fullscreen" id="dialog-full-panel" aria-labelledby="dialog-full-title">
	<div class="dialog-header">
		<h2 class="dialog-title" id="dialog-full-title">Route of the day</h2>
		<button class="btn-close" type="button" commandfor="dialog-full-panel" command="close" aria-label="Close"></button>
	</div>
	<div class="dialog-body"><p>Pick-up at the hotel at 7:30, the pier at 8:15, North Bay at 9:30; snorkeling, the emerald lake, lunch on the boat, back by 17:00.</p></div>
	<div class="dialog-footer"><button class="btn btn-primary" type="button" commandfor="dialog-full-panel" command="close">Done</button></div>
</dialog>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

- `Tab` stays inside an open dialog; `Esc` closes it; the focus goes back to the button that opened it.
- The dialog is named by its title through `aria-labelledby`. A question that must be answered is `role="alertdialog"` with its focus on the safe answer.
- The page behind does not scroll while a dialog is open, and keeps its width: the scrollbar's place stays.
- A notice raised while a dialog is open shows inside the dialog, since everything outside it is inert.
- Where the browser lacks invoker commands (below Chrome 135, Firefox 144, Safari 26.2) or `closedby` (below Chrome 134, Firefox 141, and in Safari), the library's script stands in.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/dialog.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/dialog.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-16`, `--redz-bg-raised`, `--redz-shadow-3`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-space-24`, `--redz-dialog-header-end`, `--redz-dialog-header-line`, `--redz-dialog-header-bg`, `--redz-fs-16`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-bg-page`, `--redz-ease`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modal` | `dialog` | rename | on a <dialog>, opened by commandfor + command="show-modal" |
| `modal-backdrop` | - | remove | the browser's ::backdrop |
| `modal-body` | `dialog-body` | rename |  |
| `modal-content` | - | remove | no wrappers: the <dialog> is the box |
| `modal-dialog` | - | remove | no wrappers: the <dialog> is the box |
| `modal-dialog-centered` | - | remove | a dialog is centered |
| `modal-dialog-scrollable` | - | remove | the dialog's body scrolls by itself |
| `modal-footer` | `dialog-footer` | rename |  |
| `modal-fullscreen` | `dialog-fullscreen` | rename |  |
| `modal-header` | `dialog-header` | rename |  |
| `modal-static` | - | remove | closedby="closerequest" |
| `modal-title` | `dialog-title` | rename |  |
| `data-bs-toggle="modal"` | `commandfor="ID" command="show-modal"` | trigger | on the button; the dialog is a <dialog id="ID"> |
| `data-bs-dismiss="modal"` | `commandfor="ID" command="close"` | trigger |  |
| `data-bs-backdrop="static"` | `closedby="closerequest"` | trigger | Esc closes it, a click outside does not |
| `data-bs-keyboard="false"` | `closedby="none"` | trigger | only its buttons close it |
| `bootstrap.Modal` | `dialog.showModal() and dialog.close()` | trigger |  |
| `show.bs.modal` | `toggle` | review | the dialog's toggle event, or code right after showModal() |
| `shown.bs.modal` | `toggle` | review | the dialog's toggle event, or code right after showModal() |
| `hide.bs.modal` | `cancel` | review | the dialog's cancel event (Esc); your buttons close it |
| `hidden.bs.modal` | `close` | rename | the dialog's close event; dialog.returnValue holds the closing button's value |

# Drawers

A modal panel at the end of the screen - or at its start with `drawer-start` - for filters, a record's details, a long form beside the list it belongs to. Bootstrap 5 calls it offcanvas; it is a `<dialog>` here.

## Examples

A drawer opens and closes like a dialog: `command="show-modal"` and `command="close"`. It slides in from its side - mirrored right to left - unless the person asks for less motion.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="drawer-filters-panel" command="show-modal"><i class="bi bi-funnel" aria-hidden="true"></i>Filters</button>
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="drawer-filters-start" command="show-modal"><i class="bi bi-layout-sidebar" aria-hidden="true"></i>From the start</button>
<dialog id="drawer-filters-panel" class="drawer" closedby="any" aria-labelledby="drawer-filters-panel-title">
	<div class="drawer-header">
		<h2 class="drawer-title" id="drawer-filters-panel-title">Filters</h2>
		<button class="btn-close" type="button" commandfor="drawer-filters-panel" command="close" aria-label="Close"></button>
	</div>
	<div class="drawer-body vstack gap-16">
		<fieldset class="vstack gap-8">
			<legend class="form-label">Status</legend>
			<label class="form-check"><input class="check" type="checkbox" name="published" checked>Published</label>
			<label class="form-check"><input class="check" type="checkbox" name="draft">Draft</label>
		</fieldset>
		<div class="form-floating">
			<select class="form-select" id="drawer-filters-section"><option>Any section</option><option>Marine</option><option>Land</option></select>
			<label for="drawer-filters-section">Section</label>
		</div>
		<div class="hstack gap-8 justify-content-end">
			<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="drawer-filters-panel" command="close">Reset</button>
			<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button" commandfor="drawer-filters-panel" command="close">Show 9</button>
		</div>
	</div>
</dialog>
<dialog id="drawer-filters-start" class="drawer drawer-start" closedby="any" aria-labelledby="drawer-filters-start-title">
	<div class="drawer-header">
		<h2 class="drawer-title" id="drawer-filters-start-title">Sections</h2>
		<button class="btn-close" type="button" commandfor="drawer-filters-start" command="close" aria-label="Close"></button>
	</div>
	<div class="drawer-body"><p>A drawer at the start edge: the left in English, the right in Arabic.</p></div>
</dialog>
```

A product tints the head of every drawer with `--redz-drawer-header-bg`.

### Wide

`drawer-lg` is 38rem (608 px) wide instead of 28rem, for a record's details with a table or a form of two columns; on a narrower window it takes the window less a margin, as every drawer does.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="drawer-lg-panel" command="show-modal"><i class="bi bi-receipt" aria-hidden="true"></i>Booking details</button>
<dialog id="drawer-lg-panel" class="drawer drawer-lg" closedby="any" aria-labelledby="drawer-lg-panel-title">
	<div class="drawer-header">
		<h2 class="drawer-title" id="drawer-lg-panel-title">Booking 2026-0418</h2>
		<button class="btn-close" type="button" commandfor="drawer-lg-panel" command="close" aria-label="Close"></button>
	</div>
	<div class="drawer-body"><p>North Bay by speedboat, 4 guests, 12 November 2026. Paid in full by card.</p></div>
</dialog>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

- Everything said of [dialogs](dialog.md) holds: the focus moves in and back, `Tab` stays inside, `Esc` closes.
- A drawer is a region: the width prefixes inside it measure the drawer, 28 rem wide at most.
- The drawer's body scrolls by itself; its header stays.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/drawer.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/drawer.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-bg-raised`, `--redz-shadow-3`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-drawer-header-bg`, `--redz-fs-16`, `--redz-ease`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `offcanvas` | `drawer` | rename | on a <dialog>, opened by command="show-modal" |
| `offcanvas-backdrop` | - | remove | the browser's ::backdrop |
| `offcanvas-body` | `drawer-body` | rename |  |
| `offcanvas-bottom` | - | missing |  |
| `offcanvas-end` | `drawer` | rename | on a <dialog>, opened by command="show-modal" |
| `offcanvas-header` | `drawer-header` | rename |  |
| `offcanvas-start` | `drawer drawer-start` | rename |  |
| `offcanvas-title` | `drawer-title` | rename |  |
| `offcanvas-top` | - | missing |  |
| `data-bs-toggle="offcanvas"` | `commandfor="ID" command="show-modal"` | trigger | the drawer is a <dialog id="ID"> |
| `data-bs-dismiss="offcanvas"` | `commandfor="ID" command="close"` | trigger |  |
| `bootstrap.Offcanvas` | `dialog.showModal() and dialog.close()` | trigger |  |

# Popovers

A small panel that opens beside its button and holds more than a label: a title, a few lines of text, a link. A click outside or `Esc` closes it; the page under it stays usable.

## Examples

`popover` on the panel, `popover-header` on its title, `popover-body` on its text. The button opens it with `commandfor` and `command="toggle-popover"`; the panel stands below the button, its start edge on the button's, and turns above or across where there is no room.

```html
<button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" commandfor="popover-titled-panel" command="toggle-popover">Park fee</button>
<div id="popover-titled-panel" class="popover" popover role="dialog" aria-labelledby="popover-titled-title">
	<div class="popover-header" id="popover-titled-title">North Bay marine park</div>
	<div class="popover-body">The fee is paid in cash at the pier and is not part of the tour price. <a href="#popover-titled">The park rules</a></div>
</div>
```

### Only a body

Without a title the panel is its text alone.

```html
<button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" commandfor="popover-body-panel" command="toggle-popover">Pickup time</button>
<div id="popover-body-panel" class="popover" popover>
	<div class="popover-body">The driver comes 15 minutes before the time on the voucher.</div>
</div>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The panel comes right after its button in the page, so a screen reader reads it there and `Tab` from the button moves into it. Opening it moves no focus; `Esc` closes it and brings focus back to the button.
- The button says whether the panel is open: the browsers set `aria-expanded` for a button with `commandfor`, and `js/commands.js` sets it in Firefox, which does not.
- A panel with a title and a link or a field in it is `role="dialog"`, named by its title in `aria-labelledby`. A panel of words only has no role.
- Nothing that must be read to use the screen lives only in a popover; a choice that needs an answer is a [dialog](dialog.md).
- `js/menu-place.js` keeps the panel beside its button where an engine cannot anchor it.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/popover.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/popover.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-bg-raised`, `--redz-shadow-2`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-fs-14`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-text-muted`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bs-popover-auto` | - | remove | no arrow: anchor positioning places and flips the panel |
| `bs-popover-bottom` | - | remove | no arrow: anchor positioning places and flips the panel |
| `bs-popover-end` | - | remove | no arrow: anchor positioning places and flips the panel |
| `bs-popover-start` | - | remove | no arrow: anchor positioning places and flips the panel |
| `bs-popover-top` | - | remove | no arrow: anchor positioning places and flips the panel |
| `popover-arrow` | - | remove | no arrow: anchor positioning places and flips the panel |
| `data-bs-toggle="popover"` | `commandfor="ID" command="toggle-popover"` | trigger | the panel is a <div id="ID" class="popover" popover> right after the button |
| `bootstrap.Popover` | `panel.showPopover(), panel.hidePopover(), panel.togglePopover()` | trigger |  |

# Tooltips

A short dark label beside a control. A small button opens it as a toggletip, which a click outside or `Esc` closes; or an element's own title shows it on hover and focus.

## Examples

The tooltip is a `popover` opened by its button's command. It sits above the button and turns below when there is no room - `js/menu-place.js` keeps it beside its button where an engine cannot.

```html
<span class="hstack gap-4">Partner license
	<button class="btn btn-icon btn-xs btn-text" type="button" commandfor="tooltip-why-tip" command="toggle-popover" aria-label="What is a partner license" aria-describedby="tooltip-why-tip"><i class="bi bi-question-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</span>
<div id="tooltip-why-tip" class="tooltip" popover role="tooltip">A partner can hide the brand and set their own help link.</div>
```

### From a title

Inside an element with `data-tooltips` - `<html>` for the whole page - an element's own `title` shows as this tooltip: after a short hover by a mouse, at once when the keyboard's focus lands on it, but not when the focus comes back from a closed menu or dialog, where the person has just been. It says why a control cannot run, what an icon button does, what a dot stands for. No markup but the title.

```html
<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" title="Duplicate"><i class="bi bi-copy" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
<button class="btn" type="button" aria-disabled="true" title="Publish needs a price for every season">Publish</button>
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="dot dot-warning" title="2 translations are outdated"></span>North Bay</span>
```

`data-tooltip-delay` on that element, or on any element around the title, sets the wait after a hover in milliseconds, 400 unless it says otherwise; `0` shows the tooltip as soon as the pointer is on it.

```html
<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" title="Duplicate"><i class="bi bi-copy" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" title="Delete"><i class="bi bi-trash3" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
```

On a folded side navigation a link's tooltip stands beside it, at the end of the rail, so it covers no other icon; the rail names its links from their words by itself.

A click or a tap on a control that cannot run - `aria-disabled="true"` with a title, as Publish above - shows its title for three seconds and says it politely, so the person learns why without a mouse.

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The button is named after its question; the tooltip's words answer it. Nothing that must be read to use the screen lives only in a tooltip.
- The button names its tooltip in `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader says the answer with the question, closed or open - opening a popover says nothing of its words.
- A tooltip from a title is the title itself to a screen reader: the element keeps its title on focus, and the tooltip is hidden from assistive technology. While a mouse rests on the element the title is held back, so the browser does not show its own as well; an icon button named only by its title keeps that name meanwhile.
- It stays while the pointer rests on it, hides on `Esc` without moving the focus, and never opens for a touch, which has no hover: on a phone, what a title says must be on the screen too.
- The label is the page's text color on the page color reversed: 4.5:1 in both themes, an outline in forced colors.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/tooltip.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/tooltip.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-radius-6`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-fs-12`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bs-tooltip-auto` | - | remove | the tooltip is one element |
| `bs-tooltip-bottom` | - | remove | the tooltip is one element |
| `bs-tooltip-end` | - | remove | the tooltip is one element |
| `bs-tooltip-start` | - | remove | the tooltip is one element |
| `bs-tooltip-top` | - | remove | the tooltip is one element |
| `tooltip-arrow` | - | remove | the tooltip is one element |
| `tooltip-inner` | - | remove | the tooltip is one element |
| `data-bs-toggle="tooltip"` | `data-tooltips` | review | keep the title: data-tooltips on <html> or a container shows every title inside as a tooltip; a toggletip for longer words |
| `data-bs-title` | `title` | rename | the element's own title, inside data-tooltips |
| `bootstrap.Tooltip` | - | remove | data-tooltips on <html> or a container shows the titles inside |

# Image viewer

A picture opened large over the page: a link to the full image with `data-zoom`, and the library does the rest - one modal dialog it makes when first needed, which opens above an open dialog too.

## Examples

An `a` with `data-zoom` whose `href` is the full image, around its thumbnail. Links with the same word in `data-zoom` make a set, in the page's order: the arrow keys - mirrored right to left - and the viewer's buttons step through it, wrapping, and the count says where it is. The caption is the link's `title`, or its image's `alt`. `Escape`, × and a click beside the image close it, and the focus goes back to the link; a click with a modifier key opens the image as a link does.

```html
<div class="grid cols-3 gap-12">
	<a href="img/lagoon.svg" data-zoom="tour" title="The lagoon at North Bay"><img class="w-100 ratio-16x9 rounded" src="img/lagoon.svg" alt="A lagoon under green hills"></a>
	<a href="img/pier.svg" data-zoom="tour" title="The pier at sunset"><img class="w-100 ratio-16x9 rounded" src="img/pier.svg" alt="A wooden pier over the sea"></a>
	<a href="img/cliffs.svg" data-zoom="tour"><img class="w-100 ratio-16x9 rounded" src="img/cliffs.svg" alt="Cliffs above a bay with a boat"></a>
</div>
```

### Above a dialog

The viewer is in the top layer: opened from a dialog, it covers the dialog, and closing it leaves the dialog as it was, the focus back on the link. A link with an empty `data-zoom` opens its image alone.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="viewer-dialog-room" command="show-modal">The room</button>
<dialog class="dialog" id="viewer-dialog-room" aria-labelledby="viewer-dialog-room-title" closedby="any">
	<div class="dialog-header">
		<h2 class="dialog-title" id="viewer-dialog-room-title">Sea view, room 12</h2>
		<button class="btn btn-icon btn-text" type="button" commandfor="viewer-dialog-room" command="close" aria-label="Close"><i class="bi bi-x-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	</div>
	<div class="dialog-body vstack gap-12">
		<a href="img/pier.svg" data-zoom title="The pier below the room"><img class="w-100 ratio-16x9 rounded" src="img/pier.svg" alt="A wooden pier over the sea"></a>
		<p>Two guests, a terrace, the pier a minute away.</p>
	</div>
</dialog>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The viewer is a modal dialog named by its caption: the focus starts on ×, `Tab` stays inside it, and `Escape` closes it.
- In a set, `←` and `→` step - mirrored right to left -, and the caption with the count is said politely when it changes.
- The image keeps the thumbnail's `alt`; a link whose image has none is named by its `title`.

## Texts

The library has no words of its own; it reads these from the page's island `#redz-ui-text`.

| Key | For | In English |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `close` | The × button | Close |
| `viewer.prev`, `viewer.next` | The buttons that step through a set | Previous image, Next image |
| `viewer.count` | Where the image is in its set; `{position}` and `{count}` | {position} of {count} |

## Tokens

From [`css/components/viewer.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/viewer.css). It declares `--redz-btn-bg`, `--redz-btn-fg`, `--redz-btn-hover` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-64`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-space-24`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-fs-14`.

# Alerts

A message that stays on the page beside what it is about: a check passed, a suggestion, a warning before an action. A message that comes and goes is a [toast](toast.md).

## Examples

An icon, then the words in a `<div>`. The plain `alert` is neutral; the tones follow Bootstrap's.

```html
<div class="alert"><i class="bi bi-info-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i><div>The changes apply to the next booking.</div></div>
<div class="alert alert-primary"><i class="bi bi-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i><div>A shorter title would fit the search results.</div></div>
<div class="alert alert-success"><i class="bi bi-check-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i><div>White text on it: 5.6:1, AA in both themes.</div></div>
<div class="alert alert-warning"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-triangle" aria-hidden="true"></i><div>The Thai translation is older than the English.</div></div>
<div class="alert alert-danger"><i class="bi bi-x-octagon" aria-hidden="true"></i><div>The theme template raised a PHP warning; the page did not rebuild.</div></div>
<div class="alert alert-info"><i class="bi bi-robot" aria-hidden="true"></i><div>Translated by machine; a person has not read it yet.</div></div>
```

### With a title and actions

```html
<div class="alert alert-primary align-items-start" role="region" aria-label="AI suggestion">
	<i class="bi bi-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<div class="vstack gap-8">
		<strong>A shorter title</strong>
		<p>“North Bay by speedboat” fits the 60 characters search results show.</p>
		<div class="hstack gap-8"><button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" type="button">Use it</button><button class="btn btn-sm btn-text" type="button">Dismiss</button></div>
	</div>
</div>
```

### Filled in place

An alert whose words come after an action - a refused sign-in, a wrong code - is on the page from the start, empty, as `role="alert"`, and the page fills it. Empty - no child, not even a space - it takes no room; filled, it shows, and a screen reader says its words. An alert shown from `hidden` at the moment it is filled is not always heard: VoiceOver on macOS 15 can miss it.

```html
<div class="alert alert-danger" id="alert-fill-words" role="alert"></div>
<div class="hstack gap-8"><button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" data-docs-run="alert-fill">Fill the alert</button></div>
```

`REDZ.ui.alert(box, {tone, text})` does it from code without a live role on the box: it gives the box the class of the tone, its icon and the words - text, never HTML - and says them through the page's hidden status, politely, at once for `danger`; the same words again are said again. `REDZ.ui.alert(box, null)` empties the box. Given a promise, it shows the page's text `busy` with a spinner once the promise waits past 400 ms, then the `{tone, text}` the promise answers - nothing empties the box - or the rejection's message as `danger`, and answers the promise. A later call wins.

```html
<div class="alert" id="alert-code-box"></div>
<div class="hstack flex-wrap gap-8">
	<button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" data-docs-run="alert-code-info">Code sent</button>
	<button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" data-docs-run="alert-code-wait">Make the dump</button>
	<button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" data-docs-run="alert-code-clear">Empty it</button>
</div>
```

```js
const box = document.getElementById('sign-in-words');
REDZ.ui.alert(box, {tone: 'info', text: 'A code went to your phone. A new one in 60 s.'});
REDZ.ui.alert(box, fetch('/dump', {method: 'POST'}).then((answer) => answer.json())
  .then(({file, size}) => ({tone: 'success', text: 'Done: ' + file + ' (' + size + ')'})));
REDZ.ui.alert(box, null);
```

### Sizes

`alert-sm` for a note inside a card or a form, `alert-lg` for the one message a page is about.

```html
<div class="alert alert-info alert-sm"><i class="bi bi-info-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i><div>Prices include the park fee.</div></div>
<div class="alert alert-info alert-lg"><i class="bi bi-info-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i><div>Prices include the park fee.</div></div>
```

### A title over its text

The words may be a `vstack`: it stays beside the icon however long its text.

```html
<div class="alert alert-warning"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-triangle" aria-hidden="true"></i><div class="vstack gap-4"><strong>The backup is two days old</strong><span>The nightly copy stopped on Tuesday, so today's changes are not in it yet. Run one by hand before the next update.</span></div></div>
```

## Accessibility

- An alert that is on the page from the start is plain content - no live region. One that appears after an action and must be heard goes in a live region, or is a toast.
- A suggestion with its own actions is a `region` named after what it is.
- The icon carries the tone in forced colors; the words carry the meaning.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/alert.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/alert.css). It declares `--redz-alert-bg`, `--redz-alert-icon` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-secondary-subtle`, `--redz-secondary-text`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-radius-8`, `--redz-fs-14`, `--redz-space-20`, `--redz-fs-16`, `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-primary-text`, `--redz-success-subtle`, `--redz-success-text`, `--redz-danger-subtle`, `--redz-danger-text`, `--redz-warning-subtle`, `--redz-warning-text`, `--redz-info-subtle`, `--redz-info-text`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alert-dark` | - | review | the plain alert, or a tone |
| `alert-dismissible` | - | review | a btn-close at the end, removed by your script |
| `alert-heading` | - | review | a strong title in the alert's div |
| `alert-light` | - | review | the plain alert, or a tone |
| `alert-link` | - | review | a plain link |
| `alert-secondary` | - | review | the plain alert, or a tone |
| `data-bs-dismiss="alert"` | - | review | remove the alert in your script |

# Toasts

A notice after an action - saved, failed, moved with a way to undo - shown by `REDZ.ui.toast()` in a stack at the corner of the screen and read aloud from a live region.

## Examples

Success and info leave after 8 seconds, unless the pointer or the focus rests on them. An error, and a notice with an action, stay until closed.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="toast-success">Saved</button>
<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="toast-info">Import started</button>
<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="toast-danger">Not saved</button>
<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="toast-action">With an action</button>
```

The call takes the words and the tone and answers a function that closes the toast:

```js
const close = REDZ.ui.toast({title: 'Moved to the archive', tone: 'info', action: {label: 'Undo', run: restore}});
```

### The stack

The page carries the stack from the start, so that screen readers know its live regions before anything is said in them: `role="status"` for notices, `role="alert"` for errors. Without one, the library adds it at load.

```html
<div class="toast-container"><div role="status"></div><div role="alert"></div></div>
```

### How a toast looks

```html
<div class="toast toast-success"><i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i><div class="toast-body"><strong>Saved</strong><div class="text-muted fs-12">North Bay · 3 pages rebuilt</div></div><button class="btn-close" type="button" aria-label="Close"></button></div>
<div class="toast toast-info"><i class="bi bi-info-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i><div class="toast-body"><strong>Import started</strong><div class="text-muted fs-12">You can leave this page.</div></div><button class="btn-close" type="button" aria-label="Close"></button></div>
<div class="toast toast-warning"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-triangle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i><div class="toast-body"><strong>Saved without the Thai text</strong></div><button class="btn-close" type="button" aria-label="Close"></button></div>
<div class="toast toast-danger"><i class="bi bi-x-octagon-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i><div class="toast-body"><strong>Not saved</strong><div class="text-muted fs-12">The connection was lost; try again.</div></div><button class="btn-close" type="button" aria-label="Close"></button></div>
<div class="toast toast-primary"><i class="bi bi-bell-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i><div class="toast-body"><strong>Moved to the archive</strong></div><button class="btn btn-sm" type="button">Undo</button><button class="btn-close" type="button" aria-label="Close"></button></div>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

- A toast never takes the focus; its close button and its action are in the tab order at the end of the page.
- While a modal dialog is open, toasts show inside it, since everything outside it is inert.
- The close button's name comes from the page's texts: `close` in the island `#redz-ui-text`.
- Nothing a person must act on lives only in a toast that leaves by itself.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/toast.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/toast.css). It declares `--redz-toast-mark` on its root, never on rows or items.
