It reads the theme's `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-text-faint`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-bg-raised`, `--redz-shadow-2`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-success`, `--redz-danger`, `--redz-warning`, `--redz-info`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `toast-header` | - | review | REDZ.ui.toast builds the toast from its title, text and tone |
| `data-bs-dismiss="toast"` | - | remove | REDZ.ui.toast adds its close button |
| `bootstrap.Toast` | `REDZ.ui.toast({title, text, tone})` | trigger |  |

# Spinners

A turning ring, 1 em across in the color of the text around it, for something small that is on its way. A button shows its own while busy; a region shows an overlay.

## Examples

The words beside the spinner say what is happening; the ring alone is hidden from assistive technology.

```html
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="spinner-border" aria-hidden="true"></span>Rebuilding 3 pages…</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8 text-primary fs-20"><span class="spinner-border" aria-hidden="true"></span>Larger, in the accent</span>
```

### A growing dot

`spinner-grow` is a dot that grows and fades in place of the ring, for a calmer sign in a line of text.

```html
<span class="hstack gap-8"><span class="spinner-grow" aria-hidden="true"></span>Checking the server…</span>
<span class="hstack gap-8 text-success"><span class="spinner-grow" aria-hidden="true"></span>Syncing the calendar</span>
```

## Accessibility

- A spinner turns at half the speed for people who ask for less motion and never stops - it is the sign that something is happening - and stays a ring or a dot in forced colors.
- Say the same in words, in a live region when it starts after an action.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/spinner.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/spinner.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

# Progress and meters

The browser's own `<progress>` for work under way and `<meter>` for a measure within known limits - a quota, a score. The value is an attribute, the browser announces it, and a progress without a value says the work has no known end.

## Examples

`progress` on a `<progress>` with `value` and `max`; the words of the value go beside the bar, `text-nowrap` so the bar gives way, and the label names it.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="progress-basic-upload">Uploading photos</label>
	<div class="hstack gap-12">
		<progress class="progress" id="progress-basic-upload" value="40" max="100">40 %</progress>
		<span class="text-muted fs-12 text-nowrap">40 %</span>
	</div>
</div>
<progress class="progress" aria-label="Rebuilding pages"></progress>
```

### Tones and sizes

`progress-{tone}` for the tones, `progress-sm` and `progress-lg` for the height; `progress-striped` lays stripes on the bar, `progress-animated` moves them while motion is allowed.

```html
<progress class="progress progress-success" value="75" max="100" aria-label="Published, 75 percent"></progress>
<progress class="progress progress-warning progress-sm" value="50" max="100" aria-label="Translated, 50 percent"></progress>
<progress class="progress progress-danger progress-lg" value="20" max="100" aria-label="Failed, 20 percent"></progress>
<progress class="progress progress-lg progress-striped progress-animated" value="60" max="100" aria-label="Deploying, 60 percent"></progress>
```

### Meters

`meter` on a `<meter>`: `low`, `high` and `optimum` divide the range, and the browser colours the value by the part it falls in - green in the good part, amber next to it, red in the far one.

```html
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="progress-meter-storage">Storage used</label>
	<div class="hstack gap-12">
		<meter class="meter" id="progress-meter-storage" value="3.1" min="0" max="10" low="7" high="9" optimum="0">3.1 of 10 GB</meter>
		<span class="text-muted fs-12 text-nowrap">3.1 of 10 GB</span>
	</div>
</div>
<meter class="meter" value="8" min="0" max="10" low="7" high="9" optimum="0" aria-label="Photos, 8 of 10 GB">8 of 10 GB</meter>
<meter class="meter" value="9.6" min="0" max="10" low="7" high="9" optimum="0" aria-label="Backups, 9.6 of 10 GB">9.6 of 10 GB</meter>
```

### A meter of several parts

`meter meter-stacked` on a `div role="meter"` shows the parts of one amount - the free, the paid, what goes over the limit - each a child with its `data-v`, its share of the whole scale, and `data-tone`; 2 px apart, the ends rounded. A part with `data-over`, past the limit, is hatched red, so it reads without its colour too. The meter's numbers and its words are the page's: `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemax`, an `aria-valuetext` that says the parts, and a legend of [dots](dot.md) beside it.

```html
<div class="vstack gap-8 max-w-480">
	<div class="hstack gap-8 fs-14"><span class="flex-grow-1" id="progress-stacked-title">Seats this month</span><span class="text-muted tabular-nums">130 of 120</span></div>
	<div class="meter meter-stacked" role="meter" aria-labelledby="progress-stacked-title" aria-valuenow="130" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="130" aria-valuetext="130 seats: 50 free, 70 paid, 10 over the limit">
		<span data-tone="success" data-v="0.385"></span>
		<span data-tone="primary" data-v="0.538"></span>
		<span data-over data-v="0.077"></span>
	</div>
	<ul class="hstack flex-wrap gap-12 fs-12 text-muted" aria-hidden="true">
		<li class="hstack gap-4"><span class="dot dot-success"></span>Free 50</li>
		<li class="hstack gap-4"><span class="dot dot-primary"></span>Paid 70</li>
		<li class="hstack gap-4"><span class="dot dot-danger"></span>Over 10</li>
	</ul>
</div>
```

### Hairlines

`progress-xs`, 3 px, and `meter-xs`, 2 px, sit under a row's words without fighting them: how far a job is between its runs, amber when it is late, and how often it succeeded, colored by the meter's own parts.

```html
<div class="vstack gap-4">
	<span>Nightly backup <span class="text-muted fs-12">next in 2 h</span></span>
	<progress class="progress progress-xs" value="70" max="100" aria-label="Nightly backup, 70 percent of its cycle"></progress>
	<meter class="meter meter-xs" value="0.98" min="0" max="1" low="0.8" high="0.95" optimum="1" aria-label="Nightly backup, 98 percent succeeded">98%</meter>
</div>
<div class="vstack gap-4">
	<span>Mail queue <span class="text-muted fs-12">late by 6 min</span></span>
	<progress class="progress progress-xs progress-warning" value="100" max="100" aria-label="Mail queue, late"></progress>
	<meter class="meter meter-xs" value="0.71" min="0" max="1" low="0.8" high="0.95" optimum="1" aria-label="Mail queue, 71 percent succeeded">71%</meter>
</div>
```

### Along the window's top

`REDZ.ui.progress(promise)` shows a thin bar along the top of the window while a request runs, and answers the promise: it comes after 150 ms, so a quick answer shows nothing, then stays at least 400 ms, so it never flickers; however many requests run at once, there is one bar. It is `progress-top`, in the top layer, and readers do not hear it - what waits says so itself, a [busy](busy.md) region or button. For people who ask for less motion it runs slower, like every bar without a value, and never stops: a bar that stands still looks like a page that hangs.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="progress"><i class="bi bi-cloud-arrow-down" aria-hidden="true"></i>Load for 2 seconds</button>
```

```js
const rows = await REDZ.ui.progress(fetch('/bookings?page=2').then((answer) => answer.json()));
```

A product sets how much it shows in its tokens: `--redz-progress-top-size`, `--redz-progress-top-track` and `--redz-progress-top-glow`, a `box-shadow`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

- Name every bar: a `<label for>`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The browser announces the value as a percentage of `max`; the words beside the bar are for the eye.
- Colour is not the message: a meter in the red part also says so in words where it matters.
- A screen reader does not follow a bar as it fills: say the end of a long task in a notice, by `REDZ.ui.toast`.
- In forced colours the bar takes the system's highlight; right to left it fills from the right.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/progress.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/progress.css). It declares `--redz-part`, `--redz-track` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-secondary`, `--redz-success`, `--redz-danger`, `--redz-warning`, `--redz-info`, `--redz-danger-contrast`, `--redz-progress-top-track`, `--redz-progress-top-size`, `--redz-progress-top-glow`, `--redz-motion`, `--redz-ease`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `progress` | `progress` | review | on a <progress value="40" max="100"> itself, not around a progress-bar with a width; a tone is progress-success and the like, not bg-* on the bar |
| `progress-bar` | - | remove | the browser draws the bar from value |
| `progress-bar-animated` | `progress-animated` | rename | it moves only while motion is allowed |
| `progress-bar-striped` | `progress-striped` | rename |  |
| `progress-stacked` | - | review | not planned: one <progress> a value |

# Busy

`REDZ.ui.busy(element, promise)` marks a button or a region busy until the promise settles: a button shows a spinner and ignores clicks, a region turns inert under an overlay, a switch the person flipped goes back on a refusal.

## Examples

A region - a card, its body, a dialog's or a drawer's body, any `region` - keeps its old content under a dimmed overlay while the new comes. The overlay shows only after 400 ms, so a quick answer does not flash; once shown it stays at least 400 ms. A focus the region dropped comes back to the same element, to the element with its id in the new content, or to the region.

```html
<section class="card" id="busy-region-card" aria-labelledby="busy-region-title">
	<div class="card-header"><h2 id="busy-region-title">Bookings this week</h2><button class="btn btn-sm ms-auto" type="button" data-docs-run="busy-region" aria-controls="busy-region-card"><i class="bi bi-arrow-repeat" aria-hidden="true"></i>Reload for 2 seconds</button></div>
	<div class="card-body vstack gap-8">
		<p class="fs-24 fw-600 tabular-nums">128</p>
		<p class="text-muted">bookings, 312,400 THB</p>
	</div>
</section>
```

```js
await REDZ.ui.busy(card, fetch(url).then((answer) => answer.text()).then((html) => { body.innerHTML = html; }));
```

`data-busy` on the region gives the words that show under its spinner and are said instead of the page's text `busy`: "Reading the file list…".

```html
<section class="card" id="busy-region-words-card" aria-labelledby="busy-region-words-title" data-busy="Preparing the download…">
	<div class="card-header"><h2 id="busy-region-words-title">Backup files</h2><button class="btn btn-sm ms-auto" type="button" data-docs-run="busy-region" aria-controls="busy-region-words-card"><i class="bi bi-download" aria-hidden="true"></i>Prepare for 2 seconds</button></div>
	<div class="card-body vstack gap-8">
		<p>base-2026-11-08.sql · 2.4 MB</p>
		<p>files-2026-11-08.tar · 380 MB</p>
	</div>
</section>
```

### The page's own picture

A `busy-art` child of the region shows in place of the spinner: any picture, such as an inline SVG of any size with its own motion. It is hidden until the region is busy, then stands over the overlay after the same 400 ms, the region's words under it. Its colors and its motion are the page's: written inline, it takes the theme's colors and the page's CSS in every engine, while an SVG file shown as an image stands still in Safari. Its motion slows down for people who ask for less motion and never stops, as every busy mark of the library does. In the main column, which may be far taller than the window, it goes first, and there it stays in the middle of what shows; a main column without one is given the library's ring the same way.

```html
<section class="card" id="busy-art-card" aria-labelledby="busy-art-title">
	<div class="busy-art" aria-hidden="true"><span class="docs-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span></div>
	<div class="card-header"><h2 id="busy-art-title">Trips today</h2><button class="btn btn-sm ms-auto" type="button" data-docs-run="busy-region" aria-controls="busy-art-card"><i class="bi bi-arrow-repeat" aria-hidden="true"></i>Reload for 2 seconds</button></div>
	<div class="card-body vstack gap-8">
		<p class="fs-24 fw-600 tabular-nums">14</p>
		<p class="text-muted">boats out, 3 coming back</p>
	</div>
</section>
```

The example's picture is three dots drawn by the page's CSS; an inline SVG stands there the same way, its parts in the theme's colors:

```html
<div class="busy-art" aria-hidden="true">
  <svg class="dots" viewBox="0 0 60 20" width="96" height="32"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="7"/><circle cx="30" cy="10" r="7"/><circle cx="50" cy="10" r="7"/></svg>
</div>

.dots circle { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center; fill: var(--redz-primary); animation: hop 0.9s ease-in-out infinite; }
.dots circle:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 0.15s; }
.dots circle:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 0.3s; }
@keyframes hop { 0%, 100% { scale: 0.55; opacity: 0.45; } 50% { scale: 1; opacity: 1; } }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .dots circle { animation-duration: 2.4s; } }
@media (forced-colors: active) { .dots circle { fill: CanvasText; } }
```

### A button

The button keeps its focus, ignores clicks until the promise settles and shows a spinner: in place of its leading icon, or over its words when it has none - then it keeps its size too. `data-busy` on the button gives the words it shows while it waits, said politely once the wait passes 400 ms; set it again before each call when the wait has steps.

```html
<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button" data-docs-run="busy-button">Save for 2 seconds</button>
<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button" data-busy="Signing in…" data-docs-run="busy-button"><i class="bi bi-box-arrow-in-right" aria-hidden="true"></i>Sign in for 2 seconds</button>
```

An item of a menu - Delete in a row's menu - is busy with the button that opened the menu: the menu closes as the item is pressed, and the opener shows the spinner in its place and swallows its clicks until the promise settles. In a menu inside a menu, the outermost opener does.

```html
<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" commandfor="busy-menu-list" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-label="Actions: Boat A"><i class="bi bi-three-dots" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
<div class="menu" id="busy-menu-list" popover role="menu" aria-label="Actions: Boat A">
	<button class="menu-item" type="button" role="menuitem" data-docs-run="busy-menu-item" commandfor="busy-menu-list" command="hide-popover"><i class="bi bi-arrow-repeat" aria-hidden="true"></i>Check now</button>
</div>
```

### A check, a radio or a switch

A check, a radio or a switch that applies at once is held while the page saves the person's flip: `busy(control, promise)` from its `change` marks it `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, so it keeps its focus and its look and swallows clicks and keys - a radio's whole group does. After 400 ms its mark, or a switch's knob, turns into a spinning ring, and the words of its `data-busy` or the page's text `busy` are said politely. Resolved, the flip stays. Refused, it goes back without a `change` - a radio to the choice its group held before -, and the refusal's words, the `message` of an `Error` or of an object, or a string, show in a danger toast, said at once; an empty refusal or an `AbortError` says nothing.

`data-apply` on the control does it without a listener of its own: its `change` fires the cancelable `redz:apply` with `{checked, value, signal}`, and the page answers with `event.detail.respondWith(promise)`. Left alone, or cancelled without an answer, the flip just stands. A newer `redz:apply` of the same control or radio group aborts the last one's `signal`. A tracked form leaves a `data-apply` control out, as it is saved at once; a control in a tracked form that `busy()` holds without it needs `data-track="off"`. Here the page answers in 1.5 seconds and refuses alerts for Boat C, which has no phone on board.

```html
<table class="table" aria-label="Alerts by boat">
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Boat</th><th scope="col">Alerts</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr><td>Boat A</td><td><input class="switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" id="busy-check-a" aria-label="Alerts for Boat A" data-apply checked></td></tr>
		<tr><td>Boat B</td><td><input class="switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" id="busy-check-b" aria-label="Alerts for Boat B" data-apply></td></tr>
		<tr><td>Boat C</td><td><input class="switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" id="busy-check-c" aria-label="Alerts for Boat C" data-apply data-busy="Turning the alerts on"></td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

```js
document.addEventListener('redz:apply', (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const {checked, signal} = event.detail;
  event.detail.respondWith(fetch(url, {method: 'POST', body: checked ? '1' : '0', signal}).then((answer) => {
    if (!answer.ok) throw new Error('The alerts were not changed.');
  }));
});
```

From code, in the control's own `change` - here the page refuses the hotel, outside the pickup area:

```html
<fieldset class="vstack gap-8" id="busy-check-pickup">
	<legend class="form-label">Pickup</legend>
	<label class="form-check"><input class="radio" type="radio" name="busy-pickup" value="pier" checked> At the pier</label>
	<label class="form-check"><input class="radio" type="radio" name="busy-pickup" value="hotel"> At the hotel</label>
	<label class="form-check"><input class="radio" type="radio" name="busy-pickup" value="none"> No pickup</label>
</fieldset>
```

```js
radio.addEventListener('change', () => REDZ.ui.busy(radio, save(radio.value)).catch(() => {}));
```

Any other element - a cell whose check runs, a line - shows a small ring after 400 ms and, to a screen reader, the words of its `data-busy` or the page's text `busy`, saying nothing aloud: many such checks at once would be noise.

```html
<table class="table" aria-label="Agents">
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Agent</th><th scope="col">State</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody><tr><td>Boat A</td><td id="busy-cell-state" data-busy="Checking">Running</td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<div><button class="btn btn-sm" type="button" data-docs-run="busy-cell"><i class="bi bi-arrow-repeat" aria-hidden="true"></i>Check for 2 seconds</button></div>
```

A button that starts a [cooldown](btn.md#btn-cooldown) while it waits - "Send the code again" with `data-cooldown` set as the code goes - stays disabled until the count ends: the cooldown holds `aria-disabled` while it counts, `busy()` leaves it alone, and the state from before both comes back when the last of them ends.

## States

What `busy()` sets, written by hand - the overlay appears 400 ms after the page draws it.

## Accessibility

- Screen readers mostly ignore `aria-busy`, and on a live region it breaks the region in some of them: here it is a styling hook, and `busy()` refuses a live region in the console.
- The region is `inert` while busy: no focus, no clicks, out of the accessibility tree. When the overlay shows, one polite message says so - the page's text `busy`, “Loading…”.
- A busy check, radio or switch keeps its focus and its state, so a screen reader hears the flip it made; its ring is not read, its words are said politely after 400 ms and a refusal at once.
- For a first load, where there is nothing to cover yet, use [placeholders](placeholder.md).

## Tokens

From [`css/components/busy.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/busy.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-bg`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-app-banner-height`, `--redz-space-2`, `--redz-radius-6`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-fs-14`, `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-text-muted`.

# Save bar

A tracked form remembers what it held and marks what changed since; the bar at the foot of the page says what is not saved yet, saves it or discards it, and asks before the changes are left. It sticks to the bottom of the screen while the form is longer than the screen.

## Examples

`data-track` on a form tracks it; its value names the form in the bar's words. Change a field - its mark appears, so does a dot on the tab that holds it - then save with the bar or `Control` `S`, or discard and undo. Here the page answers in 700 ms and refuses an adult price below the child price; with "A conflict" chosen, it says another person changed the name meanwhile.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-8"><label class="form-label mb-0" for="save-bar-answer">The page answers</label><select class="form-select w-auto" id="save-bar-answer"><option value="saved">Saved</option><option value="conflict">A conflict</option></select></div>
<form class="card" id="save-bar-form" data-track="Excursion" data-docs-track>
	<div class="nav nav-underline" role="tablist" aria-label="Excursion">
		<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="save-bar-tab-1" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="save-bar-pane-1">Details</button>
		<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="save-bar-tab-2" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="save-bar-pane-2">Prices</button>
	</div>
	<div class="card-body vstack gap-16" id="save-bar-pane-1" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="save-bar-tab-1" tabindex="0">
		<div class="form-field">
			<div class="form-floating">
				<input class="form-control" id="save-bar-name" name="name" value="Sunset cruise" placeholder="Name">
				<label for="save-bar-name">Name</label>
			</div>
		</div>
		<fieldset class="vstack gap-8">
			<legend class="form-label">Departure</legend>
			<label class="form-check"><input class="radio" type="radio" name="departure" value="morning">Morning, 8:30</label>
			<label class="form-check"><input class="radio" type="radio" name="departure" value="sunset" checked>Sunset, 16:30</label>
		</fieldset>
		<label class="form-check"><input class="switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" name="shown" value="1" checked>Shown on the site</label>
		<div class="form-field">
			<div class="form-floating">
				<button class="form-select combobox-toggle" type="button" id="save-bar-guide-face" role="combobox" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false" commandfor="save-bar-guide-panel" command="toggle-popover"><span class="combobox-value" data-placeholder="Choose a language…">Thai</span></button>
				<label for="save-bar-guide-face">Guide speaks</label>
			</div>
			<div class="menu combobox-menu" id="save-bar-guide-panel" popover role="dialog" aria-label="Guide speaks">
				<div class="combobox-search">
					<i class="bi bi-search" aria-hidden="true"></i>
					<input class="form-control form-control-sm combobox-search-input" type="search" id="save-bar-guide-search" role="combobox" aria-controls="save-bar-guide-list" aria-expanded="true" aria-autocomplete="list" aria-label="Find a language" placeholder="Find a language" autocomplete="off" autofocus>
				</div>
				<div class="combobox-list" id="save-bar-guide-list" role="listbox" aria-label="Languages" data-name="guide">
					<div class="menu-item" role="option" id="save-bar-guide-en" data-value="en" aria-selected="false">English</div>
					<div class="menu-item" role="option" id="save-bar-guide-th" data-value="th" aria-selected="true">Thai</div>
					<div class="menu-item" role="option" id="save-bar-guide-de" data-value="de" aria-selected="false">German</div>
				</div>
				<p class="combobox-no-results" hidden>Nothing found</p>
				<input type="hidden" name="guide" value="th" data-label="Thai">
			</div>
		</div>
	</div>
	<div class="card-body vstack gap-16" id="save-bar-pane-2" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="save-bar-tab-2" tabindex="0" hidden>
		<div class="form-field">
			<label class="form-label" for="save-bar-adult">Adult price</label>
			<div class="input-group"><input class="form-control tabular-nums" id="save-bar-adult" name="adult" type="number" value="2500" min="0" step="100" aria-describedby="save-bar-adult-hint"><span class="input-group-text">THB</span></div>
			<div class="form-text" id="save-bar-adult-hint">Adults pay at least the child price.</div>
		</div>
		<div class="form-field">
			<label class="form-label" for="save-bar-child">Child price</label>
			<div class="input-group"><input class="form-control tabular-nums" id="save-bar-child" name="child" type="number" value="1900" min="0" step="100"><span class="input-group-text">THB</span></div>
		</div>
		<div class="form-field">
			<label class="form-label" for="save-bar-key">Payment key</label>
			<div class="input-group">
				<input class="form-control" id="save-bar-key" name="key" type="password" autocomplete="off" placeholder="Stored - type to replace" data-secret aria-describedby="save-bar-key-hint">
				<button class="btn" type="button" command="--clear" commandfor="save-bar-key" aria-pressed="false" data-clear="key_clear">Clear</button>
			</div>
			<div class="form-text" id="save-bar-key-hint">Left empty, the stored key stays.</div>
		</div>
	</div>
</form>
<div class="save-bar" data-track hidden></div>
```

### The bar's states

At rest the bar says everything is saved; with unsaved changes it names them. The script sets `data-state` - `clean`, `dirty`, `saving`, `saved`, `error` - and a bar written by hand takes `save-bar-dirty` for the second.

```html
<div class="save-bar" role="region" aria-label="Changes">
	<i class="bi bi-check2-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<span class="save-bar-text">All changes saved</span>
</div>
<div class="save-bar save-bar-dirty" role="region" aria-label="Unsaved changes">
	<i class="bi bi-pencil" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<span class="save-bar-text">2 unsaved changes: product name, accent color</span>
	<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button">Discard</button>
	<button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" type="button"><i class="bi bi-floppy" aria-hidden="true"></i>Save</button>
</div>
```

### Refused and saved

`error` is in the danger tone, its words saying how many fields the page refused; `saved` in the success tone fades back to the bar at rest after two seconds, and under reduced motion it stays until the next change.

```html
<div class="save-bar" data-state="error" role="region" aria-label="Changes not saved">
	<i class="bi bi-exclamation-triangle" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<span class="save-bar-text">2 fields refused: the address is taken, the price is below the child price</span>
	<button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" type="button"><i class="bi bi-floppy" aria-hidden="true"></i>Save</button>
</div>
<div class="save-bar" data-state="saved" role="region" aria-label="Changes">
	<i class="bi bi-check2-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<span class="save-bar-text">Saved at 14:05</span>
</div>
```

### The fields that changed

`data-changed` marks a field whose value differs from the saved one: a bar at the start of a `form-control` or a `form-select` - a combobox's face is one - or of a chips field's `chip-input` box, and a dot after a check or a switch. On a tab it is a dot too. A tracked form sets it; a page may set it by hand.

```html
<div class="form-floating">
	<input class="form-control" id="save-bar-changed-name" value="North Bay by speedboat" placeholder="Name" data-changed>
	<label for="save-bar-changed-name">Name</label>
</div>
<label class="form-check" data-changed><input class="check" type="checkbox" name="shown-on-the-site" checked> Shown on the site</label>
```

### A form in a dialog

A tracked form in a dialog keeps its own button, which takes `Control` `S` when it is the form's only one; the dialog waits while the page saves, and closing it with changes asks first.

```html
<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="save-bar-dialog-panel" command="show-modal"><i class="bi bi-pencil" aria-hidden="true"></i>Rename the boat</button>
<dialog class="dialog dialog-sm" id="save-bar-dialog-panel" aria-labelledby="save-bar-dialog-title">
	<form method="dialog" data-track="Boat" data-docs-track>
		<div class="dialog-header"><h2 class="dialog-title" id="save-bar-dialog-title">Boat B</h2></div>
		<div class="dialog-body vstack gap-12">
			<div class="form-field"><label class="form-label" for="save-bar-dialog-name">Name</label><input class="form-control" id="save-bar-dialog-name" name="boat" value="Blue Heron" autocomplete="off"></div>
		</div>
		<div class="dialog-footer">
			<button class="btn" type="button" commandfor="save-bar-dialog-panel" command="close">Cancel</button>
			<button class="btn btn-primary" value="save">Save</button>
		</div>
	</form>
</dialog>
```

## What a field is

- One field per name: a radio group, checkboxes of one name, a `select multiple` and a combobox's list each count once. A disabled field is compared too, by its value.
- The saved state is read one task after `DOMContentLoaded` - after the page's own scripts, so a field a script formats at load is already in it - and one task after a tracked form lands later. A value typed back to the saved one is no change; a field added or removed since is one.
- `data-track="off"` on a control or a fieldset leaves it out. Hidden fields are compared but never marked. A field's words in the bar are its `data-track-label`, else its label, its group's legend or its combobox's label.
- A value set by code: `REDZ.ui.track.refresh(form)` draws the change, `REDZ.ui.track.baseline(form)` takes what the form holds as saved - a dialog refilled for another record.

## Saving

Save, `Control` `S`, `Enter` in a field or `REDZ.ui.track.save()` fires the cancelable `redz:save` on each changed form in turn, and stops at the first refusal. The page answers with `event.detail.respondWith(promise)`; what the form held when it was sent becomes the saved state once the promise resolves, so what the person typed meanwhile stays changed. Nothing changed: the bar says so, and nothing is sent.

| In `redz:save` | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `changed` | The changed fields, `{name, label, was, now}`: a value is a string, a list for a kind that sends several, `null` for one that sends nothing. A secret's has `secret: true`, `was: null`, and `cleared: true` once cleared. |
| `data` | The whole form's `FormData` |
| `submitter` | The button that saved: the bar's Save or the form's own |
| `signal` | Aborted when a dialog that waits is closed by code |

- Resolved: every password field is emptied, then `redz:saved` `{form, value}` bubbles from the form with what the promise resolved to - the place to reload or go on.
- Refused with `{message, fields}`: each field `fields` names gets `aria-invalid="true"` and its sentence in an `invalid-feedback` under its control, above its hints, first in its `aria-describedby`; the bar says how many are left to fix, with the message; the first is brought into view - its tab selected, its fold opened - and focused. A field refused with `''` is marked without words; a sentence goes once the field is edited. An `AbortError` is silent.
- A field refused as `{text, stored}` - another person saved it meanwhile - shows the words in a warning under it with Keep mine, which takes `stored` as the saved state and keeps the person's value, and Take saved, which puts `stored` in the field.
- Left alone, a lone changed form is submitted as usual.

## Discarding and leaving

- Discard puts the saved values back, each with `input` and `change` so whatever a field drives follows, fires `redz:discard` on the form, and offers Undo until the next edit or ten seconds.
- While anything is changed, a link that leaves the page, a tab whose pane holds a changed form and a dialog's cancel or close ask first: Save and go - the focus starts there -, Discard, Stay. The browser's own question guards the rest, and only while something is changed.
- An `input type="password"` with `data-secret` keeps the stored value while it is empty. A button with `command="--clear"` for it and `data-clear` clears it: the field is disabled and emptied, `aria-pressed="true"`, and the form sends the name `data-clear` gives as `1`.

## For a page's probes

What a page's own checks may rely on, also in the passport as `contracts.track`.

| Part | Names |
| --- | --- |
| Selectors | `form[data-track]`, `[data-changed]`, `.save-bar[data-state]`, `.invalid-feedback[data-track-error]`, `.alert-warning[data-track-conflict]`, `[data-track-action]` |
| The bar's states | `clean`, `dirty`, `saving`, `saved`, `error` |
| Actions | `save`, `discard`, `undo`, `keep`, `take` |
| Attributes | `data-track`, `data-track-label`, `data-changed`, `data-secret`, `data-clear`, `data-state`, `data-track-action`, `data-track-error`, `data-track-conflict`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby` |
| Events | `redz:save`, `redz:saved`, `redz:discard` |
| `REDZ.ui.track` | `refresh`, `baseline`, `reset`, `dirty`, `changed`, `save` |

## Accessibility

- The bar is a region named by the page's text; its words name the changes, not only their count. They are not a live region: a screen reader hears only that the changes were saved, refused, discarded, or that there is nothing to do.
- Save and Discard are never disabled; pressed with nothing to do, they say so.
- It does not print, and it never hides the last field of the form: the form keeps room under it.
- A changed field's mark is drawn, not read out: the bar's words name the changes; a changed tab is described as not saved. In forced colors the mark is a thicker start border.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/save-bar.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/save-bar.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-bg-raised`, `--redz-shadow-2`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-warning`, `--redz-warning-subtle`, `--redz-danger`, `--redz-danger-subtle`, `--redz-success`, `--redz-success-subtle`.

# Status lines

A line beside a form's button that says what its save is doing: saving, saved, or why it was refused. It stays where the person looks; a message that comes and goes over the page is a [toast](toast.md).

## Examples

An element `form-status` beside the button, and `REDZ.ui.status(line, promise)` as the save starts. Past 400 ms the line says "Saving…" with a spinner; when the promise is kept it says "Saved" with a check and fades after three seconds; when it is refused it says the refusal's own message with a danger icon, and stays. The words come from the page's texts `status.saving` and `status.saved`.

```html
<div class="hstack flex-wrap gap-12">
	<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button" data-docs-run="status-save"><i class="bi bi-floppy" aria-hidden="true"></i>Save</button>
	<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="status-refuse">Save a taken name</button>
	<div class="form-status" id="status-save-line"></div>
</div>
```

```js
const line = document.getElementById('status-save-line');
REDZ.ui.status(line, fetch('/excursions/12', {method: 'PUT', body}).then((answer) => {
	if (!answer.ok) {
		throw new Error('The name is taken. Pick another.');
	}
}));
```

### Words of the page

`REDZ.ui.status(line, {tone, text})` says the page's own words at once with the tone's icon: `success` and `info` fade, `warning` and `danger` stay. A later call takes the line over from an earlier one, and `REDZ.ui.status(line, null)` empties the line, for a next step that must not show an old refusal.

```html
<div class="hstack flex-wrap gap-12">
	<button class="btn" type="button" data-docs-run="status-words">Publish</button>
	<div class="form-status" id="status-words-line"></div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- The line holds a polite status from the page's load, so a screen reader says each message once - "Saving…" only when the save takes longer than 400 ms.
- A refusal stays until the next save: its words say what to change, not only that something failed.
- The icon carries the tone; the words carry the meaning, in the page's text colors.

# Selection bar

The bar over a list that shows when rows are checked: how many, and what can be done with all of them at once.

## Examples

Plain buttons in the bar stand on the page's ground over its tint; a toned button keeps its own colors, and the one action the bar suggests is a `btn-primary`; clearing the selection is a quiet icon button at the end. Inside a `data-select` the library hides the bar at zero and writes its count into a `data-select-count` - see [checked rows](table.md#table-selection).

```html
<div class="selection-bar" role="region" aria-label="Selected excursions">
	<strong>2 selected</strong>
	<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button"><i class="bi bi-send" aria-hidden="true"></i>Publish</button>
	<button class="btn btn-sm" type="button"><i class="bi bi-eye-slash" aria-hidden="true"></i>Withdraw</button>
	<button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" type="button"><i class="bi bi-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i>Translate what changed</button>
	<button class="btn btn-sm ms-auto" type="button"><i class="bi bi-trash3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Delete…</button>
	<button class="btn btn-sm btn-icon btn-text" type="button" aria-label="Clear the selection"><i class="bi bi-x" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- The bar is a region named after the list; its count says what is selected.
- An action that removes asks first - its words end in “…” and it opens a [confirmation](dialog.md).

## Tokens

From [`css/components/selection-bar.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/selection-bar.css). It declares `--redz-btn-bg` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-primary-subtle`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-control-height-sm`.

# Navs and tabs

A row of links between views of one thing - `nav-underline` - or of choices - `nav-pills`; and the same row as tabs that switch panels on the page, driven by the keyboard as the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern.

## Examples

Links between pages are a `<nav>`; the current one is `aria-current="page"`.

```html
<nav class="nav nav-underline" aria-label="List views">
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-links" aria-current="page">All<span class="badge">28</span></a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-links">Needs attention<span class="badge badge-subtle-warning">3</span></a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-links">Drafts</a>
</nav>
<nav class="nav nav-pills" aria-label="Period">
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-links" aria-current="page">Week</a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-links">Month</a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-links">Year</a>
</nav>
```

### Tabs

Tabs switch panels in place: `role="tablist"`, each tab `role="tab"` with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, each panel `role="tabpanel"`. The library keeps only the selected tab in the tab order and only its panel shown. The arrow keys select as they move.

```html
<div class="nav nav-underline" role="tablist" aria-label="Excursion">
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-tabs-1" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="nav-tabs-panel-1">Details</button>
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-tabs-2" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-tabs-panel-2">Prices</button>
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-tabs-3" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-tabs-panel-3">History</button>
</div>
<div id="nav-tabs-panel-1" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-tabs-1" tabindex="0"><p>A day at sea: snorkelling at two reefs, lunch on the boat.</p></div>
<div id="nav-tabs-panel-2" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-tabs-2" tabindex="0" hidden><p>Adults 2,500 · children 1,900 · under four free.</p></div>
<div id="nav-tabs-panel-3" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-tabs-3" tabindex="0" hidden><p>Edited yesterday by M. K.; published on three sites.</p></div>
```

### A tab with changes

`data-changed`, set by the page, puts a dot on a tab whose panel holds something not saved yet, the same word as on a field. Its `aria-label` says so to a screen reader.

```html
<div class="nav nav-underline" role="tablist" aria-label="Settings">
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-changed-1" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="nav-changed-panel-1">Company</button>
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-changed-2" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-changed-panel-2" aria-label="Mail, not saved" data-changed>Mail</button>
</div>
<div id="nav-changed-panel-1" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-changed-1" tabindex="0"><p>The company's name and address.</p></div>
<div id="nav-changed-panel-2" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-changed-2" tabindex="0" hidden><p>The address mail is sent from.</p></div>
```

### Tabs whose panels load

When a panel comes from the server, the arrows should not load every panel they pass: `data-activation="manual"` on the tablist makes them move the focus only, and `Enter` or `Space` selects.

```html
<div class="nav nav-pills" role="tablist" aria-label="Report" data-activation="manual">
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-manual-1" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="nav-manual-panel-1">Bookings</button>
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-manual-2" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-manual-panel-2">Revenue</button>
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-manual-3" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-manual-panel-3">Refunds</button>
</div>
<div id="nav-manual-panel-1" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-manual-1" tabindex="0"><p>128 bookings this week.</p></div>
<div id="nav-manual-panel-2" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-manual-2" tabindex="0" hidden><p>312,400 THB this week.</p></div>
<div id="nav-manual-panel-3" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-manual-3" tabindex="0" hidden><p>2 refunds this week.</p></div>
```

### A tab that asks before it is left

Before a person's click or key selects a tab, the tablist fires the cancelable `redz:select`; its `detail` holds `tab`, the one asked for, and `from`, the one being left. A page that must ask first - a form with unsaved edits - calls `event.preventDefault()` and `event.detail.respondWith(promise)`: the tab is selected when the promise gives `true`, and otherwise the one being left stays, with the focus. Change the note below, then choose another tab.

```html
<div class="nav nav-underline" role="tablist" aria-label="Excursion">
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-guard-1" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="nav-guard-panel-1">Note</button>
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-guard-2" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-guard-panel-2">Prices</button>
</div>
<div id="nav-guard-panel-1" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-guard-1" tabindex="0">
	<label class="form-label" for="nav-guard-note">A note for the guides</label>
	<input class="form-control" id="nav-guard-note" type="text" value="Meet at the pier at 8:00">
</div>
<div id="nav-guard-panel-2" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-guard-2" tabindex="0" hidden><p>2,900 THB an adult.</p></div>
```

```js
tablist.addEventListener('redz:select', (event) => {
  if (form.dataset.changed !== undefined) {
    event.preventDefault();
    event.detail.respondWith(REDZ.ui.confirm({title: 'Leave without saving?', ok: 'Leave'}));
  }
});
```

### Tabs in the address

A tablist with `data-hash` follows the address: `location.hash` naming a panel, or anything inside one, selects its tab - when the page loads, and when the hash changes as a person's choice through `redz:select`, whose refusal puts the address back; a tablist inside a panel too -, and a person's choice writes the panel's id into the address, so a link or a reload opens the same tab. After every selection, the first one too, the tablist fires `redz:selected` with `detail.tab`. `REDZ.ui.select(tab)` chooses a tab from code as a person would - through `redz:select`, so the page can still refuse - and answers a promise of whether it was selected.

A tab with `data-hash-within="PREFIX"` stands for a panel whose contents come later, such as a `data-lazy` one: an address that begins with PREFIX and names nothing on the page yet selects that tab, the address staying, and the tablist the panel brings takes its own tab from the same address. A tablist put in later is taken up as it comes, as at load: one selection and one `redz:selected`, the address left as it is, no scroll. A tab added to a tablist leaves the tab order unless it is the selected one.

```html
<div class="nav nav-underline" role="tablist" aria-label="Booking" data-hash>
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-hash-1" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="nav-hash-guests">Guests</button>
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-hash-2" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-hash-payment">Payment</button>
	<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-hash-3" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-hash-history">History</button>
</div>
<div id="nav-hash-guests" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-hash-1" tabindex="0"><p>Two adults, one child.</p></div>
<div id="nav-hash-payment" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-hash-2" tabindex="0" hidden><p>Paid in full by card on 2 November.</p></div>
<div id="nav-hash-history" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-hash-3" tabindex="0" hidden><p>Booked on 1 November; the date moved once.</p></div>
<p><a href="#nav-hash-payment">The payment</a> opens its tab.</p>
```

```js
tablist.addEventListener('redz:selected', (event) => load(event.detail.tab));
await REDZ.ui.select(document.getElementById('nav-hash-3'));
```

### Filling the width

`nav-fill` lets the links share the width by their length, `nav-justified` in equal parts.

```html
<nav class="nav nav-underline nav-fill" aria-label="Filled">
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-fill" aria-current="page">Overview</a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-fill">Prices and seasons</a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-fill">Reviews</a>
</nav>
<nav class="nav nav-underline nav-justified" aria-label="Justified">
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-fill" aria-current="page">Overview</a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-fill">Prices and seasons</a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-fill">Reviews</a>
</nav>
```

### Where you are on the page

A nav or a list group with `data-scrollspy` marks the link to the section in view `aria-current="location"` as the page - or the box the sections scroll in - scrolls: the last section whose top has passed a quarter of the height, or the last one at the end.

```html
<div class="grid md:cols-12 gap-16">
	<nav class="list-group list-group-flush md:span-4" aria-label="On this example" data-scrollspy>
		<a class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" href="#nav-spy-plan">Plan</a>
		<a class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" href="#nav-spy-boat">The boat</a>
		<a class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" href="#nav-spy-lunch">Lunch</a>
		<a class="list-group-item list-group-item-action" href="#nav-spy-back">Back</a>
	</nav>
	<div class="docs-scroll md:span-8 vstack gap-16" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="The day, by section">
		<section id="nav-spy-plan" class="vstack gap-4"><h4 class="fs-14">Plan</h4><p class="mb-0">Pick-up at the hotel at 7:30, the pier at 8:15. The crew hands out life vests and snorkels before the boat leaves the bay.</p></section>
		<section id="nav-spy-boat" class="vstack gap-4"><h4 class="fs-14">The boat</h4><p class="mb-0">A speedboat for 30 guests with shade and a toilet; the ride to the park takes an hour across open water.</p></section>
		<section id="nav-spy-lunch" class="vstack gap-4"><h4 class="fs-14">Lunch</h4><p class="mb-0">Lunch on a beach of the park: rice, green curry, fruit and water; vegetarian on request.</p></section>
		<section id="nav-spy-back" class="vstack gap-4"><h4 class="fs-14">Back</h4><p class="mb-0">The boat leaves the park at 15:30 and reaches the pier by 17:00; the transfer brings everyone back to the hotel.</p></section>
	</div>
</div>
```

### A row that scrolls

A nav or a tab list wider than its box scrolls sideways, and the edge it goes on past fades - `data-more` says which, `start`, `end` or both, as the person scrolls; when the page loads, the current or selected item is scrolled into the row's view, the page itself left where it is.

```html
<nav class="nav nav-underline max-w-320" aria-label="Task views">
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-scrolling">All <span class="badge">48</span></a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-scrolling">New <span class="badge">6</span></a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-scrolling">Doing <span class="badge">9</span></a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-scrolling">Checking <span class="badge">4</span></a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-scrolling" aria-current="page">Done <span class="badge">25</span></a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-scrolling">Returned <span class="badge">3</span></a>
	<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-scrolling">Cancelled <span class="badge">1</span></a>
</nav>
```

### When the links do not fit

`nav-overflow` around a nav keeps it on one line: the links that do not fit hide from the end and come back, in their order, as the items of a menu behind a “More” button after the nav. The link the person is on and a link with `nav-overflow-keep` stay in the row. A link that opens a [menu](menu.md) folds with it, as a group of its items under the link's words, and stays in the row while its menu holds the page the person is on; a [navbar](navbar.md) shows one. A link the page hides with `hidden` leaves the row and the menu, and comes back when the page shows it. A danger or warning badge on a hidden link shows on the button, so a problem in the menu is seen with the menu closed: a badge of the worst tone with the sum of their numbers, or a dot of that tone when one of them is not a plain number. The button's name says which links they are, in the links' own words; other badges stay in the menu. It measures the room its own box has, not the window, so a nav in a narrow column folds as early as it needs to. For a row of links the wrapper is the `<nav>`, so the menu stays inside the landmark.

```html
<nav class="nav-overflow max-w-480" aria-label="Excursion sections">
	<div class="nav nav-underline">
		<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-overflow" aria-current="page">Overview</a>
		<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-overflow">Program</a>
		<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-overflow">Prices</a>
		<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-overflow">Dates</a>
		<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-overflow">Pickup</a>
		<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-overflow">Reviews<span class="badge">42</span></a>
		<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-overflow">Photos<span class="badge badge-subtle-warning">3</span></a>
		<a class="nav-link" href="#nav-overflow">Questions<span class="badge badge-subtle-danger">1</span></a>
	</div>
</nav>
```

Tabs fold the same way. The arrows move between the tabs in the row; a tab chosen in the menu comes back into the row selected, with the focus, and the last one in the row takes its place in the menu.

```html
<div class="nav-overflow max-w-320">
	<div class="nav nav-pills" role="tablist" aria-label="Guest">
		<button class="nav-link nav-overflow-keep" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-overflow-tabs-1" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="nav-overflow-tabs-panel-1">Profile</button>
		<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-overflow-tabs-2" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-overflow-tabs-panel-2">Bookings</button>
		<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-overflow-tabs-3" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-overflow-tabs-panel-3">Payments</button>
		<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-overflow-tabs-4" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-overflow-tabs-panel-4">Messages</button>
		<button class="nav-link" type="button" role="tab" id="nav-overflow-tabs-5" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="nav-overflow-tabs-panel-5">Notes</button>
	</div>
</div>
<div id="nav-overflow-tabs-panel-1" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-overflow-tabs-1" tabindex="0"><p>Anna Sample, two trips this year.</p></div>
<div id="nav-overflow-tabs-panel-2" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-overflow-tabs-2" tabindex="0" hidden><p>North Bay on 12 December, 2 adults.</p></div>
<div id="nav-overflow-tabs-panel-3" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-overflow-tabs-3" tabindex="0" hidden><p>Paid in full by card.</p></div>
<div id="nav-overflow-tabs-panel-4" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-overflow-tabs-4" tabindex="0" hidden><p>No messages yet.</p></div>
<div id="nav-overflow-tabs-panel-5" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="nav-overflow-tabs-5" tabindex="0" hidden><p>Vegetarian lunch.</p></div>
```

## States

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | In a tablist |
| --- | --- |
| `→` / `←` | The next / the previous tab, round the ends - mirrored right to left; `↓` / `↑` in a list with `aria-orientation="vertical"` |
| `Home` / `End` | The first / the last tab |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Selects the focused tab - what the arrows do not, with `data-activation="manual"` |
| `Tab` | From the selected tab into its panel, or first to the “More” button when the row has one |

- Links that change the page are a `<nav>` of links, never tabs: tabs only switch what is already on the page.
- A link folded into the “More” menu is hidden in the row, so a screen reader and `Tab` meet it once, in the menu. The button says the page's text `more`, reports whether its menu is open, and opens it by the menu's keys; a plain click on an item clicks the hidden link itself, so the page's own handlers run.
- A mark beside a tab's words - a dot, a count - has its own name, so the tab reads as “EN, 1 field outdated”.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/nav.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/nav.css). It declares `--redz-fade-left`, `--redz-fade-right` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-warning`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-radius-8`, `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-radius-6`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-shadow-1`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nav-item` | - | remove | links sit straight in the nav |
| `nav-tabs` | `nav-underline` | rename | tabs are drawn as an underline |
| `tab-content` | - | remove | panels are siblings with role="tabpanel", hidden when not selected |
| `tab-pane` | - | remove | panels are siblings with role="tabpanel", hidden when not selected |
| `data-bs-toggle="tab"` | `role="tab" aria-controls="ID"` | trigger | in a role="tablist"; the library selects and shows the panel |
| `data-bs-toggle="pill"` | `role="tab" aria-controls="ID"` | trigger | in a role="tablist" |
| `data-bs-spy` | `data-scrollspy` | trigger | on the nav or list group of the links, not on the scrolled box; the link to the section in view gets aria-current="location" |
| `bootstrap.Tab` | `tab.click()` | review | the library selects on click and by the keys |
| `shown.bs.tab` | - | review | watch aria-selected, or the tab's click |

# Navbars

A site's header: its name, its main links and what stands beside them. Where the header is too narrow for the links, a button opens them as a panel at the side of the screen.

## Examples

`navbar` on the `<header>`, `navbar-brand` on the site's name, `navbar-toggler` on the button, and the links in a `<nav class="drawer" popover>` after it: `drawer-header` with the panel's title and its close button, `drawer-body` with a `nav navbar-nav`. `md:navbar-expand` sets the links in the row where the header is 768 px wide or wider; below that the button opens them. The width is the header's own, so a header in a column folds as one on a phone does.

```html
<header class="navbar md:navbar-expand">
	<a class="navbar-brand" href="#navbar-site"><i class="bi bi-sun" aria-hidden="true"></i>Example Tours</a>
	<button class="btn btn-text btn-icon navbar-toggler" type="button" commandfor="navbar-site-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-label="Menu"><i class="bi bi-list" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	<nav class="drawer" id="navbar-site-menu" popover aria-labelledby="navbar-site-title">
		<div class="drawer-header">
			<h2 class="drawer-title" id="navbar-site-title">Menu</h2>
			<button class="btn-close" type="button" commandfor="navbar-site-menu" command="hide-popover" aria-label="Close"></button>
		</div>
		<div class="drawer-body">
			<div class="nav navbar-nav">
				<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-site" aria-current="page">Excursions</a>
				<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-site">Transfers</a>
				<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-site">Villas</a>
				<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-site">Reviews</a>
			</div>
			<a class="btn btn-primary" href="#navbar-site">Book a tour</a>
		</div>
	</nav>
</header>
```

### More links than room

With [`nav-overflow`](nav.md) around the links, a header that is wide enough for its row but not for all of them keeps the first ones and moves the rest into a “More” menu; only below its width does the whole row go behind the button. A link that opens a [menu](menu.md) folds with it: “More” shows that menu's items as a group under the link's words. This header is 640 px wide at most and sets its row from 576 px with `sm:navbar-expand`.

```html
<header class="navbar sm:navbar-expand max-w-640">
	<a class="navbar-brand" href="#navbar-overflow"><i class="bi bi-sun" aria-hidden="true"></i>Example Tours</a>
	<button class="btn btn-text btn-icon navbar-toggler" type="button" commandfor="navbar-overflow-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-label="Menu"><i class="bi bi-list" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	<nav class="drawer" id="navbar-overflow-menu" popover aria-labelledby="navbar-overflow-title">
		<div class="drawer-header">
			<h2 class="drawer-title" id="navbar-overflow-title">Menu</h2>
			<button class="btn-close" type="button" commandfor="navbar-overflow-menu" command="hide-popover" aria-label="Close"></button>
		</div>
		<div class="drawer-body">
			<div class="nav-overflow">
				<div class="nav navbar-nav">
					<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-overflow">Excursions</a>
					<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-overflow">Transfers</a>
					<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-overflow" aria-current="page">Villas</a>
					<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-overflow">Yachts</a>
					<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-overflow">Reviews</a>
					<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-overflow">Blog</a>
					<button class="nav-link" type="button" commandfor="navbar-overflow-help" command="toggle-popover" aria-haspopup="menu">Help<i class="bi bi-chevron-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
					<div class="menu" id="navbar-overflow-help" popover role="menu" aria-label="Help">
						<a class="menu-item" role="menuitem" href="#navbar-overflow">Questions and answers</a>
						<a class="menu-item" role="menuitem" href="#navbar-overflow">Contacts</a>
						<a class="menu-item" role="menuitem" href="#navbar-overflow">Cancellation policy</a>
					</div>
				</div>
			</div>
			<a class="btn btn-primary" href="#navbar-overflow">Book</a>
		</div>
	</nav>
</header>
```

### Always behind the button

Without a `navbar-expand` class the links always wait behind the button, for a header that keeps its row for something else. `navbar-text` is a line of text in the row. `data-theme="dark"` on the header turns it and its panel dark on a light page, and `drawer-start` opens the panel at the start edge.

```html
<header class="navbar bg-body" data-theme="dark">
	<a class="navbar-brand" href="#navbar-folded"><i class="bi bi-sun" aria-hidden="true"></i>Example Tours</a>
	<span class="navbar-text ms-auto">Open daily, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.</span>
	<button class="btn btn-text btn-icon navbar-toggler" type="button" commandfor="navbar-folded-menu" command="toggle-popover" aria-label="Menu"><i class="bi bi-list" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	<nav class="drawer drawer-start" id="navbar-folded-menu" popover aria-labelledby="navbar-folded-title">
		<div class="drawer-header">
			<h2 class="drawer-title" id="navbar-folded-title">Menu</h2>
			<button class="btn-close" type="button" commandfor="navbar-folded-menu" command="hide-popover" aria-label="Close"></button>
		</div>
		<div class="drawer-body">
			<div class="nav navbar-nav">
				<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-folded" aria-current="page">Excursions</a>
				<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-folded">Transfers</a>
				<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-folded">Villas</a>
				<a class="nav-link" href="#navbar-folded">Contacts</a>
			</div>
		</div>
	</nav>
</header>
```

## Where the row starts

The class says from which width of the header its links stand in the row; below it the button opens them.

| Class | The links in the row |
| --- | --- |
| `navbar-expand` | Always |
| `sm:navbar-expand` | From 576 px |
| `md:navbar-expand` | From 768 px |
| `lg:navbar-expand` | From 1024 px |
| `xl:navbar-expand` | From 1280 px |
| `2xl:navbar-expand` | From 1536 px |
| None | Never: the button opens them |

### At the top while the page scrolls

A header that stays at the top takes `position-sticky top-0` and a background: `bg-body`, or `navbar-translucent`, which lets the page show through it, blurred.

```html
<header class="navbar navbar-translucent md:navbar-expand position-sticky top-0 z-3">…</header>
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The header is a `<header>` and the links a `<nav>` named by the panel's title, so a screen reader finds the same navigation in the row and in the panel.
- The button says whether the panel is open. `Tab` from it goes into the panel; `Esc` or a click outside closes it and brings the focus back to the button. The panel also closes when a link in it is followed, when the focus leaves it for the page, and when the header grows wide enough for its row. The page under it does not scroll while it is open.
- The link the person is on is `aria-current="page"`, underlined so it shows without color, in forced colors too.
- A link that opens a menu is a `<button>` with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, and its [menu](menu.md) keeps its keys in the row and in the panel.
- `js/navbar.js` closes the panel; the button, the panel and the row are the browser's commands and CSS.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/navbar.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/navbar.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-fs-18`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-bg`.

## From Bootstrap 5.3

| Bootstrap 5.3 | REDZ.UI | Change | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `navbar-collapse` | `drawer` | review | a <nav class="drawer" popover id="ID"> after the toggler: drawer-header with its title, the links in drawer-body |
| `navbar-dark` | - | review | data-theme="dark" on the navbar, with a background such as bg-body |
| `navbar-nav-scroll` | - | remove | the panel scrolls by itself |
| `navbar-toggler-icon` | `bi bi-list` | rename | an icon in the toggler |

# Breadcrumbs

The way up from a record to the list it belongs to, above the record's title. The separators are drawn by CSS and turn with the direction.

## Examples

```html
<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
	<ol class="breadcrumb">
		<li class="breadcrumb-item"><a href="#breadcrumb-trail">Content</a></li>
		<li class="breadcrumb-item"><a href="#breadcrumb-trail">Excursions</a></li>
		<li class="breadcrumb-item" aria-current="page">North Bay</li>
	</ol>
</nav>
```

## Accessibility

- A `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` around an ordered list; the last item is the page itself, `aria-current="page"`, not a link.
- The separators are not read: they are drawn, not written.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/breadcrumb.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/breadcrumb.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-text-faint`.

# Pagination

Links to the pages of a long list, with Bootstrap's names: the current page says so in `aria-current="page"`, a page there is none of says so in `aria-disabled`. A list that pages by "the next 50" shows only previous, next and where you are.

## Examples

A `nav` named for what it pages holds the list; each page is a link. A page there is none of - the previous one of the first page - is a link without `href` and `aria-disabled="true"`, out of the Tab order. Skip no page silently: an ellipsis stands for the pages between. Show no pagination for a single page.

```html
<nav aria-label="Pages of excursions">
	<ul class="pagination">
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-numbers"><i class="bi bi-chevron-left flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i><span class="visually-hidden">Previous page</span></a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-numbers">1</a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-numbers" aria-current="page">2</a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-numbers">3</a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><span class="page-text" aria-hidden="true">…</span></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-numbers">12</a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-numbers"><span class="visually-hidden">Next page</span><i class="bi bi-chevron-right flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i></a></li>
	</ul>
</nav>
```

### Previous and next

A list that reads its rows page by page from where the last one ended - the fast way for a large table - knows no page numbers: it shows the rows on view and the way back and on. `page-text` holds words between the links.

```html
<nav aria-label="Pages of bookings">
	<ul class="pagination">
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-keyset"><i class="bi bi-chevron-left flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i>Previous</a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><span class="page-text">51-100 of 1 234</span></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-keyset">Next<i class="bi bi-chevron-right flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i></a></li>
	</ul>
</nav>
```

### Sizes

`pagination-sm` and `pagination-lg` on the list.

```html
<nav aria-label="Small pages">
	<ul class="pagination pagination-sm">
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" aria-disabled="true"><i class="bi bi-chevron-left flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i><span class="visually-hidden">Previous page</span></a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-sizes" aria-current="page">1</a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-sizes">2</a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-sizes"><span class="visually-hidden">Next page</span><i class="bi bi-chevron-right flip-rtl" aria-hidden="true"></i></a></li>
	</ul>
</nav>
<nav aria-label="Large pages">
	<ul class="pagination pagination-lg">
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-sizes">1</a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-sizes" aria-current="page">2</a></li>
		<li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#pagination-sizes">3</a></li>
	</ul>
</nav>
```

## States

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The `nav` has a name - "Pages of excursions" - so a screen reader lists it among the landmarks; the current page is `aria-current="page"`, read as "current page".
- An arrow-only link carries its words in `visually-hidden` text; the chevrons turn round right to left by `flip-rtl`.
- A page there is none of has no `href`, so Tab passes it, and `aria-disabled="true"` greys it.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/pagination.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/pagination.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-control-height`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-8`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-primary-contrast`, `--redz-text-faint`, `--redz-control-height-sm`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-control-height-lg`, `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-fs-16`.

# Steppers

The steps of a task that takes more than one screen: a booking, an import, the first run of a site. A list of steps in order, the one the person is on marked by the attribute a screen reader says, the ones before it done by their place.

## Examples

`stepper` on an `<ol>`, `stepper-item` on each step, and `aria-current="step"` on the step the person is on. Every step before it reads as done, every step after it as still to come; the numbers are counted by the list.

```html
<ol class="stepper" aria-label="Booking">
	<li class="stepper-item">Choose a tour</li>
	<li class="stepper-item" aria-current="step">Pick a date</li>
	<li class="stepper-item">Guests</li>
	<li class="stepper-item">Payment</li>
</ol>
```

### Across

`stepper-horizontal` sets the steps in a row, each under its number. With a prefix, `md:stepper-horizontal`, the row starts where the region is wide enough, and the steps stay a column below it.

```html
<ol class="stepper md:stepper-horizontal" aria-label="Import">
	<li class="stepper-item">Upload the file</li>
	<li class="stepper-item">Match the columns</li>
	<li class="stepper-item" aria-current="step">Check the rows</li>
	<li class="stepper-item">Import</li>
</ol>
```

### Steps to go back to

A step done may lead back to its screen: its words are a link inside the `stepper-item`. A step still to come is plain text, as it cannot be reached yet.

```html
<ol class="stepper stepper-horizontal" aria-label="New site">
	<li class="stepper-item"><a href="#stepper-links">Name</a></li>
	<li class="stepper-item"><a href="#stepper-links">Languages</a></li>
	<li class="stepper-item" aria-current="step">Theme</li>
	<li class="stepper-item">Publish</li>
</ol>
```

## States

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The list is an `<ol>` with a name of its own (`aria-label`): a screen reader says how many steps there are and which one this is.
- The step the person is on is `aria-current="step"`, never a class: VoiceOver and NVDA say "current step", and the look follows the attribute.
- The stepper shows where the person is; it moves nothing by itself. The screen's own buttons, "Back" and "Next", move between steps.
- A step done that leads back is a link, reached by `Tab`; a step still to come is text, never a disabled link.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/stepper.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/stepper.css). It declares `--redz-stepper-size`, `--redz-stepper-gap` on its root, never on rows or items.

It reads the theme's `--redz-space-12`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-border-strong`, `--redz-bg`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-border`, `--redz-primary`, `--redz-primary-contrast`, `--redz-text`.

# Command palette

One search for every place and action of an app, opened from anywhere by `⌘K` or `Ctrl K`: a dialog with the combobox's search and a list of links and buttons - Enter opens a page by its plain link or runs a button's command.

## Example

The button opens the dialog by the browser's command and names its keys in `aria-keyshortcuts`, which the library also takes as the shortcut. The options are links and buttons with `role="option"`, in groups; the search finds them by their words and by `data-keywords`.

```html
<button class="btn btn-subtle-secondary" type="button" commandfor="palette-demo-dialog" command="show-modal" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K"><i class="bi bi-search" aria-hidden="true"></i>Find or go to…<kbd>⌘K</kbd></button>
<dialog class="palette" id="palette-demo-dialog" closedby="any" aria-label="Find or go to">
	<input class="palette-search" type="search" id="palette-demo-search" role="combobox" aria-controls="palette-demo-list" aria-expanded="true" aria-autocomplete="list" aria-label="Find or go to" placeholder="Find or go to…" autocomplete="off" autofocus>
	<div class="palette-list" id="palette-demo-list" role="listbox" aria-label="Places and actions">
		<div role="group" aria-labelledby="palette-demo-go">
			<div class="menu-header" id="palette-demo-go" role="presentation">Go to</div>
			<a class="menu-item" role="option" id="palette-demo-pages" href="#palette-examples"><i class="bi bi-file-text" aria-hidden="true"></i>Pages</a>
			<a class="menu-item" role="option" id="palette-demo-excursions" href="#palette-examples"><i class="bi bi-compass" aria-hidden="true"></i>Excursions</a>
			<a class="menu-item" role="option" id="palette-demo-media" href="#palette-examples" data-keywords="images photos files"><i class="bi bi-images" aria-hidden="true"></i>Media library</a>
			<a class="menu-item" role="option" id="palette-demo-languages" href="#palette-examples" data-keywords="translations strings"><i class="bi bi-translate" aria-hidden="true"></i>Languages</a>
			<a class="menu-item" role="option" id="palette-demo-settings" href="#palette-examples" data-keywords="preferences options"><i class="bi bi-gear" aria-hidden="true"></i>Settings</a>
		</div>
		<div role="group" aria-labelledby="palette-demo-do">
			<div class="menu-header" id="palette-demo-do" role="presentation">Actions</div>
			<button class="menu-item" role="option" id="palette-demo-new" type="button" data-docs-run="toast-success"><i class="bi bi-plus-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i>New page</button>
			<button class="menu-item" role="option" id="palette-demo-cache" type="button" aria-disabled="true"><i class="bi bi-arrow-clockwise" aria-hidden="true"></i>Rebuild every page</button>
		</div>
	</div>
	<p class="combobox-no-results" hidden>Nothing found</p>
	<div class="palette-footer"><span><kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> to move</span><span><kbd>↵</kbd> to open</span><span><kbd>esc</kbd> to close</span></div>
</dialog>
```

## Shortcuts

A button or a link whose `aria-keyshortcuts` names a combination with `Control`, `Meta` or `Alt` is pressed by it: the page states the keys once, for screen readers and for the library. Where both `Meta+K` and `Control+K` are named, Apple's systems answer `⌘K` and the others `Ctrl K`, so `Control K` keeps its meaning in a Mac's text fields; Firefox's own `Ctrl K` gives way to the page's.

- A single key is never a shortcut here: WCAG 2.1.4 asks for a way to turn such keys off, and a combination needs none.
- A disabled, hidden or inert button is left alone, and so is one outside an open modal dialog. Its combination is still the page's and never reaches the browser, so a save button that is busy or has nothing to save keeps `Ctrl S` from the browser's own save. The first that can be pressed now is pressed.
- A combination held down presses once; its repeats are kept from the browser.
- The hint the button shows - `⌘K` or `Ctrl K` - is the page's to write.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | In the palette |
| --- | --- |
| `⌘K`, `Ctrl K` | Opens it from anywhere, the focus in its search |
| `↓` / `↑` | The next / the previous option, round the ends |
| `Page Down` / `Page Up` | Ten options on / back |
| `Enter` | Opens the active link or presses the active button; the palette closes |
| `Esc` | Empties the search; on an empty search, closes the palette, the focus back where it was |

- The palette is a modal `<dialog>` with a name; a click on its backdrop closes it (`closedby="any"`). Opening it empties its search.
- Its search is the WAI-ARIA combobox with a listbox, as in [Combobox](combobox.md): the options are plain links and buttons with `role="option"`, so a link opens in a new tab with `⌘` or the middle button as any link does. The library keeps them out of the Tab order (`tabindex="-1"`): the arrow keys reach them, as in every listbox.
- Where the options come from - the app's menu, recent pages, a search on the server - is the page's: a server search answers `redz:search` as a combobox's does.

## Tokens

From [`css/components/palette.css`](https://github.com/redz-tech/REDZ.UI/blob/main/css/components/palette.css), which declares no custom property of its own.

It reads the theme's `--redz-border`, `--redz-radius-12`, `--redz-bg-raised`, `--redz-shadow-3`, `--redz-text`, `--redz-space-16`, `--redz-fs-16`, `--redz-text-muted`, `--redz-focus`, `--redz-space-4`, `--redz-space-8`, `--redz-bg-hover`, `--redz-fs-12`, `--redz-ease`.

# App shell

The frame of an admin screen: `app` with a header, a side navigation, the main column and an optional side column. Below 1024 px the side navigation becomes a panel opened from the header. These docs stand in it. A site's header is a [navbar](navbar.md).

## The parts

The shell is the one part of the library that looks at the window; everything inside it measures its own region. `app-main` and `app-aside` are regions, so `md:` inside the main column measures the column.

```html
<div class="app">
  <header class="app-header">
    <button class="btn btn-text btn-icon app-burger" type="button" commandfor="side" command="toggle-popover" aria-label="Sections">…</button>
    <a class="app-brand" href="/"><span class="app-mark">RZ</span>REDZ CMS</a>
    <button class="btn app-search" type="button" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K">…</button>
  </header>
  <nav id="side" class="app-sidebar" popover aria-label="Sections">
    <a class="app-link" href="/">…Overview</a>
    <div class="app-section">Content</div>
    <a class="app-link" href="/excursions/" aria-current="page">…Excursions</a>
    <details class="app-group" id="side-sales">
      <summary class="app-section">Sales</summary>
      <a class="app-link" href="/bookings/">…Bookings</a>
    </details>
  </nav>
  <main class="app-main" id="main">…</main>
  <aside class="app-aside">…</aside>
</div>
```

The [demo screens](https://redz-tech.github.io/REDZ.UI/reference/demo/list.html) show the whole shell: a list, a resource page with its side column, a settings form.

### Folded to a rail

On a wide window the side navigation folds into a rail of its icons and back: a header button with `command="--fold"` and `aria-controls` naming the sidebar puts `data-folded` on it and says so in `aria-pressed`. Folded, each link shows its words as a tooltip and keeps them as its name. The library stores nothing: it tells the page in `redz:fold` (`detail.folded`), and the page that keeps the choice writes `data-folded` back on the sidebar when it loads. These docs fold so - the button beside their burger.

```html
<button class="btn btn-text btn-icon" type="button" command="--fold" aria-controls="side" aria-label="Fold the sections">…</button>

document.addEventListener('redz:fold', (event) => localStorage.setItem('folded', event.detail.folded ? '1' : ''));
```

A shell without `app-sidebar` - a page whose role has no sections - is one column by itself: no class to add.

### Groups that open and close

A section of the side navigation may open and close: `<details class="app-group">` with its `<summary class="app-section">`, the chevron drawn by the library. The server prints each group open or closed as the person left it, so the navigation stands right before any script and without one. The group that holds the current page - its `aria-current="page"` link - opens as the page loads, even after the person closed it.
